title: Total Endovascular Aortic Arch Repair: A Review of Current Technologies and Clinical Decision Frameworks.
abstract: Endovascular technologies offer less invasive alternatives to open aortic arch repair in high-risk patients. This review evaluates contemporary total arch reconstruction platforms. PubMed literature through February 2026, manufacturer documentation, and ClinicalTrials.gov were reviewed. Branched, fenestrated, and alternative devices were assessed regarding anatomy, procedural characteristics, and clinical outcomes. No formal systematic review or meta-analysis was performed. Technical success rates reached 90-100%. Branched devices enable three-vessel revascularization, while fenestrated systems accommodate complex anatomy. Stroke rates ranged from 3.7% to 11%; endoleaks and reinterventions remained concerns. To date, anyway, device selection, anatomical suitability, planning, and institutional expertise are essential for optimal outcomes.

PubMed literature through February 2026, manufacturer documentation, and ClinicalTrials.gov were reviewed.

title: Epidemiology of 376,383 arteriovenous fistula creations for hemodialysis over 9 years within the Brazilian Unified Public Health System and the Private Healthcare Sector.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors.

METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001.

RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates.

CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

title: Individualised Versus Conventional Balloon Dilation for TIPS: Hepatic Encephalopathy in a Propensity-Matched Before-After Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 717 patients with cirrhosis underwent TIPS with 8-mm covered stents between December 2015 and December 2023. Patients received conventional 8-mm full dilation (n = 408; before December 1, 2020) or individualised dilation (n = 309; from December 1, 2020 onward), with the balloon diameter (5-7 mm) chosen by an 11-factor scoring system. The primary endpoint was overt HE (West Haven grade II-IV) within 6 months. Propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, Fine-Grey and E-value analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Six-month overt HE was lower in the individualised group (14.6%; 45 of 309) than in the conventional group (27.5%; 112 of 408), yielding an absolute risk reduction of 12.9 percentage points (number needed to treat, 8; p < 0.001). After propensity score matching on 18 covariates (259 pairs), the conditional odds ratio was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.27-0.66; p < 0.001), consistent with inverse probability weighting (odds ratio, 0.47). Six-month re-bleeding (1.5% vs. 1.3%), stent dysfunction (3.9% vs. 4.2%) and ascites improvement (61.0% vs. 62.1%) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: An individualised balloon dilation strategy incorporating an 11-factor scoring system was associated with reduced post-TIPS HE, with no clear difference in variceal re-bleeding, stent dysfunction or ascites recurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400087533.

Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

title: Early US Experience Using the Symani for Robotic-Assisted Microvascular Surgery.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted microsurgery provides motion scaling, tremor filtration, and enhanced visualization, offering potential advantages for complex microsurgical tasks. Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. This study presents the first multi-institutional US experience with Symani, evaluating feasibility, reconstructive outcomes, and technical challenges during its inaugural year of use in the United States.

METHODS: All robotic-assisted procedures performed between April 2024 and April 2025 at two tertiary academic centers were retrospectively reviewed. Demographics, clinical indications, flap type, and anastomotic details were extracted. Primary outcomes were anastomotic patency and flap loss. Secondary outcomes included overall surgical complications and conversion to conventional microsurgery.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients underwent robotic-assisted microsurgical procedures. Median age was 51 [IQR 39-63] years; 55.6% were female, and 74.1% identified as White. Indications included oncologic reconstruction (48.1%), trauma (18.5%), degenerative bony disease (14.8%), infection (11.1%), peripheral vascular disease (3.7%), and morphea (3.7%). A wide variety of flaps were performed, most commonly deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) (44.4%), free vascularized fibular grafts (18.5%), and scapular flaps (14.8%). Robotic assistance was employed for 27 arterial anastomoses (84.4%), three venous anastomoses (9.4%), and two nerve coaptations (6.3%). Anastomotic configuration was predominantly end-to-end (71.9%). No flap loss occurred. One patient (3.7%) required re-exploration for pedicle kinking. Two conversions to conventional non-robotic microsurgery were required (7.4%).

CONCLUSIONS: Early US multi-institutional experience demonstrates the Symani system is feasible and safe across diverse reconstructive procedures, enabling reliable microvascular anastomoses and nerve coaptations with minimal complications and no flap loss.

Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. title: Changes in Circulating Insulin and Glucose Homeostasis After Portosystemic Shunt Creation and Obliteration: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched through September 2026 for paired glucose or insulin measurements before and after either intervention. Ratios of post-intervention to pre-intervention means were pooled by random effects with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, excluding cohorts at critical risk of bias.

RESULTS: Fifteen cohorts (17 records) were included. After shunt creation, fasting insulin rose 49% (95% confidence interval 24% to 80%; 6 cohorts) and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance rose 55% (5% to 129%; 4 cohorts), whereas fasting glucose (2.5%; -0.3% to 5.4%; 5 cohorts), glycated haemoglobin, and fructosamine were unchanged. Glucose tolerance worsened in one of two cohorts tested (area under the curve +14%). Insulin rose more than C-peptide or proinsulin in four cohorts; clamp-measured insulin sensitivity was unchanged. After obliteration, fasting insulin fell 15% (one cohort) and insulin area under the curve 17% and 19% (two cohorts). Antihyperglycaemic requirements changed in both directions after shunt creation and fell after obliteration.

CONCLUSIONS: Shunt creation raises insulin by nearly half without changing fasting glucose or glycation markers, and obliteration reverses the pattern. Secretion markers change less than insulin, indicating altered first-pass hepatic insulin extraction rather than secretion. Insulin-based resistance indices may mislead after shunting, and the consequences of chronic shunt-induced hyperinsulinemia need prospective study.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

title: The many faces of contrast-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The increased use of endovascular procedures shows an increase of neurological deficits after intravascular administration of iodine-based contrast media (ICM). Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR. Additionally, we evaluated, if unifying different terminology of nADR seems to be warranted.

METHODS: A PRISMA-2020 systematic literature search was conducted. We included scientific articles on contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE), contrast-induced neurotoxicity (CIN), and transient cortical blindness (TCB) following administration of ICM. A total of 228 records were eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: The majority of neurological adverse reactions manifests after invasive contrast enhanced procedures and are mostly described as CIE, CIN, and TCB. Patients present with stroke mimickers and TCB. The onset of symptoms varies from shortly after the administration of ICM till up to 24 h following ICM application. In most of the patients the neurological symptoms are reversible. The available evidence suggests that there seems to be a common underlying pathophysiology, most likely due to dysfunction of the blood brain barrier. Risk factors include chronic or end stage renal disease, underlying vascular dysfunction, ICM volume, and the territory of ICM administration.

CONCLUSIONS: There is need for implementation of formal criteria and raising awareness on risk factors and therapeutic management of nADR following ICM administration. The authors suggest to summarize currently different terminology under 1 umbrella of contrast-associated encephalopathy.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: The increase of diagnostic and therapeutic endovascular procedures reveals ICM-associated neurological adverse reactions. Knowledge and awareness on neurotoxic effects after ICM application must be raised among radiologists and clinicians which may be enhanced by unifying the nomenclature.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: The increased use of endovascular procedures shows an increase of neurological deficits after intravascular administration of iodine-based contrast media (ICM). Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR.

title: 2025 National Guidelines on the Mediterranean Diet: Executive Summary of a Joint Report by Italian Scientific Societies and the National Institute of Health Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading global causes of morbidity, mortality, and escalating health care costs, driven largely by unhealthy lifestyles in an aging population.

OBJECTIVE: The Mediterranean Diet (MD), traditionally associated with healthy longevity, is increasingly recognized for its preventative and therapeutic benefits across many NCDs.

DATA SOURCES: Using the NUTRIGRADE methodology, a multidisciplinary panel of clinical, methodological, and public health experts conducted a comprehensive systematic review across 9 health domains and one economic domain.

DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted from multiple databases without date restrictions, assessing outcomes such as disease incidence and prevalence, mortality rates of nutrition-related NCDs, quality of life indicators, and relevant biochemical markers. Evidence was critically appraised and synthesized to formulate evidence-based recommendations.

DATA ANALYSIS: A total of 84 evidence-based recommendations were developed. The MD was found to significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the general population and cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, particularly in high-risk individuals. High-quality evidence supports the protective role of the MD against myocardial infarction, stroke, atrial fibrillation, and peripheral arterial disease. In oncological evidence, MD adherence has been found to be linked to a lower incidence of several cancer types and improved survival outcomes. Additional benefits include reduced incidence and progression of cognitive decline, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and obesity, and improved pregnancy outcomes. The strength of recommendations varied by outcome and target population, with many supported by robust evidence.

CONCLUSIONS: The MD is a scientifically supported dietary intervention with broad preventive and therapeutic benefits. Its integration into clinical practice, public health strategies, and policy initiatives is strongly recommended to promote health and reduce the global health care burden.
englishSummary: CONTEXT: Chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading global causes of morbidity, mortality, and escalating health care costs, driven largely by unhealthy lifestyles in an aging population. OBJECTIVE: The Mediterranean Diet (MD), traditionally associated with healthy longevity, is increasingly recognized for its preventative and therapeutic benefits across many NCDs. DATA SOURCES: Using the NUTRIGRADE methodology, a multidisciplinary panel of clinical, methodological, and public health experts conducted a comprehensive systematic review across 9 health domains and one economic domain.

title: SLC3A2 Silencing Alleviates Aortic Dissection via cAMP-PKA Activation and Disulfidptosis Inhibition.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis. Bioinformatic analyses of Gene Expression Omnibus datasets combined machine learning algorithms to identify SLC3A2 as a core gene. A murine AD model was established using β-aminopropionitrile and angiotensin II, with lentiviral knockdown of SLC3A2. Human aortic vascular smooth muscle cells (HAVSMCs) were challenged with BAY-876 to induce disulfidptosis. Histological staining evaluated medial degeneration and elastic fiber integrity. Disulfidptosis was assessed by measuring cystine accumulation and the protein expression of filamin A (FLNA) and NCK-associated protein 1 (NCKAP1). The involvement of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP)-protein kinase A (PKA) signaling was verified by genetic knockdown of its catalytic subunit (PRKACA). We observed SLC3A2 was upregulated in AD. SLC3A2 knockdown delayed lethal aortic rupture, reduced aortic medial degeneration, decreased reactive oxygen species and cystine, while restoring glutathione and free thiols. In HAVSMCs, SLC3A2 silencing preserved filamentous actin integrity, reversed the BAY-876-induced downregulation of α-smooth muscle actin and smooth muscle 22 alpha, and restored the aberrant expression of FLNA and NCKAP1. Mechanistically, SLC3A2 knockdown reactivated the cAMP-PKA signaling axis suppressed by BAY-876, and PRKACA knockdown abrogated the protective effects of SLC3A2 silencing on oxidative stress, cytoskeletal integrity, and disulfidptosis. In conclusion, SLC3A2 drives AD progression by suppressing cAMP-PKA signaling, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and disulfidptotic cytoskeletal collapse. Targeting the SLC3A2/cAMP-PKA axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AD.
englishSummary: Aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Disulfidptosis, a novel disulfide stress-induced cell death, remains unexplored in AD. We investigated whether solute carrier family 3 member 2 (SLC3A2), a disulfidptosis-related gene, contributes to AD pathogenesis.

title: Minimally Invasive Surgery for Insertional Achilles Tendinopathy Using a Double-Row SpeedBridge Repair with Rip-Stop Augmentation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The present video article describes a minimally invasive surgery (MIS) technique utilizing a double-row rip-stop SpeedBridge (Arthrex) repair for the treatment of insertional Achilles tendinopathy (IAT). This procedure is utilized when nonoperative treatment has failed, with the goal of returning patients to their previous levels of activity while avoiding the complications associated with more open procedures. All products mentioned in the videos are manufactured by Arthrex.

DESCRIPTION: The surgical technique is performed with 4 small incisions-2 distal and 2 proximal. Any Haglund deformity and/or enthesophyte are resected with use of an MIS burr through the 2 distal portals. The central third of the Achilles tendon is partially detached with this resection and is repaired with use of a double-row repair. Proximal anchors are placed, and sutures are passed through the Achilles tendon. Working knotless sutures are tensioned to create a rip-stop suture. The sutures are passed and shuttled to the distal row, creating a double-row repair. The distal row is drilled and tapped. The double-row repair is completed with insertion of distal anchors under appropriate tension.

ALTERNATIVES: Nonoperative treatment is beneficial in the initial stages of the condition and is successful in 60% to 80% of patients1-3. Initial treatment strategies for IAT include RICE (rest, ice, compression, and elevation), nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and physical therapy. Eccentric exercise and extracorporeal shockwave therapy have shown promising results3. Paratendinous injections, such as with platelet-rich plasma, have shown various levels of success and need further evaluation3. When nonoperative treatment has failed, operative treatment is a viable option. The surgical approach should be chosen on a patient-specific basis, as different tendinopathy patterns and different associated osseous and soft-tissue conditions may influence preoperative planning. There are a variety of different surgical techniques that include open, endoscopic, and MIS procedures.

RATIONALE: This MIS technique utilizing a double-row SpeedBridge repair with rip-stop augmentation yields fewer wound complications, less pain, quicker initiation of rehabilitation protocols, and quicker return to sport compared with more invasive techniques. Furthermore, the addition of the rip-stop augment to the double-row SpeedBridge repair improves dynamic mechanical strength and mitigates suture tearing through the tendon4.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: In our experience, patients who undergo this technique will be weight-bearing in a controlled-ankle-motion boot immediately postoperatively and out of the boot by 6 weeks postoperatively, with progressive return to full activities as tolerated. Our study of 61 patients undergoing the double-row SpeedBridge repair demonstrated favorable outcomes, with Foot and Ankle Disability Index scores improving from a mean of 56.3 preoperatively to 98.62 at 12 months postoperatively and visual analog scale pain scores improving from a mean of 7.25 to 0.476. There were no postoperative ruptures at a mean follow-up of 12.5 months. Eleven patients had minor complications within 3 months, including 6 who reported some central numbness over the Achilles tendon6. We expect these outcomes to improve as surgeons become more comfortable and skilled performing MIS techniques.

IMPORTANT TIPS: Proper patient selection (chronic IAT with Haglund deformity and/or an enthesophyte) will help ensure optimal outcomes.It is important to develop a subcutaneous plane for suture passage.The use of fluoroscopy or a nanoscope is helpful in ensuring that the proper bone is resected with the MIS burr.We have found that the irrigator from the MIS burr can be utilized alongside a Frazier suction tip to help remove excess bone.Suture management is important. Precisely maneuver the sutures at all times; it is very important that the sutures do not get tangled so that the procedure flows efficiently.Make sure to fully tension both sutures in order to place the ripstop.

ACRONYMS AND ABBREVIATIONS: NSAID = nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugMRI = magnetic resonance imagingK-wire = Kirschner wireCI = confidence intervalBID = twice dailyprn = as neededDVT = deep vein thrombosis.

This procedure is utilized when nonoperative treatment has failed, with the goal of returning patients to their previous levels of activity while avoiding the complications associated with more open procedures. title: Sex-specific differences in patient-prosthesis mismatch following valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: Female sex is associated with increased rates of mortality and readmission following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and is a risk factor for patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM). Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI. This retrospective study analyzed 77 patients who underwent ViV-TAVI at Kettering Health from 2015 to 2021, evaluating PPM incidence and bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) utilization. Indexed effective orifice area following ViV-TAVI was compared between females and males using an unpaired t test. Fisher exact test assessed the association between BVF and PPM for the overall cohort and within each sex. Statistical analyses were performed using R software. Males represented 57% of patients (body mass index = 28.8 kg/m2), while females comprised 43% (body mass index = 29.1 kg/m2). There was no significant difference in average indexed effective orifice area between females and males (P = .370). BVF rates were similar between sexes (33.3% in females; 29.6% in males), with an overall reduction in PPM (P = .028) and in females (P = .029). Cramér's V showed a moderate association between BVF and PPM in the overall cohort (0.305) and females (0.475), with a weaker association in males (0.183). Similar rates of PPM between sexes suggest that appropriate patient selection and valve sizing are crucial in PPM prevention. The significant reduction of PPM with BVF in females calls for further research into sex-specific outcomes and optimization of ViV-TAVI results.

Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI.

title: Repeated nasal and gingival bleeding caused by high-flow maxillary arteriovenous malformation: A case report.
abstract:
RATIONALE: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital vascular anomalies characterized by abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins due to arrested embryonic development. Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

PATIENT CONCERNS: We report the case of a 21-year-old female presenting with recurrent, profuse left-sided nasal and gingival bleeding.

DIAGNOSES: Clinical evaluation, computed tomography angiography, and digital subtraction angiography were performed for diagnosis.

INTERVENTIONS: Endovascular embolization was performed as the primary treatment, with staged embolization treatment and a total follow-up of 14 months.

OUTCOMES: A high-flow maxillary AVM was confirmed. The initial embolization successfully controlled the hemorrhage. At the 8-month follow-up after the initial embolization, residual lesions were detected and treated with a second embolization. At the 6-month follow-up after the second embolization, no recurrent bleeding was observed.

LESSONS: Maxillary AVMs may present with both gingival bleeding and epistaxis and can easily mimic common dental conditions. Early recognition and timely endovascular intervention are essential to prevent life-threatening hemorrhage.
englishSummary: RATIONALE: Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are congenital vascular anomalies characterized by abnormal direct connections between arteries and veins due to arrested embryonic development. Although rare, maxillary AVMs may lead to life-threatening hemorrhage. The association of epistaxis with maxillary AVMs has been relatively underemphasized in the literature.

title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes.

RESULTS: Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially.

CONCLUSIONS: In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

title: Comparative evaluation of otolith function using vestibular evoked myogenic potentials and rotational chair testing.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Correspondence between off-vertical axis rotation (OVAR) responses and vestibular evoked myogenic potentials (VEMPs) remains unclear.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To relate VEMP findings to the gain difference between OVAR and earth-vertical axis rotation (EVAR).

MATERIAL AND METHODS: We prospectively studied 11 VEMP-normal adults and 12 patients with abnormal cervical and/or ocular VEMPs (cVEMP/oVEMP). EVAR and OVAR were sinusoidal at 0.16 Hz. Wilcoxon rank-sum tests compared groups; exploratory Spearman analyses pooled healthy participants with corresponding VEMP-abnormal patients. P values and confidence intervals were unadjusted for multiplicity.

RESULTS: EVAR and OVAR gains did not differ significantly. Median gain differences were 0.308 in healthy participants and 0.109 in patients (p = 0.0489; Cliff's δ = 0.485, 95% CI 0.030-0.848). Compared with healthy participants, the difference was lower in the oVEMP-abnormal subgroup (n = 10; p = 0.0346), but not significantly different in the cVEMP-abnormal subgroup (n = 6; p = 0.1317). Correlations with absolute asymmetry ratios were ρ = -0.108 for cVEMP (n = 17; p = 0.6806) and ρ = -0.485 for oVEMP (n = 21; p = 0.0275).

CONCLUSIONS AND SIGNIFICANCE: Results suggest preliminary associations with oVEMP findings, without establishing utricular specificity. Larger cohorts with comparable age and sex distributions are needed.

AIMS/OBJECTIVES: To relate VEMP findings to the gain difference between OVAR and earth-vertical axis rotation (EVAR). MATERIAL AND METHODS: We prospectively studied 11 VEMP-normal adults and 12 patients with abnormal cervical and/or ocular VEMPs (cVEMP/oVEMP).

title: Comparison of conventional logistic, random forest, and random forest-assisted models for 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model. The three models were compared in 251 patients with complete Model C predictors using 20 repeats of stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Mean AUCs (SD) were 0.9361 (0.0045), 0.8843 (0.0095), and 0.9301 (0.0089) for Models A, B, and C; corresponding Brier scores were 0.0886 (0.0033), 0.1246 (0.0026), and 0.0933 (0.0060). Model A showed slightly better average cross-validated discrimination and prediction error than Model C, whereas Model C performed better than Model B.

CONCLUSIONS: Random forest-assisted modeling did not improve cross-validated predictive performance over the simpler logistic model. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model.

title: Macroscopic evidence of regression of sinus dilatation inside the Florida sleeve.
abstract: The Florida sleeve procedure is a valve-sparing technique for aortic root aneurysms. Because redo surgeries are rare, macroscopic evidence of how the native aorta adapts inside the graft has never been reported. We report two reoperative cases performed for recurrent aortic regurgitation and infective endocarditis 12 and 14 months, respectively, after the initial Florida sleeve procedure. Intraoperatively, the previously folded, aneurysmal native aortic walls had neatly regressed and tightly adhered to the graft's inner surface, obliterating any potential dead space. These cases provide the first macroscopic evidence of true biological reverse remodeling inside the Florida sleeve.

Because redo surgeries are rare, macroscopic evidence of how the native aorta adapts inside the graft has never been reported. We report two reoperative cases performed for recurrent aortic regurgitation and infective endocarditis 12 and 14 months, respectively, after the initial Florida sleeve procedure.

title: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic clustering capture distinct clinically relevant aspects of carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract:
AIMS: Patients with carotid atherosclerosis exhibit substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, plaque characteristics, and future cardiovascular risk, which do not always align. Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 1075 patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with matched clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data. Unsupervised clustering was applied separately to each data modality, and resulting clusters were evaluated for overlap and association with current symptom status and 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Clusters derived from different modalities showed limited overlap, but distinct associations with clinical outcomes. Clinical clusters were most strongly associated with 3-year MACE, whereas histological and transcriptomic clusters were more closely related to current cerebrovascular symptoms. Transcriptomic clusters further delineated molecular pathways and plaque biology. Integration of modalities provided modest improvement in outcome stratification, indicating that these data types capture complementary rather than redundant information.

CONCLUSION: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data capture distinct but complementary aspects of carotid atherosclerosis, reflecting systemic cardiovascular risk, local plaque phenotype, and underlying biology, with differing relevance to current cerebrovascular symptoms and future cardiovascular risk. The choice of data modality should therefore be guided by the intended clinical or biological question, rather than assuming a single approach can capture the full disease spectrum.

Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

title: Embolic stroke and breakthrough thrombosis on direct oral anticoagulants in Libman-Sacks endocarditis associated with antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is a characteristic cardiac manifestation of antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), but its presentation and management in the era of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are poorly characterised. We describe a 37-year-old man with obesity, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease and recurrent unprovoked deep vein thrombosis who developed multiple embolic strokes while taking rivaroxaban. Transoesophageal echocardiography showed a sessile aortic valve mass; repeated blood cultures and 18F-FDG PET-CT were negative, and lupus anticoagulant was the only antiphospholipid antibody detected (probable APS). He was switched to low-molecular-weight heparin and acenocoumarol and the mass was excised; histology showed an organised fibrinous thrombotic vegetation, although papillary fibroelastoma could not be fully excluded. Following the CABARET recommendations, we searched MEDLINE/PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and DOAJ for reports published between January 2020 and September 2026 and included 62 case reports/series (63 patients) and four cohort studies. Median age was 40 years (range 19-78); 22/60 patients (37%) were men; 34/63 (54%) had primary APS and 6 (10%) catastrophic APS. When reported, the antibody profile was triple-positive in 22/39 (56%) and lupus-anticoagulant-only in 4/39 (10%). The mitral valve was involved in 41/62 (66%), the aortic in 19/62 (31%) and the tricuspid in 7/62 (11%). Ischaemic stroke occurred in 29/63 (46%) and heart failure or severe valve dysfunction in 31/63 (49%). Of 16 patients anticoagulated at diagnosis, 10 (63%) were receiving a DOAC. Valve intervention was performed in 35/63 (56%) and 4/63 (6%) died. LSE should be sought in patients with APS who have embolic events, particularly while on DOACs; the evidence remains observational.

title: Epidemiology of Complications After 1434 Foot and Ankle Surgeries at a Large Medical Center Performed Without Tourniquet.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Tourniquet use in foot and ankle surgery is common, but controversial because of associated ischemia-related tissue injury and thrombotic risk. It is unclear whether the benefits of tourniquet use outweigh its risks. There is a paucity of literature evaluating the complication profile of tourniquet-free procedures. The aim of this study was to characterize complication rates and evaluate the safety of tourniquet-free foot and ankle surgery.

METHODS: A retrospective review of tourniquet-free foot and ankle procedures performed by a single fellowship-trained surgeon at a tertiary academic medical center from January 2018 to December 2022 was conducted. Demographics, comorbidities, and procedure types were recorded. Complications included superficial infection, deep infection, noninfectious revision surgery, and venous thromboembolism (VTE) within 90 days. Associations between patient factors and complications were analyzed using chi-square testing.

RESULTS: A total of 1434 tourniquet-free procedures were performed in 1165 patients (mean age 48.9 ± 16.4 years; mean body mass index [BMI] 29.6 ± 7.2 kg/m2). Superficial infection occurred in 2.7%, deep infection in 0.98%, and noninfectious revision surgery in 0.98% of procedures. The rate of VTE was 1.6% (0.4% pulmonary embolism, 1.3% deep vein thrombosis). Diabetes, age, BMI, sex, procedure type, and opioid use were not associated with complications. Chronic pulmonary disease and hemiplegia/paraplegia were linked to higher deep infection rates. Revision surgeries were more frequent among patients with congestive heart failure, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary disease, renal disease, and mild liver disease. VTE risk was elevated among tobacco users, Hispanic patients, and those with a history of myocardial infarction, renal disease, or mild liver disease.

CONCLUSION: Tourniquet-free foot and ankle surgery demonstrated rates of infection, revision surgery, and VTE comparable to those reported for procedures performed with a tourniquet. Medical comorbidities and tobacco use were risk factors, whereas age, BMI, sex, diabetes, procedure type, and opioid use were not. These findings support the safety of a tourniquet-free approach and aid perioperative risk assessment and patient counseling.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Tourniquet use in foot and ankle surgery is common, but controversial because of associated ischemia-related tissue injury and thrombotic risk. It is unclear whether the benefits of tourniquet use outweigh its risks. There is a paucity of literature evaluating the complication profile of tourniquet-free procedures.

title: Real-World Use and Clinical Outcomes of Jetstream Atherectomy Extending to the P2/P3 Popliteal Artery Segments: Results of the PULSAR Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular treatment of mid- and distal popliteal artery (P2/P3) lesions remains challenging owing to repetitive mechanical deformation and concerns regarding permanent stent implantation. In this setting, Jetstream atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation; however, data on its use in the P2/P3 segments, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes remain limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 443 limbs of 381 patients who underwent Jetstream atherectomy for femoropopliteal artery lesions in a multicenter registry. Limbs were classified by the most distal segment treated with Jetstream into the SFA/P1 and P2/P3 groups. The primary outcomes were procedural characteristics and periprocedural safety, including distal embolization (DE). Secondary outcomes were 1-year primary patency (PP) and freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

RESULTS: The Jetstream atherectomy was extended to the P2/P3 segments in 94 limbs (21.2%). Distal protection was more frequently used in the P2/P3 group (90.4% vs. 80.8%, p = 0.035). Overall DE occurred in 37.2% of the P2/P3 group and 33.8% of the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.51), whereas DE requiring endovascular intervention was numerically more frequent in the P2/P3 group (9.6% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.067). Jetstream use extending to the P2/P3 segments was not independently associated with overall DE (adjusted odds ratio 1.22, 95% CI 0.72-2.07; p = 0.47). At 1 year, PP was 84.4% in the P2/P3 group and 85.0% in the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.74), whereas freedom from CD-TLR was 89.9% and 90.8%, respectively (p = 0.50).

CONCLUSIONS: Jetstream atherectomy extended to the P2/P3 segments in approximately one-fifth of the treated limbs, with more frequent use of distal protection. Although no clear differences in periprocedural complications or 1-year clinical outcomes were observed, careful attention to DE is warranted.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Endovascular treatment of mid- and distal popliteal artery (P2/P3) lesions remains challenging owing to repetitive mechanical deformation and concerns regarding permanent stent implantation. In this setting, Jetstream atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation; however, data on its use in the P2/P3 segments, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes remain limited. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 443 limbs of 381 patients who underwent Jetstream atherectomy for femoropopliteal artery lesions in a multicenter registry.

title: Lorlatinib-Associated Dyslipidemia in ALK-Positive NSCLC: Atherosclerotic Risk and the Unresolved Question of Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: Lorlatinib, a brain-penetrant third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has markedly improved outcomes in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In the CROWN trial, median progression-free survival had not been reached with first-line lorlatinib after 7 years of follow-up, compared with 9.1 months for crizotinib, with 7-year progression-free survival of 55% versus 3%. Median treatment duration was 62.6 months versus 9.6 months. This duration extends cumulative exposure to lorlatinib's characteristic metabolic toxicity: hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia. At 7 years, these occurred in 73% and 71% of patients receiving lorlatinib, with grade 3 or 4 events in 22% and 26%. Onset is rapid, at a median of about 2 weeks. At 5 years, any-grade elevations had persisted for a median of 36 to 38 months; 71% of events were managed with lipid-lowering agents. ALK-positive NSCLC carries a high risk of venous thromboembolism across observational cohorts and a meta-analysis, more so for venous than arterial events. Laboratory evidence suggests the EML4-ALK fusion raises tissue factor through the pERK1/2-AP-1 pathway. At 7 years, aggregate cardiovascular adverse events were similar between treatment groups, and venous events were not more frequent with lorlatinib; small event counts and differing treatment exposure limit comparison of individual events. Statin choice is limited because lorlatinib is a moderate cytochrome P450 3A inducer; rosuvastatin and pravastatin are preferred. We review lorlatinib-associated dyslipidemia and its management and separate two claims: prompt, guideline-concordant lipid management is supported by established atherosclerotic prevention principles, whereas any effect on venous thromboembolism remains untested.

Median treatment duration was 62.6 months versus 9.6 months.

title: Real-World Risk of Venous Thromboembolism with Bevacizumab Biosimilar versus Reference Biologic in Japanese Patients with Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Large-scale safety data for newly introduced bevacizumab biosimilars in routine oncology practice remain limited. As part of post-marketing safety evaluations under the Risk Management Plan in Japan, we evaluated the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) associated with a bevacizumab biosimilar (CTNK) and compared the findings with those for a reference biologic (Avastin®) in Japanese patients with cancer.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using a large-scale hospital-based claims database (Medical Data Vision) in Japan, we identified new users of bevacizumab diagnosed with colorectal, breast, or ovarian cancer or glioblastoma between November 2020 and February 2025. Patients were classified into the biosimilar group or the reference biologic group. The primary outcome was the incidence of VTE, evaluated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Exploratory safety outcomes, including bleeding/hemorrhage and infections, were also assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 8599 eligible patients (1967 in the biosimilar group and 6632 in the reference biologic group; male versus female patients, 45.60% and 41.74% versus 54.40% and 58.26%, respectively; median age, 69.0 years in both groups) were included in the primary analysis. The overall incidence of VTE was 2.36%. The adjusted hazard ratio for VTE in the biosimilar group compared with that in the reference biologic group was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 0.57-1.19; P = 0.30), indicating no significant difference. This finding was consistent across subgroups stratified by target cancer type or by VTE history. Furthermore, the incidence of exploratory safety events was comparable between the two treatment groups.

CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective cohort study showed no evidence of increased VTE risk with the bevacizumab biosimilar or major safety differences between the bevacizumab biosimilar and the reference biologic in Japanese patients with cancer, providing reassuring real-world evidence supporting the safe use of the bevacizumab biosimilar in routine clinical practice. title: The Case for Interpretable Geometry: Statistical Shape Models vs. Curvature-Based Descriptors in Aortic Disease Classification.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Quantifying aortic morphology is central to surgical planning for thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), yet no consensus exists on how best to represent three-dimensional aortic shape for outcome prediction. Two broad strategies have emerged: statistical shape analysis (SSA), which relies on statistical methods and dimensionality reduction to capture the most significant shape modes, and geometrically-informed approaches that extract descriptors grounded in differential geometry. Here, we directly compare these paradigms on a cohort of 290 CTA scans classified by surgical outcome (non-pathological, successful TEVAR, failed TEVAR).

METHODS: For the geometrically-informed approach, we use a two-dimensional feature space using fluctuation in integrated Gaussian curvature δ K and mean aortic radius R. For SSA, we construct a point-cloud shape model with dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and evaluate classification performance as a function of the number of retained principal components. Both approaches are evaluated by repeated cross-validation grouped by patient, with all scaling, PCA, and hyperparameter selection performed within the training folds, and by external testing on scans from the GORE TAG 08-01 trial.

RESULTS: SSA's leading principal components encode variations in global aortic size and shape and are statistically redundant with (R, δ K ), yet they lack a one-to-one correspondence with interpretable anatomical quantities. With the same number of dimensions, the geometric descriptors classified at least as well as SSA (Gaussian process classification, cross-validated weighted F 1 of 85.8% versus 84.9%). SSA's cross-validated F 1 peaked with two principal components (83.1%) and declined as more were added, although its training-set accuracy rose above 90%, which indicates overfitting. On the independent trial cohort, in which every patient required TEVAR, SSA classified 50.7% of scans as non-pathological, compared with 21.2% for the geometric approach, suggesting better generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Two physically defined descriptors classified aortic disease at least as well as the leading SSA modes and transferred better to an independent cohort. SSA modes offer an intuitive visualization of how shape varies across a cohort, but geometric descriptors, which are measured identically for any patient and do not depend on the cohort used to build a model, provide a more robust basis for patient-level classification.

Two broad strategies have emerged: statistical shape analysis (SSA), which relies on statistical methods and dimensionality reduction to capture the most significant shape modes, and geometrically-informed approaches that extract descriptors grounded in differential geometry. Here, we directly compare these paradigms on a cohort of 290 CTA scans classified by surgical outcome (non-pathological, successful TEVAR, failed TEVAR).

title: Diabetic foot disease.
abstract: Diabetic foot disease (DFD) encompasses the lower-extremity complications of diabetes mellitus, including peripheral neuropathy, peripheral artery disease, ulceration, infection and amputation. An estimated 199 million people worldwide had DFD in 2017, including 18.6 million with foot ulcers, which precede most lower-extremity amputations. The 5-year mortality approaches 30% after ulceration and >70% after major amputation, rivalling that of many advanced cancers. DFD disproportionately affects socioeconomically disadvantaged, rural and underserved populations, creating wide disparities in outcomes. Although DFD has traditionally been viewed as a neuropathic complication of diabetes mellitus, most clinically overt disease is neuroischaemic. Neuropathy permits injury to go unnoticed, whereas peripheral artery disease, which is present in ~50% of patients with foot ulcers, impairs healing and substantially increases the risk of amputation. The Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification has therefore emerged as a unifying framework for risk stratification, whereas multidisciplinary 'toe and flow' teams and advances in revascularization, wound care and pressure offloading have transformed management. Even after ulcer healing, recurrence reaches 40% at 1 year and ~60% within 3 years, reframing ulcer healing as remission rather than cure and emphasizing the need for lifelong surveillance and secondary prevention.

title: Association between atherosclerotic lower extremity peripheral artery disease and physical activity on carotid intraplaque haemorrhage.
abstract:
AIM: Lower extremity peripheral arterial disease (LE-PAD) combined with carotid atherosclerotic plaques increases carotid plaque instability and the risk of ischemic events. The benefits of regular physical activity (PA) on morbidity, mortality, and long-term quality of life in LE-PAD patients were previously demonstrated. The aim is to explore the association of PA levels and intercurrent LE-PAD on carotid plaque instability markers.

METHODS: Patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis>50% were divided into two groups: LE-PAD (+) and LE-PAD (-). PA levels were assessed using validated questionnaires, allowing further stratification into subgroups. Carotid plaque instability, particularly intraplaque haemorrhage (IPH), was assessed by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

RESULTS: Fifty-two patients were included (30 LE-PAD (+), 22 LE-PAD (-)). Among physically inactive patients, LE-PAD (-) patients presented a lower IPH score (estimate: -0.75, 95% CI: -1.33; -0.16, P=0.014). These differences were not observed in physically active ones. Moreover, in LE-PAD patients, physically active patients had a lower score of IPH than the less active ones (estimate: -0.54, 95% CI: -1.08; -0.01, P=0.048).

CONCLUSION: Patients with carotid atherosclerosis and LE-PAD that are inactive have higher intraplaque haemorrhage. Regular physical activity could therefore help mitigate carotid plaque instability in these patients.

The benefits of regular physical activity (PA) on morbidity, mortality, and long-term quality of life in LE-PAD patients were previously demonstrated. The aim is to explore the association of PA levels and intercurrent LE-PAD on carotid plaque instability markers.

title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

RESULTS: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

CONCLUSIONS: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded.

title: A standardised ultrasound strategy safely excludes recurrent deep-vein thrombosis without prior imaging.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnosing recurrent ipsilateral deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) is challenging because current diagnostic strategies often require comparison with prior imaging, which is frequently unavailable in clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether a sequential diagnostic strategy using colour duplex ultrasound with newly developed standardised criteria, and D-dimer testing could safely exclude recurrent DVT without previous imaging.

METHODS: In this multicentre diagnostic outcome study, we enrolled 466 consecutive outpatients with suspected recurrent ipsilateral lower-limb DVT at 27 centres in France. Ultrasound classified findings as acute occlusive/sub-occlusive thrombosis (absence of vein compressibility and flow, or flow outlining the thrombus, no reflux), chronic post-thrombotic changes (partial obstruction, partial compressibility and filling, reflux), or normal. Patients with non-diagnostic (i.e., inconclusive) ultrasound underwent D-dimer testing and, if positive (≥500 ng/mL FEU), repeat ultrasound at day 7±2. Anticoagulation was withheld after a negative strategy result. The primary outcome was the 3-month cumulative incidence of adjudicated symptomatic venous thromboembolism in untreated patients.

RESULTS: Baseline ultrasound was negative in 280 (60.1%), positive in 176 (37.8%), and non-diagnostic in 10 (2.1%). Five patients with non-diagnostic ultrasound had a negative D-dimer and five had a positive D-dimer but unchanged repeat ultrasound. Two patients (0.4%) were lost to follow-up. Among untreated patients with a negative strategy result, symptomatic venous thromboembolism occurred in three patients (1.1%; 95% CI 0.0-2.2).

CONCLUSIONS: The absence of venous occlusion or sub-occlusion on ultrasound safely excluded recurrent ipsilateral DVT without requiring comparison with prior imaging. This approach could simplify diagnostic pathways and overcome a major limitation of current strategies.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether a sequential diagnostic strategy using colour duplex ultrasound with newly developed standardised criteria, and D-dimer testing could safely exclude recurrent DVT without previous imaging. METHODS: In this multicentre diagnostic outcome study, we enrolled 466 consecutive outpatients with suspected recurrent ipsilateral lower-limb DVT at 27 centres in France.

title: Hypercoagulable Thrombin Generation Correlates with High-Risk Clinical Features and Venous Thrombosis Recurrence.
abstract: Following venous thromboembolism (VTE), predictive biomarker testing for risk assessment is hampered by the presence of anticoagulation. This study aims to remove in vitro interference caused by direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with DOAC-Stop, enabling thrombin generation testing during anticoagulation. Platelet-poor plasma was collected approximately 3 months after VTE diagnosis from adults who were therapeutically anticoagulated with apixaban or rivaroxaban. Thrombin generation testing was performed using ST-Genesia ThromboScreen, following use of DOAC-Stop. A total of 251 patients were included (mean age 55.4 years, 54.2% male). Patients with thrombophilia and/or family history of VTE demonstrated hypercoagulable thrombin generation parameters. A total of 165 patients (65.7%) were classified as clinically "high risk," defined as one or more of unprovoked pulmonary embolism (PE) and/or proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT), family history of VTE, personal prior history of VTE, and hereditary thrombophilia, with remaining cases considered "low-risk" VTE. The "high-risk" group demonstrated increased peak height, endogenous thrombin potential, and velocity index compared with the "low-risk" cohort. About 52.2% (n = 131/251) of all patients subsequently ceased anticoagulation, with five episodes of unprovoked recurrence occurring within 1 year of cessation. These patients had higher median peak height (139.4 vs. 104.6%, p = 0.043, percentile difference - 34.8, 95% confidence interval (CI): [- 68.4, - 1.81]) and ETP (119.5 vs. 103.7%, p = 0.006, percentile difference: - 27.5, 95% CI: [- 43.5, - 11.3]) without thrombomodulin. This study provides evidence that thrombin generation testing after DOAC-Stop can identify hypercoagulable VTE patients without interrupting anticoagulation. Thrombin generation was increased in several groups with clinical risk factors associated with hypercoagulability. Key thrombin generation parameters were increased and associated with unprovoked VTE recurrence in patients who later stopped anticoagulation. Larger confirmatory studies are required.

This study aims to remove in vitro interference caused by direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) with DOAC-Stop, enabling thrombin generation testing during anticoagulation. Platelet-poor plasma was collected approximately 3 months after VTE diagnosis from adults who were therapeutically anticoagulated with apixaban or rivaroxaban.

title: Assessment of aspirin response in patients undergoing neuroendovascular treatments: A comparison of five platelet function tests across two platforms.
abstract: Aspirin is widely used for periprocedural antiplatelet therapy in neuroendovascular procedures; however, variability in patient response poses clinical challenges. This study aimed to assess five platelet function tests on two different platforms: light transmission aggregometry (LTA) using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system, which were utilized to assess patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Platelet function was assessed at three time points: before surgery, 1-3 days after surgery, and 1 month following the procedure. The assessments included maximum aggregation (MA) induced by 1 mM arachidonic acid (AA), 10 μM ADP, and 1 μg/mL collagen, as well as collagen-induced platelet aggregation level (CPAL) and aspirin reaction units (ARU). Significant perioperative changes were observed only with 1 mM AA MA, which increased immediately after surgery (p < 0.001) and decreased at 1 month (p = 0.013), while other tests showed no significant differences. Correlation analysis revealed the strongest association between 1 mM AA MA and 1 μg/mL collagen MA (r = 0.65), followed by CPAL (r = 0.62). ARU correlated modestly with LTA-based measures (r ≤ 0.34). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified CPAL >6.0 and collagen MA > 43.2% as equivalent to AA MA > 20%. In this cohort, perioperative changes were detected by 1 mM AA MA but not by the other platelet function tests, and correlations between VerifyNow ARU and LTA-based measurements were modest. However, the clinical significance of these differences remains to be established. Automated LTA using CN-6000 may offer a practical option for aspirin monitoring in patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate its clinical utility.

A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism in adults with sepsis: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adults with sepsis are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), because of sepsis-related inflammation, endothelial injury, coagulation activation and treatment-related exposures. Although several potential risk factors have been reported, the evidence remains fragmented and findings are inconsistent across populations, VTE subtypes and diagnostic approaches. This protocol aims to prespecify transparent and reproducible methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis of factors associated with incident VTE in adults with sepsis.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prospective and retrospective cohort studies and case-control studies involving adults with sepsis or septic shock will be included. Studies evaluating potential risk factors for incident VTE after sepsis onset or diagnosis will be eligible. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library will be searched from inception to the final search date, supplemented by grey-literature searching and citation screening. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment. Where sufficient comparable data are available, random-effects meta-analysis will be conducted, with adjusted estimates prioritised. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses will be performed to explore heterogeneity, and certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE approach adapted for prognostic-factor evidence.

title: Ultrasound Thermal Strain Imaging for Atherosclerosis Plaque Characterization: Image Acquisition, Processing, and In Vivo Results in a Porcine Model.
abstract: The accumulation of lipids in atherosclerosis plaque (AP) is one of the key features associated with plaque rupture, which can lead to heart attack and stroke. To predict rupture-pone cases, ultrasound thermal strain imaging (US-TSI) can identify lipids based on the contrast of the echo shift gradient between water-bearing tissue and lipids induced by different speed-of-sound (SoS) changes when temperature increases. However, US-TSI faces technical challenges in vivo: 1) heating a sufficiently large tissue volume within the imaging field-of-view (FOV) safely, uniformly, and effectively; 2) thermal-induced echo shifts (< 10 μm) are often masked by physiological motions greater than 50 μm. This study aimed to overcome these obstacles. We developed a new US-TSI transducer design along with image acquisition and processing techniques. Specifically, a co-registered multi-beam approach was used to enlarge the diagnostic FOV and a wavelet-based motion analysis was conducted to reconstruct extremely small SoS change-induced echo shifts in vivo. Experiments were conducted on a tissue-mimicking phantom, a human carotid endarterectomy (CEA) sample, and in the femoral artery of a hypercholesterolemic pig. Experimental US-TSI results were compared to the histology for lipid staining. Experiments with the tissue-mimicking phantom and CEA sample demonstrated the capability of large-FOV US-TSI. Successful in vivo US-TSI lipid detection was achieved, for the first time, in a large animal AP model. This work introduces new methods to enable in vivo US-TSI for AP lipid detection, paving the way for further validation in pre-clinical large animal studies and translational human subject studies on carotid artery.

title: Association Between Post-procedural Mean Arterial Pressure and Functional Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-vessel occlusion (LVO) strokes carry high morbidity despite advances in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Optimal post-EVT blood pressure (BP) management remains unclear, with current guidelines recommending uniform targets. We investigated the association between post-EVT mean arterial pressure (MAP) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVO stroke at Emory University Hospital (2016-2024) who underwent EVT. BP readings up to 48 h postprocedure were extracted and summarized in sequential time windows. Maximum MAP deviation from postprocedural baseline served as the primary exposure, specified a priori. Outcomes included modified Rankin Scale (mRS) grade at discharge as the primary measure dichotomized as favorable (mRS grades 0-2) versus unfavorable (mRS grades 3-6). Associations were examined using restricted cubic spline logistic regression with a likelihood-ratio test for nonlinearity. Patients were stratified by baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS).

RESULTS: Among 632 patients (median age 66 years, 53.0% male), successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] grade 2b-3) was achieved in 93.7%. Despite this, only 23.7% achieved favorable outcomes at discharge. Larger deviations in either direction from the individual baseline tended to accompany higher discharge mRS grade, but the shape of this association varied with the time window examined and with the summary metric used to define the exposure. It also differed by baseline stroke severity: severe strokes (NIHSS ≥ 16) showed comparatively flat associations, whereas in milder strokes (NIHSS ≤ 5) larger deviations tended to accompany higher mRS grades.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, single-center analysis, the association between early post-EVT MAP deviation and functional outcome differed across multiple conditions varying with the time window examined, the summary metric used, and baseline stroke severity. These findings suggest that post-EVT hemodynamic variability may be relevant in a patient-specific way, challenging the adequacy of uniform BP targets and supporting further investigation of individualized management strategies.

Optimal post-EVT blood pressure (BP) management remains unclear, with current guidelines recommending uniform targets. We investigated the association between post-EVT mean arterial pressure (MAP) and functional outcomes.

title: Tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement of ANCA-associated vasculitis: A diagnostic challenge mimicking infective endocarditis.
abstract: Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated vasculitides (AAV) are small-vessel vasculitides with heterogeneous clinical manifestations. Cardiac valvular involvement is rare and may closely mimic infective endocarditis, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Tricuspid valve involvement, especially at the subvalvular apparatus, is particularly uncommon. We report a case of a 46-year-old man who presented with constitutional symptoms, pulmonary nodules with cavitation, acute kidney injury, venous thromboembolism, and positive c-ANCA with anti-proteinase-3 antibodies. Transesophageal echocardiography revealed a serpiginous vegetation attached to the tricuspid subvalvular apparatus, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, extensive infectious evaluation, including multiple blood cultures, was negative. Kidney biopsy demonstrated pauci-immune crescentic and necrotizing glomerulonephritis, supporting a diagnosis of granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA). Antibiotics were discontinued, and the patient was treated with glucocorticoids, rituximab, and avacopan, resulting in marked clinical improvement. Follow-up echocardiography demonstrated complete resolution of the subvalvular apparatus vegetation without surgical intervention. This case highlights a rare presentation of GPA with tricuspid subvalvular apparatus involvement and underscores the importance of distinguishing AAV-related endocardial disease from infective endocarditis. Histopathologic findings, particularly renal biopsy, can be critical in establishing the correct diagnosis. Recognition of this entity is essential, as appropriate immunosuppressive therapy may lead to resolution of valvular lesions and avoidance of unnecessary antimicrobial therapy or surgical intervention.

Cardiac valvular involvement is rare and may closely mimic infective endocarditis, posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. title: Median arcuate ligament syndrome: Current evidence and controversies-A narrative review.
abstract: Median arcuate ligament syndrome is a rare and controversial cause of chronic abdominal pain, attributed to extrinsic compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament. The 2025 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider median arcuate ligament syndrome a diagnosis of exclusion and recommend management in specialized multidisciplinary centers. Anatomical compression of the celiac artery has been recognized for over a century, but a clear clinicopathological entity remains disputed. Median arcuate ligament syndrome is rare, with an estimated incidence of about 1.3 (0.5-3.6) per 100,000 inhabitants in a recent Dutch population study. Patients, predominantly women, typically present with long-standing postprandial epigastric pain and, in most cases, weight loss, often after years of extensive investigations for more common gastrointestinal disorders. Both ischemic and neurogenic mechanisms have been proposed, and data support elements of each. Diagnostic work-up relies on exclusion of differential diagnoses and imaging evidence of ⩾70% celiac artery stenosis, often with dynamic testing. Laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic decompression and video-assisted retroperitoneal decompression of the celiac artery are now the preferred approaches. Clinically significant symptom improvement is reported in up to 80% of operated patients, although treatment failure rates close to 50% have also been reported in large multicenter cohorts. Median arcuate ligament syndrome remains a challenging and controversial diagnosis with limited high-quality evidence. Careful patient selection, multidisciplinary evaluation, and realistic expectations regarding prognosis are essential. Ongoing randomized controlled trials and studies on objective ischemia biomarkers and quality of life may help refine indications and improve outcomes.

Anatomical compression of the celiac artery has been recognized for over a century, but a clear clinicopathological entity remains disputed.
