title: Safety of home treatment for incidental pulmonary embolism in cancer patients.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) is increasingly detected in computed tomography (CT) scans for scheduled cancer staging, but the safety of outpatient management in these patients with active cancer remains uncertain, as current guidelines usually do not define patients with pulmonary embolism and cancer as low risk.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival. Events were unscheduled consultations or emergency department presentations, progression of venous thromboembolism, clinically relevant bleeding or death.

RESULTS: Of 212 patients included, 89.2% were managed as outpatients. Patients treated at home were less likely to have bilateral pulmonary embolism, evidence of right ventricular dysfunction, an elevated troponin or hypoxemia. 90-day all-cause mortality was 5.2%, deaths occurred usually while the patient was receiving hospice care. For patients treated at home clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1.6% and progression of thromboembolism in 2.1%.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients diagnosed with iPE, most patients were treated at home. With 90-day mortality likely being mainly caused by the malignancy, home treatment appears safe if cancer is the only risk factor present.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S.

METHODS: We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality.

RESULTS: Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.

title: Post-Traumatic Abdominal Aortic Dissection Associating Solid Organ Injury in a Child.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Handlebar injuries are frequent events in children, often perceived as minor, but may result in severe intra-abdominal damage.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 13-year-old boy who sustained a blunt abdominal trauma following impact against a bicycle handlebar. In this case, the trauma produced an unusual and potentially life-threatening combination of lesions, including massive hemoperitoneum, a deep hepatic laceration, a severe pancreatic injury with disruption of the main pancreatic duct, and a post-traumatic dissection of the infrarenal abdominal aorta.

RESULTS: The patient was admitted in critical condition and underwent prompt clinical, laboratory, and radiological evaluation. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed the extent of the abdominal injuries and confirmed the vascular involvement. Given the complexity and severity of the findings, management required a rapid multidisciplinary approach involving pediatric surgeons, interventional radiologists, vascular surgeons, and gastroenterologists. The infrarenal aortic dissection was treated urgently with an endovascular approach using the placement of a covered stent, allowing successful exclusion of the lesion and stabilization of the vascular injury while avoiding open surgery. The hepatic injury was managed conservatively with close hemodynamic and radiological monitoring. During the subsequent clinical course, the patient developed a large post-traumatic pancreatic pseudocyst related to the pancreatic duct disruption. This complication was successfully treated with endoscopic ultrasound-guided drainage using a lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS), which allowed effective internal drainage and progressive resolution of the collection.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the potentially severe nature of bicycle handlebar injuries in children and emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for occult intra-abdominal and vascular injuries. Early diagnosis and timely multimodal management are crucial to optimize outcomes in these complex traumatic scenarios.

title: An MRI-Based Framework for Patient-Specific Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Mechanics Assessment.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To develop and validate a patient-specific Bayesian inverse modeling framework for the simultaneous estimation of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) wall and intraluminal thrombus (ILT) material properties using in vivo magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

METHODS: Finite element models (FEMs) of four AAA patients were constructed from MRI geometries. Bayesian optimization combined with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was applied to identify nonlinear anisotropic material parameters minimizing the discrepancy between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements. Validation was performed against equibiaxial mechanical tests on tissues excised from the same patients. Sensitivity analyses assessed the impact of wall thickness and ILT inclusion on stress predictions.

RESULTS: Bayesian-identified parameters closely matched experimental equibiaxial responses, reproducing both displacement magnitudes and anisotropy. RMSE values between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements were low, confirming high model fidelity. Peak wall stresses (PWS) distributions revealed that ILT significantly attenuates wall stress, with stress concentrations localized in ILT-free regions. Moderate variations in wall thickness or ILT material properties had limited impact on PWS locations, while exclusion of ILT markedly increased predicted stresses.

CONCLUSION: The proposed Bayesian framework provides a robust, patient-specific methodology for accurate estimation of AAA wall and ILT mechanical properties, enabling reliable prediction of wall stress distributions and highlighting the protective role of ILT. This approach has potential to improve individualized rupture risk assessment and inform clinical decision-making.

Bayesian optimization combined with Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) was applied to identify nonlinear anisotropic material parameters minimizing the discrepancy between FE-predicted and MRI-derived displacements.

title: Improving venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in hospitalized pediatric patients with inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Youth hospitalized with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. Using quality improvement methods, we aimed to increase the rate of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst select hospitalized patients with IBD by reaching 90% algorithm adherence by June 2023 and sustaining.

METHODS: Current evidence, external institutional algorithms, and multidisciplinary collaboration (hematology, pharmacy, surgery) were used to create an algorithm for providing pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin. The algorithm was implemented in February 2023 for all patients admitted with active IBD to a large, tertiary care children's hospital. Rates of algorithm adherence and rates of enoxaparin receipt during the project period were compared to baseline rates. Patient and provider education, electronic data tracking, and regular data auditing and review with providers were used to improve algorithm adherence. Reasons for non-adherence to the algorithm and rates of VTE, bleeding complications, and medication side effects during hospitalization were tracked.

RESULTS: The proportion of patients who appropriately followed the algorithm reached 94%, increased from 50% when the algorithm was retrospectively applied to the pre-project period (p < 0.001). The total proportion of hospitalized patients who received pharmacologic prophylaxis increased from 1% to 31% (p < 0.001). Following algorithm introduction, there were no VTEs or reported complications from enoxaparin during hospitalization.

CONCLUSIONS: The introduction of a standardized algorithm was associated with significantly increased rates of pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis amongst children hospitalized with IBD with no recorded adverse in-hospital events.

Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin is routine in adults hospitalized with IBD, but standardized pediatric protocols are rare. title: Suture-Only vs Hybrid Closure Techniques for Vascular Access Haemostasis in Percutaneous Cardiovascular Procedures: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vascular complications and bleeding increase morbidity and mortality after percutaneous cardiovascular procedures, including transcatheter aortic valve replacements (TAVR) and percutaneous endovascular aneurysm repair (pEVAR), often from vascular closure device (VCD) failure. We compared suture-only (SO) with suture and plug-based hybrid (HSP) vascular closure technique for vascular access haemostasis after percutaneous procedures such as TAVR and pEVAR.

METHOD: We performed a systematic literature search of randomised controlled trials (RCT) and observational studies using PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and ClinicalTrials.gov following the PRISMA guidelines. The study protocol was registered at PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024627875). We calculated the relative risk (RR) and 95% confidence interval (CI) for individual end points of vascular complications, bleeding risk, VCD failure, and mortality, using random-effects models to report overall effect sizes.

RESULTS: Nine studies, including two RCTs and seven observational studies, comprising 3,765 patients (SO, 1,971; HSP, 1,790), were analysed. The SO strategy was associated with a significantly higher risk of vascular complications (RR 1.95; p<0.01), bleeding (RR 2.14; p=0.01), and VCD failure (RR 4.00; p<0.01) compared with the HSP technique. No significant difference was noted in all-cause mortality (RR 1.61; p=0.11) between the two groups, although the analysis was limited by the relatively small number of observed events and wide CIs.

CONCLUSIONS: Use of the HSP technique for vascular access haemostasis after TAVR or pEVAR was associated with significantly lower rates of vascular complications, bleeding, and VCD failure compared with SO closure, without a significant difference in mortality.

title: Operative management and outcomes of symptomatic carotid near occlusions stenosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To present the outcomes of carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion (CNO) and to compare these outcomes with those of patients with symptomatic non-CNO carotid stenosis.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis included patients who underwent CEA of the internal carotid artery between January 2011 and December 2025. Outcomes in patients with symptomatic CNO were compared with those in patients with symptomatic non-CNO using propensity score matching on sex, age, amaurosis fugax, hyperlipidaemia, emergency status, and shunt as matching covariates. The primary endpoint was perioperative stroke, defined as a stroke occurring within 30 days after surgery. Secondary endpoints were cranial nerve injury, cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome, myocardial injury after non-cardiac surgery, surgical revision, bleeding complications, reintubation, and in-hospital mortality.

RESULTS: In the unmatched cohort, 1,321 patients underwent carotid endarterectomy (CEA), of whom 85 (6.4%) presented with symptomatic CNO. After propensity score matching (2:1), 255 patients were analysed, comprising 85 with symptomatic CNO and 170 matched controls with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis. Baseline and operative characteristics were well balanced. The perioperative stroke rate was similar between patients with symptomatic CNO and those with symptomatic non-CNO stenosis (1.2% vs. 2.4%). No significant differences were observed in myocardial injury (2.4% vs. 2.4%, p>0.9), cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (13% vs. 14%, p>0.9), cranial nerve injury (5.9% vs. 4.1%, p=0.5), surgical revision (7.1% vs. 5.9%, p=0.7), or postoperative bleeding (5.9% vs. 5.3%, p>0.9).

CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy using the eversion technique appears feasible and can be performed with an acceptable perioperative complication rate in selected patients with symptomatic carotid near-occlusion. Although no statistically significant differences in perioperative outcomes were observed compared with patients undergoing CEA for conventional symptomatic carotid stenosis, the limited sample size and low event rates preclude conclusions about equivalence. Further studies with larger cohorts and long-term neurological follow-up are warranted to establish the clinical benefit of surgical revascularisation in this patient population.

title: Survival and Aortic Reintervention Following Hemiarch vs. Extended Arch for Acute Type A Dissection in Patients Over Age 65.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although ascending hemiarch replacement is considered standard, some have advocated extended arch reconstruction as the preferred strategy in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

METHODS: Patients aged ≥65 years undergoing non-elective hemiarch or extended arch for ATAAD in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Database with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services linkage (July 2017-2023,N=3,562;2,442[68.6%] hemiarch;1,120[31.4%] extended arch) were compared. Primary endpoints were long-term mortality and aortic reintervention beyond 30 days and were analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and cumulative incidence functions, followed by multivariable regressions.

RESULTS: Hemiarch patients tended to be slightly older (73.8±6.1vs.73.1±5.9 years), female (46.6%vs.39.6%), and hyperacute ATAAD (80.1%vs74.7%). Malperfusion was more frequent in extended arch (27.8% vs 20.6%). Extended arch patients had: i) longer cardiopulmonary bypass, cross-clamp, and circulatory arrest times and ii) more frequent antegrade and/or retrograde cerebral perfusion. Short-term outcomes and rates of concomitant procedures were similar between groups. Risk-adjusted analysis showed no treatment effects for survival, aortic reintervention, operative mortality, and stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Extended arch for treatment of ATAAD in patients aged ≥65 years was not associated with improved mortality or aortic reintervention compared to hemiarch at intermediate followup. Absent patient-specific indications, hemiarch may be sufficient in patients aged ≥65 years with ATAAD.

Patients aged ≥65 years have increasing competing risk of non-aortic death, potentially undermining the late benefits of extended arch for ATAAD. The impact of hemiarch vs extended arch for ATAAD on long-term survival and aortic reintervention in this population is examined.

title: Variation in Inferior Vena Cava Filter Retrieval Across U.S. Veterans Health Administration Facilities.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters prevent pulmonary embolism (PE) in patients unable to receive anticoagulation but require prompt retrieval once protection is no longer needed. Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective longitudinal cohort study included Veterans who underwent IVC filter implantation at VA facilities between 2016 and 2023. Veterans who died within 90 days of implantation or lacked 1 year of follow-up were excluded. IVC filter implantation and retrieval were identified using procedure codes in the VA Corporate Data Warehouse. A multivariable Bayesian mixed-effects model estimated risk-adjusted retrieval rates across facilities. Logistic regression was performed to identify specific patient- and facility-level factors associated with non-retrieval.

RESULTS: Among 3,670 Veterans (median age 69 years; 95.9% male), retrieval occurred in 10.5% within 90 days, 22.2% within 1 year, and 24.7% overall. Risk-adjusted 1-year retrieval varied widely across facilities: 0-60%. Older veteran age (> 75 years), facility academic affiliation, and Southern census region were associated with lower retrieval, whereas implantation at higher-complexity facilities and pre-COVID years were associated with higher retrieval.

CONCLUSIONS: IVC filter retrieval rates among Veterans remain low but exceed those reported in non-VA Medicare cohorts. Substantial inter-facility variation highlights opportunities to standardize structured device surveillance, with clear responsibility for follow-up.

Despite national safety advisories and multidisciplinary guidelines, IVC filter retrieval remains low in the United States. How much variation underlies low retrieval across Veterans Affairs (VA) facilities has not been studied.

title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.

RESULTS: The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.

CONCLUSION: Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.

Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

CONCLUSION: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

title: Dissecting the molecular machinery of CRISPR-associated transposons.
abstract: CRISPR-associated transposons (CASTs) are naturally occurring mobile genetic elements that combine programmable RNA-guided DNA recognition with transposase-mediated integration, enabling site-selective insertion of kilobase-scale DNA without nuclease-induced double-strand breaks. Current structural and biochemical knowledge can be viewed in terms of three functional modules: the transposase module, which performs DNA cleavage and strand transfer; the AAA+ ATPase TnsC, which forms a recruitment and regulatory platform; and TnsD or CRISPR effector-TniQ targeting complexes, which position this platform at selected DNA sites. Here, we synthesize recent structural and biochemical advances in target recognition, recruitment, donor-end pairing, and strand transfer. Comparisons with Tn7 and phage Mu highlight conserved transposase and ATPase functions and system-specific differences in how these components are organized and regulated. We discuss the implications of these advances for engineering programmable DNA-insertion systems and highlight unresolved questions in CAST transposition.

title: Three-dimensional longitudinal morphometric outcomes following minimally invasive surgery and helmet therapy in single-suture craniosynostosis.
abstract: The aim of this study was to evaluate clinical and three-dimensional morphometric outcomes following minimally invasive strip craniectomy combined with postoperative helmet therapy in children with single-suture craniosynostosis and to identify subtype-specific parameters suitable for objective outcome assessment. Fifty-seven patients with single-suture craniosynostosis treated between 2019 and 2024 were retrospectively analysed. Serial three-dimensional cranial photographs were obtained preoperatively, postoperatively, during helmet therapy, and at treatment completion. Morphometric assessment included cephalic index (CI), anterior arc angle (AAA), circumference index (CFI), and symmetry ratios (ASR, PSR), depending on synostosis subtype. Fifty-seven children (37% female) with single-suture craniosynostosis were included (31 sagittal, 17 metopic, 9 coronal suture synostosis). The mean age at operation was 12.3 weeks, and the average duration of helmet therapy was 9.7 months (SD 4.4 months). In sagittal craniosynostosis, significant improvements in the CI were observed (p < 0.001). In metopic craniosynostosis, AAA and CFI showed significant improvements (p < 0.001). In coronal synostosis, anterior volume ratios demonstrated stabilization during follow-up. Minimally invasive strip craniectomy combined with postoperative helmet therapy results was associated with improvements of morphometric outcomes in single-suture craniosynostosis. Subtype-specific indices such as CI, AAA, CFI, and symmetry ratios enable standardized and objective longitudinal assessment in routine clinical practice.

title: Urban-Rural Disparities in Outcomes of Acute Pancreatitis: A Nationwide Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of hospital location on clinical outcomes in patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis (AP).

METHODS: We used the National Inpatient Sample database (2016-2022) to identify adult patients with AP. Patients were stratified by hospital location into urban and rural groups. Data on demographics, comorbidities, infections, and clinical outcomes were collected. Multivariate regression was used to assess the association between hospital setting and outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 2 467 234 patients hospitalized with AP, 246 820 (10%) received care in rural hospitals. Patients in urban settings had a higher incidence of in-hospital mortality (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.48, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.35-1.62), sepsis (aOR 1.16, 95% CI 1.08-1.24), shock (aOR 1.77, 95% CI 1.64-1.92), acute kidney injury (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.20-1.29), intensive care unit admission (aOR 1.63, 95% CI 1.51-1.75), pulmonary embolism (aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.05-1.47), and deep vein thrombosis (aOR 1.78, 95% CI 1.52-2.09); (all P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Our findings indicate that patients with AP treated in urban hospitals experience worse clinical outcomes and greater health care utilization than those in rural settings. These results underscore the importance of early diagnosis and risk stratification, particularly in high-volume urban hospitals, to improve patient outcomes.

METHODS: We used the National Inpatient Sample database (2016-2022) to identify adult patients with AP. Patients were stratified by hospital location into urban and rural groups.

title: Predictors and Mid-Term Outcomes of Vascular Complications After Large-Bore Plug-Based Access-Site Closure in Patients Undergoing Transfemoral TAVI: A CHOICE-CLOSURE Substudy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The plug-based MANTA (Teleflex, Pennsylvania, USA) vascular closure device (VCD) is an alternative to suture-based VCDs for large-bore arterial closure after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but has been associated with higher rates of vascular complications. Predictors and outcomes of these complications are not well-analyzed, especially regarding the self-resorbing characteristics of the MANTA VCD.

OBJECTIVES: To identify predictors of access-site related vascular complications following transfemoral TAVI with the MANTA VCD, and to assess mid-term outcomes and late-onset events (after 30 days) in affected patients.

METHODS: This prospective substudy of the CHOICE-CLOSURE trial included all patients randomized to vascular closure with the MANTA VCD at the Leipzig Heart Center. Patients with vascular complications, defined according to the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-2 criteria, underwent additional clinical and ultrasound follow-up, at least 6 months after the index procedure. Predictors of vascular complications were assessed through multivariable analysis.

RESULTS: Of 237 patients treated with the MANTA VCD, 46 (19.4%) had an access-site related vascular complication. Pre-procedural dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) was the only independent predictor in multivariable analysis (Odds ratio 4.27, 95% confidence interval 1.58-11.59, p = 0.004). At a mean follow-up of 13.5 months, no new vascular complications occurred. Patients with an over-stented MANTA VCD (n = 5) had no in-stent stenosis, and stent diameters further expanded by 12.5% to 20.0%.

CONCLUSION: Pre-procedural DAPT independently predicted vascular complications after TAVI in MANTA patients. Patients with vascular complications had no further access-site late-onset events, and endovascular stenting of a MANTA VCD appeared safe.

Predictors and outcomes of these complications are not well-analyzed, especially regarding the self-resorbing characteristics of the MANTA VCD. OBJECTIVES: To identify predictors of access-site related vascular complications following transfemoral TAVI with the MANTA VCD, and to assess mid-term outcomes and late-onset events (after 30 days) in affected patients.

title: Economic and Humanistic Burden of Cardiovascular Comorbidity in Kidney Failure: Findings from a Systematic Literature Review.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its impact on economic and humanistic burden remains insufficiently characterized. We aimed to systematically review the published literature reporting economic outcomes, healthcare resource utilization (HRU), and humanistic impact of the association between advanced CKD and CVD.

METHODS: A systematic literature review (SLR) was conducted using MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane databases, and conference abstracts to identify evidence published between 2020 and December 31, 2025. Studies reporting economic or humanistic burden outcomes among adults with CKD G4-G5 or kidney failure and coexisting cardiovascular conditions were included.

RESULTS: In total, 6350 records were screened, with 87 studies meeting inclusion criteria. Across studies, coexisting CVD markedly increased costs and HRU in advanced CKD. In the USA, the costs per event ranged from $12,410 USD for systolic heart failure to $92,898 for chronic heart failure. Compared to CKD G4, patients in G5 incurred higher annual per patient hospitalization costs (77%), outpatient costs (65%), and total healthcare costs (61% (US) to 64% (non-US)). Emergency visits, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and rehospitalizations were more frequent among patients with coexisting CVD and advanced CKD compared to those without CVD, with 30-day readmission rates of 41% for critical limb ischemia. Evidence on humanistic burden, though limited, showed significant declines in mental health and quality of life among patients with CVD.

CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant CVD and advanced CKD or kidney failure substantially elevates the economic and humanistic burden compared to CVD or CKD alone, driving higher costs, increased healthcare utilization, and impaired quality of life. Targeted strategies addressing cardiovascular risk in patients with advanced CKD are essential to mitigate downstream clinical and financial consequences.

title: Robotic pulmonary artery reconstruction during lung resection: technical strategies, patient selection and current evidence.
abstract: Pulmonary artery (PA) reconstruction permits parenchyma-sparing resection in selected central lung cancers; its robotic application, however, requires control of a fragile vessel in a confined operative field. This narrative review examines published robot-assisted PA reconstruction, procedural configurations, haemorrhage management, patient selection and relevant video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) and open evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE and publisher sources were searched through 26 October 2026, with priority given to studies identifying actual PA repairs separately from bronchial sleeve operations. The early 30-patient uniportal robotic sleeve series contained four PA reconstructions, whereas a subsequent 134-patient sleeve cohort reported excellent overall margins without a separately extractable PA-specific denominator. In a contemporary series of 49 PA reconstructions after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, 21 operations were open and 28 were reported jointly as VATS/RATS. Small robotic technical series demonstrate tangential repair, angioplasty and circumferential anastomosis, but do not establish comparative vascular safety or durable patency. A large registry found fewer overall conversions during robotic than VATS lobectomy, although robotic conversions were proportionally more often emergent or vascular. Robot-specific safety depends on preplanned proximal and distal occlusion, unobstructed bedside access, disciplined clamp and suture strategies, and immediate conversion capability. Lung autotransplantation remains a separate, highly selected alternative. Available evidence supports feasibility in experienced programmes, not superiority over VATS or thoracotomy. Multicentre, PA-specific reporting is needed to establish vascular outcomes and reproducibility.

This narrative review examines published robot-assisted PA reconstruction, procedural configurations, haemorrhage management, patient selection and relevant video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) and open evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE and publisher sources were searched through 26 October 2026, with priority given to studies identifying actual PA repairs separately from bronchial sleeve operations.

title: Current trends in evaluation and management of superficial venous thrombosis (SVT).
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Superficial venous thrombosis (SVT) is characterised by thrombus formation accompanied by inflammation within the superficial venous system, most commonly affecting the lower limbs. SVT is relatively common, with an estimated incidence of 0.3 to 0.6 per 1,000 person-years in younger individuals and 0.7 to 1.5 per 1,000 person-years in older populations. These rates are comparable to those observed in DVT, which occurs in approximately 1 per 1,000 individuals annually.

METHODS: We performed a narrative review of the existing literature to evaluate current evidence and identify gaps in knowledge.

RESULTS: According to current National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidance, SVT can be categorised into low and high-risk groups. Low-risk SVT is defined by thrombus length less than 5 cm, below knee location, and the absence of significant thromboembolic risk factors. In contrast, high risk SVT includes thrombus greater than or equal to 5 cm in length, above-knee involvement, proximity within 3 cm of the saphenofemoral (SFJ) or sapheno-popliteal junction (SPJ), or the presence of risk factors. High-risk SVT is therefore considered analogous to DVT, requiring equivalent therapeutic anticoagulation and follow-up. Current SVT management Guidelines rely on risk stratification, but recommendations vary because the evidence base is limited. Key gaps remain, particularly for high-risk patients, including optimal treatment duration, management strategies, and recurrence prevention.

CONCLUSION: Future research should prioritise large-scale randomised controlled trials and real-world cohort studies to refine anticoagulant selection, optimise treatment duration, and support personalised risk prediction. Strengthening the evidence base will be essential to reducing practice variation and improving patient-centred outcomes in SVT management.

SVT is relatively common, with an estimated incidence of 0.3 to 0.6 per 1,000 person-years in younger individuals and 0.7 to 1.5 per 1,000 person-years in older populations. These rates are comparable to those observed in DVT, which occurs in approximately 1 per 1,000 individuals annually.

title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Patients with Resectable Colorectal Cancer According to Stage.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a significant source of morbidity in patients undergoing colectomy and proctectomy for colorectal adenocarcinoma. However, the association between cancer stage and VTE risk is unclear. We aimed to describe the association between colorectal cancer stage and post-operative VTE among patients undergoing resection for colorectal cancer.

METHODS: Utilizing the 2022-2023 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database, a retrospective cohort study was conducted. A multivariable logistic regression analyzed the association between VTE and cancer stage with adjustments for covariates.

RESULTS: Of 18,830 patients fitting inclusion criteria, 4,418 (23%) had stage I adenocarcinoma, 6,509 (35%) had stage II, 6,402 (34%) had stage III and 1,501 (8%) had stage IV; while 302 (2%) experienced postoperative VTE. On univariate analysis, patients with stage II, III and IV cancers had higher VTE rates than patients with stage I (stage I: 0.9%, stage II: 1.7%, stage III: 1.8%: stage IV 2.5%; p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis of VTE risk, patients with stage II, III and IV cancer had higher odds of VTE relative to patients with stage I cancer (OR for stage II vs. I: 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08, 2.27; p = 0.017; OR for stage III vs. I: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.22, 2.55; p = 0.002; OR for stage IV vs. I: 1.73, 95% CI:1.07, 2.79; p = 0.025).

CONCLUSION: Resectable colorectal cancers at higher stages are associated with increased risk of VTE. Understanding the differences in risk can help clinicians make more informed and targeted treatment plans for patients undergoing colectomy or proctectomy for locoregional adenocarcinoma.

However, the association between cancer stage and VTE risk is unclear. We aimed to describe the association between colorectal cancer stage and post-operative VTE among patients undergoing resection for colorectal cancer.

title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma: standardized technique and short-term outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To achieve the dual goals of effective tumor control and maximal renal function preservation, we have proposed a standardized robot-assisted nephron-sparing surgery combined with venous thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma (AML) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT). This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy. The radical-nephrectomy cohort served as a historical clinical comparator. The modified thrombectomy strategy followed the proposed "NSS" technical principles. Functional and oncological outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed without open conversion or intraoperative tumor-thrombus dislodgement, and no RAPN case required conversion to radical nephrectomy. The RAPN group had shorter operative time (160.0 vs. 232.5 min, p=0.021), shorter left renal vein clamping (3.0 vs. 16.5 min, p<0.001) and IVC clamping time (3.0 vs. 16.0 min, p<0.001), and better renal function preservation (p<0.001). Renal function was better preserved in RAPN group, primarily reflecting retention of the affected kidney. During the available follow-up (median 9 months in the RAPN group and 55 months in the Control group), no recurrence was detected; however, follow-up was insufficient for comparative or long-term oncological conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAPN with venous tumor thrombectomy appears technically feasible in patients with classic renal AML with VTT. This surgical approach could better preserve renal function, but the long-term outcomes require confirmation in larger series with longer follow-up.

This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy.

title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up. title: Impact of race, sex, and insurance status on outcomes following endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Racial, sex, and socioeconomic differences in stroke outcomes are well documented, but their associations with outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with acute ischemic stroke who underwent EVT at a comprehensive stroke center during 2016-2022. The analytic dataset contained 527 patients. Endpoint-specific available observations were used without imputation. Outcomes included expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (eTICI) grade, admission and discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), discharge and 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS), treatment-time metrics, and discharge disposition. Separate multivariable logistic regression models were fitted for seven clinical and procedural endpoints.

RESULTS: Final eTICI grade was available for 493 patients. Successful reperfusion (eTICI ≥2b) occurred in 449 (91.1%), and near-complete reperfusion (eTICI ≥2c) in 309 (62.7%). No demographic or payer variable was significantly associated with either reperfusion endpoint. Poor functional outcome occurred in 344 of 448 patients (76.8%) at discharge and 247 of 376 (65.7%) at 90 days. Black race and Medicare insurance were associated with poor discharge outcome. Female sex, Black race, and Medicare insurance were associated with poor 90-day outcome. Medicare and commercial insurance were associated with non-home discharge. Among 516 patients with available door-to-puncture time, the median was 69 min (interquartile range, 54-91), without statistically significant differences by sex, race, ethnicity, or payer.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing EVT at a single comprehensive stroke center, reperfusion rates were high and were not significantly associated with observed demographic or payer variables. Differences in functional outcomes and discharge destination were observed, but residual confounding, endpoint-specific missingness, and the single-center design limit causal interpretation.

The analytic dataset contained 527 patients.

title: Combination of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy in the treatment of the anterior saphenous vein insufficiency - a single-center retrospective study with long-term follow-up.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Isolated insufficiency of the anterior saphenous vein is common and as clinically relevant as the great saphenous vein insufficiency. Data regarding its optimal management are lacking.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosities who were treated at the Department of Dermatology, University of Lübeck, between 2013 and 2021. All patients underwent combined treatment consisting of ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy of the proximal intrafascial venous segment and phlebectomy of the extrafascial tributaries. The sclerosant was polidocanol. A successful outcome was defined as a combination of successful ablation and the absence of newly developed refluxing tributaries at follow-up.

RESULTS: 70 patients (56 female, 14 male) were included, with a mean follow-up period of 6.09 years (range: 6 months-10.2 years). The overall success rate was 81.4%. At follow-up, all patients showed an improvement in their clinical class according to the Clinical, Etiological, Anatomical, and Pathophysiological (CEAP) classification (p < 0.001). A significant correlation was found between the volume of polidocanol foam injected and successful sclerotherapy (p < 0.05).

CONCLUSIONS: Combined ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy and phlebectomy is an effective treatment for isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosis, providing long-term success while preserving the great saphenous vein.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Isolated insufficiency of the anterior saphenous vein is common and as clinically relevant as the great saphenous vein insufficiency. Data regarding its optimal management are lacking. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed data from patients with isolated anterior saphenous vein varicosities who were treated at the Department of Dermatology, University of Lübeck, between 2013 and 2021.

title: Conversion hip arthroplasty has a higher risk of venous thromboembolism disease at 30 days than primary total hip arthroplasty and revision total hip arthroplasty.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), represents a serious postoperative complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA.

METHODS: A retrospective cross-sectional analysis was performed using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database. Adult patients undergoing primary, conversion, or revision THA were identified using Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. A total of 475,002 patients met inclusion criteria (primary THA: 428,245 [90.2%], conversion THA: 10,637 [2.2%], revision THA: 36,120 [7.6%]) with a mean age of 65.6 years (range, 18 to 89); 55.0% women. The primary outcome was 30-day postoperative DVT. Multivariable logistic regressions evaluated associations between procedure type and DVT, adjusting for age, sex, BMI, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class, smoking status, chronic steroid use, and operating time.

RESULTS: Adjusted odds of DVT were significantly lower after primary THA (odds ratio (OR) 0.48, 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.28-0.88; p = 0.010) and revision THA (OR 0.44, 95% CI, 0.23-0.87; p = 0.014) compared with conversion THA. Independent predictors of higher DVT risk included older age, longer operating time, and chronic steroid use. Sex, BMI, ASA class, and smoking status were not independently associated with DVT.

CONCLUSIONS: Conversion THA is associated with higher 30-day DVT risk compared with both primary and revision THA on multivariable analyses. Recognition of conversion THA as a distinct procedural category associated with higher relative thromboembolic risk may improve perioperative risk stratification and guide more individualised thromboprophylaxis strategies.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolic disease (VTED), including deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), represents a serious postoperative complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA). While revision THA is traditionally considered higher risk than primary THA, the thromboembolic risks of conversion THA are still not well defined. This study compared 30-day DVT rates across primary, conversion, and revision THA.

title: Effectiveness and Safety of Prophylactic Inferior Vena Cava Filters in High-Risk Hip Fracture Patients: Clinical implications of an early retrieval strategy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).

METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study.

SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

PATIENT SELECTION CRITERIA: Patients older than 50 years who sustained a low-energy hip fracture (AO/OTA 31A, B, and 32A) and underwent prophylactic IVC filter insertion before hip fracture surgery between 2005 and 2025 were included. Prophylactic IVC filter placement was selectively performed in patients with either objectively confirmed deep vein thrombosis on preoperative screening or absolute contraindications to mechanical and pharmacological venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Those who had multiple trauma at the time of injury, a clinical follow-up duration ≤6 months after surgery, or undergone IVC filter placement following a confirmed diagnosis of PTE based on pulmonary computed tomography or lung perfusion scanning were excluded.

OUTCOME MEASURES AND COMPARISONS: The primary outcome was the rate of newly developed symptomatic PTE. Secondary outcomes included IVC filter-related complications, retrieval rates, and 30-day mortality.

RESULTS: One hundred fifty-six patients were included in the prophylactic IVC filter group (39 men 25.0%], 117 women [75.0%]; mean age, 75.8 ± 11.1 years; femoral neck [AO/OTA 31B], n = 71 [45.5%]; intertrochanteric [31A], n = 75 [48.1%]; subtrochanteric [AO/OTA 32A], n = 10 [6.4%];mean indwelling time, 9.1 days; retrieval rate, 88.5%). Among these patients, no cases of newly developed symptomatic PTE were observed (0%), whereas the incidence in the overall hip fracture cohort (n=4,568) was 0.44%. Filter-related complications occurred in 3.9% of patients (minor tilting, 2.6%; vessel adhesion, 1.3%), with no major mechanical failures such as migration or perforation. Although no thrombi were detected at insertion, 4.5% of the patients had trapped thrombi at the time of removal. The 30-day all-cause mortality rate was 1.3% (2/156) in the prophylactic IVC filter group, compared with 1.5% (67/4,568) in the overall hip fracture cohort. (p=0.845). Neither death in the prophylactic IVC filter group was attributed to PTE or an IVC filter-related complication.

CONCLUSIONS: In this study's selected extreme pulmonary thromboembolism risk cohort, including patients with CT-confirmed preoperative DVT, those clinically expected to undergo prolonged perioperative immobilization, or those with contraindications to prophylactic anticoagulation, such as GI bleeding, prophylactic inferior vena cava filter served as an effective and safe temporary bridge therapy rather than a routine prophylactic strategy.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Prognostic Level III.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of prophylactic inferior vena cava (IVC) filter in patients with hip fracture who were at high risk for pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE). METHODS: Design: Retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Single-center Level I Trauma Center.

title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores.

RESULTS: One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs.

CONCLUSION: In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT). METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131).

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Necrotizing Pancreatitis A Nationwide Analysis of Incidence, Risk Factors, and Outcomes.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Necrotizing pancreatitis (NP) is associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including portal vein thrombosis (PVT), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE), represent complications of NP. However, comprehensive characterization of individual VTE subtypes, risk factors, and outcomes in NP remains limited.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the 2020 National Inpatient Sample, among adult patients hospitalized with acute pancreatitis. The patients were categorized into NP and interstitial pancreatitis (IP) groups, with focus on impact of VTE in NP cohort. Outcomes included VTE incidence, risk factors, complications, mortality, length of stay, hospitalization charges, and intensive interventions. Multivariable regression analyses were performed adjusting for demographic and hospital-level covariates.

RESULTS: Of 199,190 AP hospitalizations, 5.74% had NP and 94.26% had IP. NP was associated with significantly higher incidence of PVT (6.08% vs. 0.48%, aOR 11.53), DVT (8.36% vs. 0.69%, aOR 11.19), and PE (1.44% vs. 0.24%, aOR 5.58) compared to IP (all P<0.001). All VTE subtypes significantly increased length of stay, hospitalization charges, and complication rates. Malnutrition (PVT aOR 2.79, DVT aOR 1.61, PE aOR 6.86) and coagulopathy (PVT aOR 2.41, DVT aOR 2.15) were consistent risk factors across all VTE subtypes. Among NP patients, PVT was uniquely associated with mortality (aOR 2.71, P=0.007), while DVT and PE were not.

CONCLUSIONS: NP is associated with markedly increased risks of all VTE subtypes compared to IP. VTE in patients with NP is associated with increased morbidity, with PVT uniquely associated with mortality. Malnutrition and coagulopathy represent potentially modifiable risk factors that may help identify high-risk patients. These findings support the need for prospective study of VTE screening and prophylaxis strategies in NP patients.

Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including portal vein thrombosis (PVT), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and pulmonary embolism (PE), represent complications of NP. However, comprehensive characterization of individual VTE subtypes, risk factors, and outcomes in NP remains limited.

title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 10 9 /l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

title: Impact of Inherited Thrombophilia on Cancer-associated Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies comparing genetic determinants in patients with cancer with and without venous thromboembolism (VTE). Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using Mantel-Haenszel models. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), respectively.

RESULTS: Twenty-one studies including 4,479 patients (1,115 with VTE) were included. Factor V Leiden (FVL) was associated with increased odds of CT (OR 2.48, 95% CI: 1.75-3.51; I 2 = 32%), with consistent findings after exclusion of device- or catheter-related thrombosis. Heterozygous FVL was associated with CT (OR 1.86, 95% CI: 1.27-2.73), whereas the homozygous estimate was imprecise (OR 3.42, 95% CI: 0.75-15.59). Prothrombin G20210A was associated with CT (OR 2.67, 95% CI: 1.56-4.58; I 2 = 0%). Exploratory analyses yielded estimates for methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR; OR 1.40, 95% CI: 1.02-1.93) and blood group O (OR 0.40, 95% CI 0.23-0.70); the latter was based on only two studies. Evidence for rarer determinants was sparse. Certainty was moderate for FVL and low or very low for other determinants.

CONCLUSION: FVL and prothrombin G20210A are associated with increased odds of CT. Current evidence does not support universal genetic screening but warrants prospective evaluation of the incremental predictive value of genetic markers beyond established CT risk models.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated thrombosis (CT) is a cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with malignancy. The contribution of inherited thrombophilia remains incompletely defined. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between inherited thrombophilia and other genetic determinants and CT risk in adults with malignancy.

title: Vascular risk prediction in migraine: A multimodality risk score based on artificial intelligence-electrocardiogram output, echocardiogram, and detailed migraine characteristics.
abstract: AimPatients with migraine, especially those with aura, have a higher risk of stroke and other vascular events. However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events. Herein, we aim to investigate the relative importance and combined effects of all three modalities for vascular risk prediction.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, we developed a multimodality prediction risk score to evaluate the vascular risks in patients with migraine based on the coefficients of variables extracted from our prior studies, including comprehensive AI-ECG atrial fibrillation prediction model output and computed delta age (ECG estimated age minus chronological age), echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics. We then included patients with at least one 12-lead ECG, transthoracic echocardiogram, and a visit with a headache specialist at any Mayo Clinic site within three years to evaluate the risk score. The outcome is a composite endpoint of acute ischemic stroke, acute myocardial infarction, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. We selected 20 risk parameters, including demographics, comorbidities, AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram features, and migraine characteristics found to be predictive of vascular events. Each variable was assigned a different risk score according to the hazard ratio (HR) and beta coefficient from prior Cox regression analysis for each modality. We used Contal and Q'Quigley's method to find the optimal cut-off, and an additional multivariate Cox regression was conducted to assess the relative risk of each parameter category in the final cohort. We investigated the added value of each modality by net reclassification improvement rate.ResultsA total of 29,928 patients, 12,778 patients, and 6819 patients were included to investigate how AI-ECG outputs, echocardiogram parameters, and migraine characteristics, respectively, predicted adverse vascular outcomes, and the results were used to develop a multimodal risk score. A total of 297 patients with migraine included in previous analyses, of whom 247 (83.2%) were female and 109 (36.7%) had aura, were used for proof-of-concept evaluation of the developed risk score. The mean (standard deviation, SD) age was 39.0 (13.3) and follow-up period was 68.9 (60.9) months. Thirty-five patients (11.8%) developed the composite endpoint. Those with a risk score ≥15 had a significantly shorter vascular event-free survival (HR [95% Confidence Interval (CI)], 3.83 [1.89-7.76]; p < 0.001) compared to those with a risk score <15 in our cohort of 297 patients. Furthermore, comorbidity (HR, 1.17 [1.06-1.30]; p = 0.003) and migraine characteristics (HR, 1.33 [1.06-1.67]; p = 0.014) were significantly predictive of the composite endpoint, whereas other categories were not. Net reclassification improvement was 17.7% (95% CI, 15.9-19.9%; p < 0.001) for AI-ECG model output, 16.9% (95% CI, 14.1-19.5%; p < 0.001) for echocardiogram, and 22.1% (95% CI, 16.7-26.9%; p < 0.001) for migraine characteristics, suggesting significant contribution from each modality.ConclusionThis pilot evaluation study supports the use of combined AI-ECG output, echocardiogram, and migraine characteristics for vascular risk prediction. Although future external validation and real-world clinical assessment is necessary, our preliminary results suggest significant added value of each modality and indicate the importance of obtaining detailed migraine features for vascular risk stratification.
englishSummary: AimPatients with migraine, especially those with aura, have a higher risk of stroke and other vascular events. However, the underlying mechanisms are complex, multifactorial, and may require integration of multimodal data for comprehensive characterization. We have conducted prior analyses on how artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled electrocardiogram (ECG), specifically the atrial fibrillation prediction model and age estimation model output, echocardiogram parameters, and detailed migraine characteristics separately predict vascular events.

title: Development and Internal Validation of an Integrated Clinical, Laboratory, and Ultrasound Model for 30-Day Venous Thromboembolic Deterioration After Acute Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: BackgroundShort-term prognostic tools for venous thromboembolic (VTE) deterioration after acute lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are limited. We aimed to develop and internally validate a model integrating clinical, laboratory, and duplex ultrasound characteristics.MethodsThis single-center retrospective cohort included 785 adults with ultrasound-confirmed acute lower-extremity DVT from January 2018 to December 2025. The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days. Three nested ridge-penalized logistic models included clinical predictors (Model 1), clinical plus laboratory predictors (Model 2), and clinical, laboratory, and ultrasound predictors (Model 3). Missing data were multiply imputed, and the complete modeling procedure was internally validated with 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Discrimination, calibration, Brier score, incremental performance, and decision-curve net benefit were assessed.ResultsThe primary outcome occurred in 102 patients (13.0%): 82 had DVT progression and 27 symptomatic PE, with seven having both. Optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.702, 0.766, and 0.808 (95% CI, 0.769-0.847) for Models 1-3, respectively. For Model 3, the optimism-corrected calibration slope was 0.94 and Brier score 0.087. Optimism-corrected ΔAUCs were 0.064 and 0.042, with corresponding ΔBrier scores of -0.009 and -0.008. Model 3 showed the highest optimism-corrected net benefit across thresholds of approximately 8%-25%. Observed outcome proportions across risk tertiles were 3.1%, 9.6%, and 26.3%.ConclusionsModel 3 provided internally validated prediction of clinically detected VTE deterioration under local treatment and imaging practices. External validation and prospective clinical-impact assessment are required before routine use.

The primary outcome was clinically detected and objectively confirmed ipsilateral DVT progression or new-onset symptomatic pulmonary embolism (PE) within 30 days.

title: A Two-Step Risk Stratification Model for Venous Thromboembolism Combining Caprini Score and D-Dimer in Trauma Patients Undergoing Surgery.
abstract: ObjectiveTo determine whether adding D-dimer to Caprini score-based risk assessment can further refine venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk stratification in trauma patients, particularly among those already classified as high-risk.MethodsA retrospective cohort of 206 trauma surgical patients who underwent surgical intervention was analyzed. Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort. This threshold was not externally validated. All patients received mechanical VTE prophylaxis, while patients with Caprini scores ≥9 received prophylactic-dose low-molecular-weight heparin. Bilateral lower-extremity Doppler ultrasound was performed within 24 hours of admission, with subsequent surveillance according to predefined risk criteria.ResultsOverall composite VTE incidence was 31.1%. The Caprini score showed an AUC of 0.640 for VTE discrimination. D-dimer showed the highest discrimination in the full cohort (AUC = 0.669), which decreased to 0.614 within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (≥9 points, n = 118). Applying a study-derived exploratory D-dimer threshold of ≥5.5 mg/L identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence (44.8% vs. 16.1%; RR = 2.78, 95% CI: 1.21-6.37, P = 0.005). However, after adjustment for age, sex, and ISS, the association was attenuated and did not remain statistically significant (adjusted OR = 2.418, 95% CI: 0.660-8.864, P = 0.183).ConclusionsRelying solely on clinical risk scoring provides limited VTE discrimination in trauma patients. A sequential two-step strategy identified a subgroup with a higher observed VTE incidence within the Caprini high-risk category, although an independent association between the D-dimer threshold and VTE was not demonstrated after adjustment. This approach warrants prospective validation in larger cohorts.

Caprini scores and baseline plasma D-dimer levels were assessed against VTE occurrence using ROC curves. The two-step strategy consisted of initial Caprini-based stratification, followed by secondary D-dimer re-stratification using a study-derived exploratory threshold derived from the Youden index within the Caprini high-risk subgroup (Caprini score ≥9) in the same cohort.

title: The use of side-firing intravascular ultrasound for TIPS procedures: a case series.
abstract: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation is a well-established technique for managing complications of portal hypertension. Standard portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation is fluoroscopy-guided and relies on anatomical landmarks. However, the absence of direct visualization of the portal vein can lead to complications, including misdirected punctures or damage to adjacent structures. In this context, intracardiac echocardiography has emerged as a promising tool to guide portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation, as it provides good tissue penetration and high-resolution ultrasound imaging. We present our experience using intracardiac echocardiography as a guidance method for portal vein puncture during transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation. We report on 3 cases of patients undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt with an intracardiac echocardiography catheter. The fluoroscopy time was recorded in two cases (38 and 47 minutes), and the contrast volume ranged from 150 to 215ml (mean 173 ml). We describe the challenges encountered and highlight the role of intracardiac echocardiography as a valuable adjunct to conventional techniques.

title: Postpartum Retroperitoneal Haematoma Associated With Suspected Ovarian Artery Pathology Following Spontaneous Vaginal Delivery: A Case Report.
abstract: Postpartum retroperitoneal haemorrhage is rare and can be challenging to recognise because substantial blood loss may remain concealed. A 22-year-old multiparous woman presented three days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery with syncope, severe right-sided abdominal and back pain, vomiting, and haemodynamic instability. Pelvic ultrasonography did not adequately explain the severity of her clinical presentation. Computed tomography revealed a large right-sided retroperitoneal haematoma associated with suspected ovarian artery pathology. She underwent successful endovascular coil embolization and received a blood transfusion. Her recovery was complicated by fever and a marked inflammatory response, necessitating prolonged antimicrobial treatment and close outpatient follow-up. This case highlights the importance of considering concealed extrauterine haemorrhage when postpartum symptoms are disproportionate to visible blood loss or initial ultrasonographic findings.

Pelvic ultrasonography did not adequately explain the severity of her clinical presentation.

title: Heat-Based Therapies in Hypertension Management: A Systematic Review of Physiological Mechanisms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.

RESULTS: Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.

CONCLUSION: Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential. METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous.
