title: Recurrent Multi-territory Thromboembolism As the Initial Presentation of Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma and Suspected Nonbacterial Thrombotic Endocarditis.
abstract: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis (NBTE), also known as Marantic endocarditis, is an uncommon complication of malignancy that may cause systemic embolization. We report a 74-year-old woman who developed a right gastrocnemius deep vein thrombosis followed by recurrent right middle cerebral artery occlusions requiring two mechanical thrombectomies. Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia. Repeat echocardiography demonstrated mitral valve vegetations, initially raising concern for infective endocarditis. However, repeated blood cultures and cultures of retrieved thrombotic material were negative. Imaging revealed widespread metastatic disease, and biopsy of a left supraclavicular lymph node confirmed metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The combination of recurrent arterial and venous thrombosis, advanced malignancy, and negative microbiological investigations favored a clinical diagnosis of NBTE. This case illustrates how extensive thromboembolic disease may precede the diagnosis of pancreatic cancer and highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by valvular vegetations in this setting.

Her subsequent course was complicated by further deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and acute limb ischemia.

title: Severe gastric distension in a teenage boy.
abstract: A 16-year-old male presented with acute abdominal pain, nausea, and distension and was found to have severe gastric dilation on imaging. Antroduodenal manometry showed erythromycin-induced phase 3 migrating motor complex beginning in the antrum but post-prandial antral hypoactivity. Mitochondrial DNA sequencing was normal. Exome analysis revealed a rare variant of uncertain significance in the smooth muscle myosin heavy chain 11 (MYH11) gene (NM_002474.3: c.4123G>A, p.Asp1375Asn), which is necessary for smooth muscle contraction. Pathogenic MYH11 alterations cause multiple disorders, including autosomal dominant (AD) familial thoracic aortic aneurysm, AD visceral myopathy, and autosomal recessive megacystis-microcolon-intestinal-hypoperistalsis syndrome. Amino acid p.Asp1375 is within the rod region of the MYH11 protein that self-assembles to form thick filaments; thus, pathogenic variants in this region may affect filament formation and impair interactions with thin filaments. While the phenotype overlap is compelling, further research is needed to determine the clinical significance of this alteration.

title: Broadening the Indications for the SPING Block in Palliative Care: A Case Discussion.
abstract: The Spinal Phenol IN Glycerol (SPING) block is an intrathecal neurolytic technique developed to provide sustained unilateral analgesia in frail patients with nonoperative hip fractures. Its potential role in other palliative care populations remains unexplored. Two cases are described with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain: a 76-year-old male with metastatic esophageal cancer and acetabular metastasis, and an 86-year-old female with advanced dementia and critical limb ischemia. In both cases, systemic opioids failed and were associated with significant adverse effects. Both patients experienced rapid and clinically assessed sustained pain relief, reduced opioid requirements, and improved comfort until death. These two case reports suggest that SPING may provide effective palliative analgesia with opioid reduction in patients with refractory unilateral lower-limb pain caused by metastatic bone disease and critical limb ischemia. These findings support consideration of SPING as a proportionate palliative intervention beyond its current use for hip fractures when comfort is the primary goal.

title: Serglycin regulates macrophage differentiation and is associated with human atherosclerotic plaque stability.
abstract: Inflammation contributes to the destabilization of atherosclerotic plaques and increases the risk of cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke. Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. Serglycin (SRGN), is a proteoglycan primarily expressed by immune cells that regulates inflammation, but its role in human atherosclerotic plaques remains unclear. SRGN protein levels were quantified by ELISA in carotid endarterectomy samples from patients in the Atherosclerotic Plaque Imaging Project and compared between symptomatic and asymptomatic plaques. SRGN spatial localization was evaluated by multispectral imaging and histology. Glycosylation patterns were examined by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. Functional effects were investigated using CRISPR-mediated SRGN knockout in THP-1 monocytes differentiated into macrophages and exposed to oxidized low-density lipoprotein (oxLDL). SRGN levels were higher in plaques from asymptomatic patients compared with plaques from symptomatic patients and localized primarily to macrophage- and lipid-rich regions. Plaque SRGN was positively associated with histological markers of plaque stability, displayed heterogeneous molecular forms and showed an inverse association with the plaque vulnerability index. In vitro, SRGN deficiency was associated with a more pro-inflammatory macrophage profile, impaired M2-like polarization, and increased lipid retention following oxLDL exposure. These findings indicate that SRGN is associated with inflammatory cell presence, lipid accumulation, and features of plaque stability in human plaques, and suggest a role for SRGN in macrophage differentiation and lipid handling in atherosclerotic lesions.

Extracellular matrix components modulate inflammation and immune responses within the plaque microenvironment. title: Global landscape and evolution of limb-salvage reconstruction with prostheses for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours: A bibliometric analysis.
abstract: PurposeTo delineate the evolution, collaborative structure, clinically relevant themes, and emerging priorities of limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from 1 January 1995 to 31 October 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on 31 October 2025. Co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses were conducted using CiteSpace 6.4.1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20.ResultsOf 2,606 retrieved records, 2,283 underwent title and abstract screening and 997 were included. Publication output increased, peaking at 84 in 2023. The United States led publication output and cumulative citations, while China ranked second by output. Keyword analyses indicated that research attention expanded from surgical strategy selection for specific tumour types and anatomical sites to include long-term prosthetic survival, complications and functional outcomes. Recent research themes included technologies such as 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and finite element analysis, with "3d printing" showing the strongest keyword burst (strength 9.49; 2021-2025). Research output was concentrated in a small number of centres and journals. Frequently co-cited publications provided standardised methods for assessing limb function and classifying endoprosthetic failure.ConclusionsLong-term prosthetic survival, complications, function and quality of life remain central themes in limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction. Technologies supporting individualised reconstruction, including 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and emerging robot-assisted techniques, are attracting increasing research interest. Future multicentre comparative studies should use standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up to evaluate prosthesis design, fixation and selection, as well as strategies for preventing and managing reconstructive failure.

title: Selective coil embolization of hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm causing hemobilia secondary to hemorrhagic hepatic hydatid cyst: A case report.
abstract: Hemobilia secondary to intrabiliary rupture of a hepatic hydatid cyst is rare, and concomitant arterial pseudoaneurysm formation further increases the risk of life-threatening hemorrhage. Case: An 80-year-old woman presented with 3 months of melena, progressing to large-volume melena and hematemesis. She was hypotensive and severely anemic (hemoglobin 6.0 g/dL). Upper endoscopy revealed a clot at the sphincter of Oddi, consistent with hemobilia. Multiphase CT showed a right-lobe hydatid cyst with active intracystic arterial extravasation and communication with the biliary ducts, with additional right-lobe hydatid cysts. Angiography identified a pseudoaneurysm arising from a segment V branch of the right hepatic artery. Given the patient's advanced age, hemodynamic instability, and high surgical risk, emergent selective endovascular embolization-rather than surgery-was chosen as first-line treatment, and superselective coil embolization achieved hemostasis. Post-procedure, hemoglobin improved to 10.6 g/dL by day 4; follow-up CT at day 4 demonstrated resolution of the pseudoaneurysm without rebleeding. Albendazole therapy was initiated after embolization. Echinococcus serology was not available, and reported follow-up was limited to 4 days; these are acknowledged as limitations. Conclusion: In elderly or hemodynamically unstable patients with hemorrhagic hydatid cyst and hemobilia, selective endovascular embolization can provide rapid, organ-preserving control of bleeding and a bridge to definitive antiparasitic management, although longer-term data are needed.

title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net (2D and 3D), and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet (2D and 3D). We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

title: Association of autoimmune diseases and transient risk factors with clinical outcomes in patients with venous thromboembolism: COMMAND VTE registry insights.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transient provoking factors are generally associated with a lower risk of recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE). Whether this association also applies to patients with autoimmune diseases, which constitute persistent risk factors, remains uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 6022 patients with acute symptomatic VTE without active cancer from the retrospective, multicenter COMMAND VTE Registries, including 734 with and 5288 without autoimmune diseases. Within each subgroup, clinical outcomes were compared across major, minor, and no transient provoking factor categories, using the no transient factor category as the reference.

RESULTS: Compared with patients without autoimmune diseases, those with autoimmune diseases had higher risks of recurrent VTE [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.73; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.31-2.28] and major bleeding (adjusted HR 1.45; 95% CI 1.14-1.83). In analyses stratified by autoimmune disease status, major transient provoking factors, compared with no transient provoking factors, were associated with a lower risk of recurrent VTE among patients without autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.30; 95% CI 0.19-0.48). This association was less clear among patients with autoimmune diseases (adjusted HR 0.92; 95% CI 0.36-2.35). A similar pattern was observed in the landmark analysis after anticoagulation discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: The association between transient provoking factors and a lower recurrence risk was less clear in patients with autoimmune diseases. These findings suggest that transient provoking factor status alone may provide limited guidance for recurrence risk assessment in this population, although imprecise estimates preclude firm conclusions.

Whether this association also applies to patients with autoimmune diseases, which constitute persistent risk factors, remains uncertain. title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetic Foot Disease: A Narrative Review of Mechanisms, Perfusion Assessment, and Implications for Pre-Revascularization Evaluation.
abstract: Diabetic foot disease is a major cause of ulceration, infection, lower-extremity amputation, and premature mortality. Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes. Its implications for interpreting perfusion tests, assessing prognosis, and evaluating patients before revascularization remain insufficiently integrated in the existing literature. This narrative review examines MAC as a distal arterial phenotype with diagnostic and prognostic relevance in diabetic foot disease. Targeted PubMed searches updated on 22 September 2026, supplemented by reference checking and topic-specific searches, informed a qualitative synthesis of clinical, imaging, and mechanistic studies. The review distinguishes medial from intimal calcification and evaluates recognition, scoring, and renal, metabolic, and neurovascular mechanisms. Observational cohorts of diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) and chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) link higher calcification burden with delayed healing, amputation, incomplete haemodynamic improvement, and selected systemic outcomes, although adjustment and endpoint definitions vary. In the MAC-prone diabetic foot, reliance on the ankle-brachial index alone may be misleading because calcified tibial and pedal arteries can produce falsely normal or elevated ankle pressures. Toe pressure, toe-brachial index (TBI), transcutaneous oxygen tension (TcPO2), skin perfusion pressure (SPP), anatomical imaging, and careful wound trajectory assessment should therefore be integrated with established limb-threat and anatomical classifications. Emerging evidence suggests that MAC scoring may complement Wound, Ischaemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) staging, Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) assessment, and small artery disease scoring in estimating wound-healing probability and amputation risk before revascularization. MAC scoring remains an adjunctive risk marker rather than a validated determinant of revascularization modality or a proven therapeutic target. Prospective studies should determine whether adding MAC assessment to established clinical models improves management and patient outcomes.

Medial arterial calcification (MAC), characterised by calcium-phosphate deposition within the arterial media, is associated with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and neuropathy. It complicates perfusion assessment and is associated with adverse limb outcomes.

title: Ascending Aorta Dilation in the Fontan: To Intervene or Not.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation.

CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation.

WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

DISCUSSION: There are case reports of aortic dissection, but true risk remains unknown. Weighing the risks of surgery versus conservative management in patients with single ventricle physiology is challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Surgical intervention on dilated aortas in patients with single ventricle physiology is perilous but possible in the correct circumstances.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Ascending aorta dilation is a known finding in the congenital heart disease population and specifically in patients who have undergone single ventricle palliation. CASE SUMMARY: We present 3 patients with single ventricle physiology who underwent single ventricle palliations and had severe ascending aorta dilation. WHY BEYOND THE GUIDELINES: Guidelines for the management of these patients are lacking, and decisions are made on a case-by-case basis.

title: Comparative evaluation of handheld vs. high-end ultrasound systems for TIPSS hemodynamic assessment: first impressions.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPSS) procedures require reliable post-interventional hemodynamic monitoring to detect shunt dysfunction, for which Doppler ultrasonography is the preferred modality. Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed. Blood flow measurements were obtained and compared using a high-end ultrasound system (Resona R9, Mindray) and modern handheld ultrasound device (Vscan Air™ CL, GE). The TIPSS was evaluated using B-mode and color Doppler sonography. Image quality was assessed using a 5-point scale and flow parameters using statistical analysis. The image quality and the difference between the two devices were analyzed using correlation coefficients and multivariable linear regression models including TIPSS flow values, skin-to-TIPSS distance, and TIPSS dwell time.

RESULTS: Both devices produced clinically interpretable images. However, the high-end device yielded superior image quality in 16 of 23 cases (p < 0.001). Significant correlations were observed between the difference in mean TIPSS flow measurements obtained by the two devices (Δ mean TIPSS flow) and corresponding average flow values measured by the two devices (Kendall's τ = 0.656; p < 0.001). Significant associations with Δ TIPSS mean flow were identified for skin-to-TIPSS distance (τ = 0.39; p = 0.014) and TIPSS dwell time (τ = -0.39; p = 0.017). In multivariable analysis, both mean TIPSS flow measured by the high-end system and skin-to-TIPSS distance remained significantly associated with Δ TIPSS mean flow. The TIPSS mean flow measured by the high-end system correlated with TIPSS dwell time (τ = 0.38; p = 0.021). Bland-Altman analysis revealed that handheld measurements tended to overestimate low flows and underestimate high flows.

CONCLUSION: Handheld ultrasound devices show promising potential for TIPSS surveillance; however, they could lead to distorted flow deviations. Contemporary handheld devices may nevertheless be useful in selected point-of-care settings but cannot yet replace high-end systems for precise hemodynamic monitoring. Larger prospective studies are required.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: No clinical trial registration was performed, as this study is a single-center retrospective observational analysis based on existing clinical data. The study did not involve prospective patient enrollment, international procedures, or assignment to treatment groups. Therefore, registration in a clinical trial registry was not applicable.

Owing to the rapid development of handheld ultrasound devices, their diagnostic equivalence to high-end systems warrants investigation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A pilot group of 23 patients (n = 13 males, 65%; n = 7 females; 35%; n = 3 unknown) with intrahepatic TIPSS were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed.

CONCLUSION: In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled.

title: Cardiovascular disturbances and ward hypotension after major vascular surgery: a single-centre prospective cohort study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery.

METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery. We conducted point-of-care ultrasound and sidestream darkfield microscopy imaging to detect vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. The primary outcome was hypotension (systolic blood pressure < 90 mm Hg or a vasopressor infusion) within 24 hr of surgery.

RESULTS: We recruited 100 patients, of whom 89 had data available for analysis. Hypotension occurred in 20 participants (23%), vasodilation in 30 (34%), and myocardial dysfunction in 11 (12%). Severe hypovolemia and obstruction were not observed. The adjusted marginal risk difference of hypotension was 33% (95% confidence interval [CI], 14% to 53%; P < 0.001) for vasodilation and 41% (95% CI, 3% to 79%; P = 0.03) for myocardial dysfunction. Vasodilation increased the risk of intensive care unit admission by 27% (95% CI, 8% to 45%; P = 0.006) and of requiring a vasopressor infusion by 22% (95% CI, 4% to 39%; P = 0.02).

CONCLUSIONS: Vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction increased the risk of postoperative hypotension, providing insight into the mechanistic development of postoperative hypotension. The absence of severe hypovolemia was surprising. Clinicians should assess for vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction as potential preludes to postoperative hypotension, potentially using point-of-care echocardiography and sidestream darkfield microscopy.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Postoperative hypotension can be caused by vasodilation, myocardial dysfunction, severe hypovolemia, and obstruction. We sought to estimate the effects of these causes on the incidence of hypotension after major vascular surgery. METHODS: We conducted a single-centre prospective cohort study of male and female adult patients undergoing major vascular surgery.

title: Indirect versus combined bypass for perfusion-defined high-risk adult moyamoya disease: a propensity score overlap-weighted analysis of revascularization and postoperative stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024. The cohort wasrestricted to hemispheres with a preoperative tissue volume of at least 59.5 mL showing time-to-maximum (Tmax) >6 seconds (6s). Revascularization was assessed by 6-month angiography using the Matsushima grading system, and perfusion improvement was evaluated using postoperative CT perfusion. Baseline imbalance was addressed using overlap-weighted propensity score analysis. Factors associated with postoperative stroke were evaluated using overlap-weighted logistic regression, with sensitivity analyses using patient-clustered robust standard errors and Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 124 hemispheres were analyzed (CB, 88; IB, 36). Before weighting, PCA involvement was more frequent in the IB group (86.1% vs. 61.4%; standardized mean difference = 0.586), but all prespecified covariates were balanced after overlap weighting. Good revascularization was comparable between CB and IB before weighting (93.2% vs. 94.4%, p = 1.000) and after overlap weighting (90.6% vs. 98.1%, p = 0.102). Postoperative perfusion outcomes were also similar. Postoperative stroke occurred less frequently after IB both before weighting (5.6% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.021) and after overlap weighting (5.2% vs. 34.6%, p < 0.001). In the overlap-weighted multivariable model, IB was associated with lower odds of postoperative stroke, whereas larger preoperative Tmax>6s volume was associated with higher odds. These findings remained significant after adjustment for intra-patient correlation and were directionally consistent in Firth analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort, IB achieved angiographic and perfusion outcomes comparable to CB, with a lower observed postoperative stroke. IB may be a reasonable risk-adapted option for selected high-risk hemispheres, although non-randomized treatment allocation warrants cautious interpretation.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024.

title: Accuracy and Concordance of Agitated Saline Bubble-Enhanced Ultrasound versus Chest Radiography by Internal Jugular Insertion Site.
abstract: Non-tunneled hemodialysis catheters (HDCs) are commonly used to initiate renal replacement therapy in hospitalized patients, especially those with acute kidney injury. HDC malposition is associated with delayed therapy and inadequate dialysis. Agitated saline bubble-enhanced ultrasound (SBUS) has emerged as a method for visualizing catheter position at the time of insertion. This study aimed to analyze the accuracy and concordance of SBUS and chest radiography (CXR) for assessing HDC positioning according to the internal jugular vein (IJV) insertion site. A total of 152 hospitalized patients undergoing IJV catheter insertion were assessed from December 2019 to May 2021. Time from puncture to CXR result, procedure-related complications, blood flow during dialysis, and the accuracy and concordance of SBUS compared with CXR for determining HDC position adequacy were evaluated. The median time between catheter insertion and CXR was 191 min [interquartile range (IQR), 93-288 min], with no difference between insertion sites. The main complication after catheter insertion was arterial puncture (2% overall), with a similar incidence at both sites. Inadequate catheter blood flow was more frequent with left IJV insertion than with right IJV insertion. For right IJV catheters, concordance between SBUS and CXR was high (Gwet's AC1 = 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.915-0.992), with an accuracy of 95.6%. For left IJV catheters, concordance was low (Gwet's AC1 = 0.37; 95% CI, -0.21-0.94), with an accuracy of 64.3%. Compared with CXR, SBUS was suitable for assessing catheter placement following right IJV insertion but may be less suitable following left IJV insertion.

title: Association of an Intensive Multimodal Perioperative Management Bundle With Short-Term Recovery After Surgery for Trimalleolar Fractures: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study. Patients were classified retrospectively according to contemporaneous medical and nursing records: 43 patients who received routine management were assigned to a routine-management group, and 41 who received the intensive bundle were assigned to an intensive-pathway group. The investigators did not prospectively enroll patients, assign pathways, deliver study-specific interventions, or collect research-specific data. Primary outcomes were the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) Ankle-Hindfoot Scale and Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores; secondary outcomes included first out-of-bed mobilization, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, patient satisfaction, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). Unadjusted mean differences or odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated, and longitudinal AOFAS and VAS data were analyzed using mixed-design repeated-measures analysis of variance (RM-ANOVA). Because the components were delivered together, no component-specific effect was estimated.

RESULTS: No baseline variable differed significantly between groups, although the absence of statistical significance did not establish covariate balance. In unadjusted analyses, receipt of the intensive bundle was associated with earlier first out-of-bed mobilization (mean difference [MD], -22.80 h; 95% confidence interval [CI], -26.48 to -19.12), shorter hospitalization (MD, -3.30 days; 95% CI, -4.14 to -2.46), lower hospitalization costs (MD, -13,114 CNY (1 USD = 7.1429 CNY); 95% CI, -14,979 to -11,249), and higher patient satisfaction (OR, 5.16; 95% CI, 1.04-25.56). VAS scores were lower in the intensive-pathway group at 1 week (3.9 ± 0.9 vs. 4.8 ± 1.0), 1 month (1.3 ± 0.7 vs. 3.2 ± 1.0), and 3 months (1.0 (0.0, 1.0) vs. 2.0 (1.0, 2.0)) postoperatively (all Bonferroni-adjusted p < 0.001); RM-ANOVA showed significant group, time, and group-by-time interaction effects for both AOFAS and VAS scores. DVT occurred in 3/41 (7.3%) patients in the intensive-pathway group and 8/43 (18.6%) in the routine-management group, and the difference was not statistically significant (OR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.08-1.41). These findings represent associations with the integrated bundle and cannot be attributed independently to preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, analgesia, mobilization, or follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle was associated with earlier mobilization, shorter hospitalization, lower hospitalization costs, and more favorable short-term functional and pain trajectories. Because the bundle contained multiple simultaneously delivered components, the study cannot determine the independent efficacy of preoperative optimization, ankle-pump exercise, or any other individual measure. In addition, pathway allocation was non-random and the estimates were unadjusted; therefore, the findings should be interpreted as associations rather than definitive causal effects.
englishSummary: AIM: To examine the association between receipt of an intensive multimodal perioperative management bundle and short-term functional recovery, pain, and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for trimalleolar fractures. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 84 patients who underwent open reduction and internal fixation for trimalleolar fractures between September 2023 and September 2025. The intensive management bundle was a pre-existing standardized routine-care pathway rather than a research intervention developed for this study.

title: Perioperative Impact of Incidental Durotomy in Elderly Patients Undergoing Elective Spine Surgery: A Multicenter European Cohort Study.
abstract:
AIM: Incidental durotomy is among the most frequent intraoperative complications in spine surgery, yet elderly patients may be especially vulnerable to its downstream consequences because of frailty, multimorbidity, delayed mobilization, and postoperative neurocognitive complications. The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers. Consecutive patients aged 65 years or older who underwent elective spine surgery between 2019 and 2024 were reviewed. Patients with incidental durotomy during the index procedure were compared with those without durotomy. Outcomes of interest included length of stay, thromboembolic events, postoperative infection, delirium, readmission, revision surgery, postoperative intensive care use, and discharge disposition.

RESULTS: Among 723 included patients, 107 (14.8%) sustained an incidental durotomy. Operative time was longer in the durotomy cohort (median 178 vs 138 minutes; p < 0.001), as were length of stay (8 vs 5 days; p < 0.001), thromboembolic events (6.5% vs 1.8%; p = 0.010), and postoperative delirium (14.0% vs 5.2%; p = 0.001). In descriptive analyses of patients older than 75 years, median length of stay was 10 vs 6 days, delirium occurred in 17.7% vs 7.4%, and thromboembolic events occurred in 8.1% vs 2.2%. Postoperative infection, 30-day readmission, revision surgery, intensive care use, and discharge disposition were not significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: In elderly patients undergoing elective spine surgery, incidental durotomy was associated mainly with increased perioperative morbidity rather than clearly worse short-term post-discharge outcomes. The signals for prolonged stay, delirium, and thromboembolic complications-especially in patients older than 75 years-support age-sensitive perioperative pathways emphasizing meticulous repair, early mobilization when clinically appropriate, delirium prevention, and close medical surveillance.

The literature suggests that durotomy is associated with increased perioperative resource utilization, whereas long-term functional outcomes are not well reported. METHODS: We performed a retrospective multicenter cohort study across five European academic neurosurgical centers.

title: Nursing-Related Risk Characteristics and Identification of High-Risk Patients With In-Hospital Lower-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis After Lower-Limb Fracture Surgery: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract:
AIM: Lower-limb fractures already contribute ≥5 Caprini points for venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk, limiting the ability of the conventional >5 cutoff to discriminate individual risk within this population. We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024. Of 783 patients screened, 71 were excluded, leaving 712 in the source cohort (61 DVT cases and 651 ultrasound-negative, matchable controls). Cases and controls were matched 1:3 without replacement by age (±5 years), sex, and fracture site, yielding 61 matched sets (244 patients). After matching, non-matching variables were singly imputed using a random forest algorithm for the primary analysis. To assess uncertainty associated with this approach, a separate sensitivity analysis generated 20 completed datasets from the pre-imputation matched records using a stochastic chained-equation multiple-imputation procedure. Regression estimates across the 20 datasets were combined using Rubin's rules. Associations were estimated using conditional logistic regression stratified by matched set and reported as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Incremental within-set concordance was corrected using 2000 cluster bootstrap resamples. The primary analysis, complete-case analyses and multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis were conducted separately.

RESULTS: Matching variables were well balanced after matching, with standardized mean differences (SMD) of 0.02 for age and 0 for sex and fracture site, although several non-matching characteristics remained imbalanced. Three factors were positively associated with in-hospital DVT: admission Caprini ≥9 (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.28-4.61), severe POD1 activity dependence (OR 3.89, 95% CI 1.38-10.94), and preoperative immobilization ≥72 h (OR 2.55, 95% CI 1.14-5.67). Compared with patients without any core risk features, the OR increased to 2.81 (95% CI 1.46-5.38) among those with one feature and to 6.28 (95% CI 1.57-25.03) among those with two features. Adding severe POD1 activity dependence to Caprini ≥9 was associated with a modest increase in corrected within-set concordance from 0.589 to 0.633, corresponding to a difference of 0.044 (bootstrap SE 0.022, 95% CI 0.003-0.088). Sensitivity analyses generally preserved the direction of the main associations, although the Caprini estimate was attenuated after additional adjustment for trauma-related variables and D-dimer.

CONCLUSIONS: Admission Caprini ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h, and severe POD1 activity dependence were each associated with in-hospital lower-extremity DVT. POD1 activity assessment was associated with a modest improvement in within-set risk ranking beyond Caprini stratification. This finding should not be interpreted as evidence of established clinical utility or improved patient outcomes; however, it may help guide nursing attention toward prophylaxis delivery, activity support, and symptom surveillance. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine its clinical relevance.

We evaluated whether an admission Caprini score ≥9, preoperative immobilization ≥72 h and severe postoperative day 1 (POD1) activity dependence are associated with in-hospital lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and whether POD1 activity provides additional within-group risk stratification beyond Caprini scoring. METHODS: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, 1:3 matched case-control study of adults undergoing surgery for lower-limb fractures at Ganzhou Hospital-Nanfang Hospital, Southern Medical University between January 2022 and July 2024.

title: AI Applications in Aortic and Peripheral Artery Disease: Risk Prediction, Imaging, Procedural Support, and Longitudinal Surveillance.
abstract: Aortic disease and lower-extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) generate substantial morbidity, mortality, and longitudinal imaging burden. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly studied for vascular risk prediction, image analysis, procedural support, and surveillance, but the maturity of these applications is heterogeneous. This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit. Automated image segmentation and opportunistic abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) detection have the most mature evidence base, including retrospective external validation and, for AI-assisted AAA case finding, nonrandomized evidence of improved downstream evaluation and follow-up. Conversely, while machine-learning models for vascular risk prediction and disease progression often report high retrospective accuracy, their clinical readiness remains strictly investigational. Across most aortic and PAD applications, there is a persistent lack of independent external validation, decision-curve analysis, and prospective testing against standard care. Image-fusion guidance has clinical evidence for reducing procedural resource use, but this evidence should not be conflated with autonomous AI or robotic navigation. Cardiovascular digital twins remain largely mechanistic, computational, or early-development frameworks. AI can augment vascular imaging and risk assessment, but high retrospective accuracy is not equivalent to clinical utility. Current guideline thresholds for repair, revascularization, and surveillance should not be altered on the basis of investigational radiomics or prediction models. Translation requires multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration and net-benefit assessment, transparent reporting, and trials demonstrating improved patient outcomes.

This review evaluates recent AI applications in aortic disease and PAD, emphasizing the distinction between algorithmic performance, external validation, demonstrated workflow impact, and proven patient benefit.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIM: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

METHODS: Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences.

RESULTS: Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.

METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point.

CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents.

title: Non-invasive assessment of postoperative revascularization using slab MIP images in 3D TOF MRA in pediatric moyamoya disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Repeated assessment of postoperative revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease is clinically important, but digital subtraction angiography (DSA) is invasive. We aimed to develop a novel, non-invasive scoring method (moya-ASPECTS) that applies the six cortical MCA regions of ASPECTS to slab maximum intensity projection (MIP) images from three-dimensional time-of-flight (3D TOF) magnetic resonance angiography (MRA), and to examine its correlation with DSA findings and cerebral blood flow (CBF) changes after surgery.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023. Eight hemispheres underwent indirect revascularization alone and 37 underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization. We evaluated postoperative cortical revascularization using the moya-ASPECTS score based on slab MIP images derived from 3D TOF MRA, and examined its associations with Matsushima grade, resting cerebral blood flow (CBF), cerebrovascular reserve (CVR), and regression of basal moyamoya vessels.

RESULTS: The moya-ASPECTS score showed a strong correlation with Matsushima grade (p < 0.001). Postoperative resting CBF increased by 2.27 ml/100 g/min for each point increase in moya-ASPECTS (95% CI 0.87-3.67, p = 0.003). While moya-ASPECTS was not associated with CVR change, it correlated significantly with regression of moyamoya vessels (RR 1.33, 95% CI 1.12-1.58, p < 0.001). Higher moya-ASPECTS scores were inversely associated with postoperative asymptomatic infarction, although the number of events was small.

CONCLUSION: The moya-ASPECTS score derived from slab MIP images provides a non-invasive, repeatable, and semi-quantitative method for evaluating postoperative cortical revascularization in pediatric moyamoya disease. This method correlates well with DSA-based Matsushima grade and postoperative CBF improvement, supporting its potential use as a practical non-invasive adjunct for serial outpatient follow-up.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 45 treated hemispheres in 28 pediatric patients who underwent revascularization between 2010 and 2023.

title: CTA-defined calcified nodules as a predictor of adverse outcomes following carotid revascularization.
abstract: Carotid calcification can complicate carotid artery stenting (CAS), but the clinical impact may depend on calcification morphology rather than calcification burden alone. We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis. The endpoint occurred in 4 of 83 patients (4.8%) in Groups 1/2 and in 5 of 9 patients (55.6%) in Group 3 (unadjusted OR, 24.69; 95% CI, 4.72-129.14; p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model including treatment modality and calcification pattern, Group 3 remained associated with the composite endpoint (adjusted OR, 49.05; 95% CI, 4.82-498.94; p = 0.001), whereas CEA was associated with lower risk (adjusted OR, 0.045; 95% CI, 0.003-0.664; p = 0.024). Among patients undergoing CAS, the endpoint occurred in 3 of 38 patients (7.9%) in Groups 1/2 and all 5 patients (100%) in Group 3 (p < 0.001). A CTA-defined CN pattern may identify lesions at particularly high risk for CAS-related technical failure or restenosis and may support consideration of CEA when surgically feasible.

We retrospectively evaluated 92 patients who underwent carotid revascularization with either carotid endarterectomy (CEA) or CAS and classified preoperative CTA findings as no/spotty calcification (Group 1), outer calcification (Group 2), or a calcified nodule (CN) pattern directly abutting the contrast-enhanced lumen (Group 3). The primary composite endpoint comprised procedural failure, ischemic complications, or restenosis.

title: Continuation of Clopidogrel in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Perioperative Bleeding and Cardiovascular Outcomes in a Consecutive Case Series.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Perioperative clopidogrel management in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is challenging because interruption may increase thrombotic risk, whereas continuation may increase bleeding. Evidence remains limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients (35 knees) undergoing primary TKA while continuing clopidogrel 75 mg daily (April 2018-September 2019). A multidisciplinary team involving orthopaedic surgery, cardiology, and anesthesiology determined continuation. One senior surgeon performed all procedures using a tourniquet-free technique with intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid. All patients also received low-dose aspirin for at least 2 weeks postoperatively as venous thromboembolism prophylaxis. Outcomes through 90 days included bleeding, transfusion, wound complications, infection, major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events, symptomatic venous thromboembolism, and anesthesia-related complications.

RESULTS: Mean age was 69 ± 6.4 years; mean estimated blood loss was 285 ± 95 mL, and mean hemoglobin decrease was 1.8 ± 0.6 g/dL. No transfusions or major bleeding occurred. Minor wound drainage followed 3 procedures (8.6%), and superficial cellulitis occurred in 1 knee (2.9%); no deep infections occurred. Four patients (12.9%) reported mild, nonspecific headaches; none met criteria for post-dural puncture headache. No clinical signs or symptoms suggestive of spinal hematoma or persistent neurologic deficit, and no myocardial infarction, stroke, or cardiovascular death, were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Clopidogrel continuation during primary TKA may be feasible in carefully selected patients receiving multidisciplinary assessment and multimodal blood management. The small sample, retrospective design, and absence of a control group preclude conclusions about comparative safety.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Perioperative clopidogrel management in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) is challenging because interruption may increase thrombotic risk, whereas continuation may increase bleeding. Evidence remains limited. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 31 consecutive patients (35 knees) undergoing primary TKA while continuing clopidogrel 75 mg daily (April 2018-September 2019).

title: Spontaneous rupture of an intrasplenic arterial aneurysm presenting as an acute abdomen: CT diagnosis and surgical management.
abstract: Aneurysms of the intrasplenic arterial branches are exceptionally rare. Rupture without trauma, and without the pancreatic disease behind most splenic arterial pseudoaneurysms, is rarer still, and it can be fatal. Cross-sectional imaging usually brings it to light. A 51-year-old multiparous woman with no relevant medical history presented with sudden left upper quadrant pain radiating to the left shoulder, and a positive Kehr sign. Her blood pressure was maintained and her hemoglobin normal. A heart rate of 101 beats/min, however, left open the possibility of early compensation for bleeding. Multiphasic contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT), the arterial phase acquired as a CT angiogram, showed a ruptured saccular aneurysm of 18 × 12 mm in the mid-splenic parenchyma. There was an arterial-phase contrast blush, marking active extravasation, with a heterogeneous subcapsular hematoma and a moderate hemoperitoneum. The pancreas was normal and there had been no trauma. With no endovascular treatment on site, she underwent splenectomy. Serial counts showed no fall in hemoglobin, and she was discharged on the fifth postoperative day. Histopathology found hemorrhagic change but no malignancy, vasculitis, or fibromuscular dysplasia, and no discrete aneurysmal wall. Once rupture has occurred, CT cannot reliably tell a true aneurysm from a pseudoaneurysm, so the lesion is best called one of presumed true type. Early CT found the lesion, showed how far the bleeding had gone, and allowed treatment to start without delay. The diagnosis is worth considering in acute left upper quadrant pain, even when the blood pressure is maintained and the hemoglobin normal.

title: Association of Multimodal Collateral Profiles with Outcomes After Large Core Thrombectomy.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebral collateral circulation markers in large core thrombectomy and their impact on functional outcomes have not been extensively reported. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8. A poor profile (CCC-) was defined as Tan <2 and CBVI <0.8. All others were categorized as having a mixed profile (CCC±). Multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcome, 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3. Results: 88 patients with median (interquartile range, IQR) age 65.5 (56.5-77.5) years and core volume 78 (55-116) mL were included. Forty-seven patients (53.4%) had poor collateral profiles, 31 (35.2%) were classified as CCC±, and 10 (11.4%) as CCC+. In the multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression model, CCC+ patients had higher odds of achieving a 90-day mRS of 0-3 compared with CCC- patients, though the difference was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.235-5.311, p = 0.889). No significant difference was observed between CCC± and CCC- patients (OR 0.869, 95% CI 0.293-2.577, p = 0.800). Glucose was the only factor independently associated with 90-day outcomes (OR 0.742, 95% CI 0.602-0.915, p = 0.005). Conclusions: No independent association was detected between favorable or mixed cerebral collateral circulation and 90-day mRS 0-3 after large core thrombectomy, though the study was underpowered for the CCC+ comparison. Presenting glucose may inform the likelihood of achieving independent ambulatory status at 90 days.

Methods: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8.

title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
abstract: Background: Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions. Results: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at p < 1 × 10-5 and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically, F5 rs6025 and F2 rs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set. Conclusions: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause and hormone exposure, while prospective individual-level studies remain necessary before translation into risk prediction or treatment selection.

Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants.

title: Urgent Endovascular Treatment of a Pancreatitis-Related Pseudoaneurysm Identified on Follow-Up CT.
abstract: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection. Follow-up contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a new arterial-phase enhancing focus within the WON. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirmed the pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully excluded with a covered stent placed via a right transfemoral approach. Post-procedural recovery was uneventful, and short-term follow-up CT showed persistent exclusion of the lesion.
englishSummary: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection.

title: Ruptured giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms: illustrative cases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms are rare and have a poor natural history. Compared with smaller aneurysms, giant aneurysms have a significantly higher risk of rupture, and a posterior circulation location is itself an independent predictor of rupture regardless of size. Clinical presentation and symptomatology are highly variable, often with nonspecific symptoms progressing insidiously, resulting in delays of diagnosis. There are also significant treatment challenges. The authors describe their experience in 2 cases.

OBSERVATIONS: Both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression. One patient presented with headache, gait difficulties, left face numbness, and facial droop. The other presented with left-sided trigeminal pain, sixth nerve palsy, blurry vision, and unsteady gait. Both patients developed catastrophic subarachnoid hemorrhage within days following presentation, before planned intervention, with rapid progression to death.

LESSONS: Consistent with prior reports, both patients presented with symptomatic brainstem compression, which may have reflected aneurysm growth or instability. These data, along with prior reports, emphasize the poor clinical outcomes associated with symptomatic brainstem compression due to giant vertebrobasilar aneurysms, as well as the urgent and timely need to treat them despite no prior hemorrhage. Higher clinical suspicion is warranted, and further advances in endovascular technologies are necessary to provide reliable, improved clinical outcomes. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26399.

title: Deep vein thrombosis-primed neutrophils reshape the brain microenvironment to promote brain metastasis.
abstract: Brain metastasis (BrM) is a devastating complication of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), yet how host macroenvironmental conditions influence brain metastatic susceptibility remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated the impact of deep vein thrombosis (DVT), a common complication in patients with cancer, on TNBC brain metastasis. Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer. Using two syngeneic TNBC models, we demonstrated that DVT selectively enhanced brain metastasis without significantly affecting primary tumor growth or lung metastasis. Mechanistically, DVT increased neutrophil accumulation in the brain metastatic microenvironment, and neutrophil depletion completely abrogated the metastasis-promoting effect of DVT. Single-cell RNA sequencing of CD45+ cells in peripheral blood revealed that DVT reprogrammed circulating neutrophils toward migratory and inflammatory transcriptomic profiles characterized by neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation. DVT increased CXCR2 expression on circulating neutrophils and enhanced neutrophil recruitment in brain. Moreover, DVT significantly increased circulating NETs. Collectively, our findings identify DVT as a systemic driver of TNBC brain metastasis and reveal that DVT primes circulating neutrophils toward enhanced vascular recruitment and NET formation, providing a mechanistic link between cancer-associated thrombosis and brain metastatic susceptibility.

Analysis of a large clinical cohort identified DVT as an independent risk factor for BrM in patients with metastatic breast cancer.

title: Zero-Iodinated-Contrast CO2-Guided Atherectomy for Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusions in Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) who undergo complex femoropopliteal endovascular interventions are at heightened risk of contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI). This study assessed technical feasibility, short-term creatinine-based renal outcomes, and clinical outcomes of a zero-iodinated-contrast, carbon dioxide (CO2)-guided atherectomy approach for chronic total occlusions (CTOs) of the superficial femoral artery (SFA). Materials and Methods: In this retrospective, single-center analysis, 25 non-dialysis patients with CKD underwent CO2-only angiography-guided atherectomy for SFA CTOs. Renal function, procedural characteristics, distal embolization, limb-related outcomes, and duplex ultrasound-defined patency were evaluated. Serum creatinine was measured at baseline and within 48 h after the procedure. Results: The mean age was 65.4 ± 9.8 years, and 36% of patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Baseline serum creatinine was 2.16 ± 0.44 mg/dL, and the estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) was 29.5 ± 9.1 mL/min/1.73 m2; 56% of patients had Stage 4 CKD. Technical success was achieved in all procedures. Cumulative CO2-volume data were available for 24 patients, with a mean volume of 98.8 ± 37.6 mL, and the mean procedure duration was 38.2 ± 17.2 min. Distal embolization occurred in 20% of patients (5/25), including one event requiring catheter-directed thrombolysis; all embolic events were treated endovascularly, with near-complete recanalization in the thrombolysis case. Mean serum creatinine changed by -0.016 ± 0.086 mg/dL, and no creatinine-defined AKI was observed within the available 48-h assessment. No patient required initiation of dialysis. Follow-up outcomes were available for 24 of 25 patients (96%); one patient was lost to follow-up. Over a mean follow-up period of 26 months (with incompletely reconstructed surveillance), no duplex-defined restenosis, recurrent CTO, or target lesion revascularization (TLR) was documented among patients with available follow-up imaging; this is a descriptive observation within the available follow-up and does not establish universal or long-term freedom from restenosis. Conclusions: A zero-iodinated-contrast, CO2-guided atherectomy strategy appears technically feasible for SFA CTO revascularization in patients with advanced CKD and was associated with observed short-term creatinine stability within the available 48-h assessment in this small retrospective cohort. These preliminary observations require validation in larger, prospective, controlled studies.

Materials and Methods: In this retrospective, single-center analysis, 25 non-dialysis patients with CKD underwent CO2-only angiography-guided atherectomy for SFA CTOs.

title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
abstract: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.

However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction.
