title: The Safety and Efficacy of Intravascular Lithotripsy in Treating Calcified Peripheral Arterial Disease.
abstract: Calcified peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a common health condition associated with increased morbidity and mortality. Endovascular procedures have become more common in treating these lesions, and plain balloon angioplasty (PBA) is often used for vessels with mild-to-moderate calcification. However, decreased vascular compliance in heavily calcified vessels leads to poorer outcomes and higher complication risk. Intravascular shockwave lithotripsy is a more novel endovascular management option. It uses a specially designed balloon catheter to create shockwaves in an attempt to modify and increase compliance of the calcified plaque. This review aims to assess the safety profile and efficacy of intravascular lithotripsy (IVL). The currently available literature shows that use of IVL for calcified PAD has a good safety profile and low complication rate. Intravascular lithotripsy has also been shown to be more effective in treating patients with calcified PAD as compared to PBA alone. Whilst short-term and mid-term results are promising, there is a scarcity of published long-term data. Hence, further long-term data is required before a definitive conclusion can be drawn.

title: Incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections after PICC insertion: Impact of a newly established vascular access unit in a French university hospital.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: While peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are widely used, they remain associated with infectious risk. Even though the value of dedicated catheter teams is well-recognized, evidence regarding vascular access units is limited. This study compared catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates between a Vascular and Interventional Angiography Unit (VIAU) (insertion performed by physicians) and a newly established Vascular Access Unit (VAU) (insertion performed by nurse anesthetists under anesthesiologists' supervision).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted in a French university hospital, including patients having undergone PICC insertion from January 2017 to June 2020 (VIAU) and from January to June 2020 (VAU). CRBSI rates during catheter dwell time and within 8 days after PICC insertion were compared. Risk factors for CRBSI were assessed using logistic regression analysis.

RESULTS: Among 3332 inserted PICCs, 266 (8.0%) CRBSIs occurred during catheter dwell time, with no significant difference between the VIAU (7.7%) and the VAU (9.3%). In multivariate analysis, the risk of CRBSI between the VIAU and the VAU did not significantly differ (adjusted OR = 0.978 [95%CI, 0.558-1.714]); non-metastatic cancer was associated with a higher risk of CRBSI, whereas older age appeared protective. The 8-day CRBSI rate (0.9%) was similar between the two departments (0.9% for the VIAU and 1.0% for the VAU). Slightly more than half of the CRBSIs were caused by Staphylococcus species, and one third by Gram-negative bacteria.

DISCUSSION - CONCLUSION: CRBSI rates between the established and the newly created units were similar. These results suggest that a dedicated vascular access unit staffed by trained professionals can achieve outcomes comparable to those obtained by an experienced unit.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: While peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are widely used, they remain associated with infectious risk. Even though the value of dedicated catheter teams is well-recognized, evidence regarding vascular access units is limited. This study compared catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI) rates between a Vascular and Interventional Angiography Unit (VIAU) (insertion performed by physicians) and a newly established Vascular Access Unit (VAU) (insertion performed by nurse anesthetists under anesthesiologists' supervision).

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set.

title: Expressing Needs and Concerns During Nursing Care: An Ethnographic Study of Patients Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: This focused ethnographic study aimed to explore how patients expressed their needs and concerns during nursing care while undergoing planned open repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Fieldwork was conducted in a vascular surgery ward at a Danish university hospital between December 2024 and August 2025. Ten patients admitted for planned open repair were followed during their inpatient stay through participant observation. The ethnographic record comprised 85 hours of observation and was analyzed using Spradley's Developmental Research Sequence within a hermeneutic interpretive orientation. The overall cultural theme identified was "Expressing vulnerability while trying not to be a burden." This theme captures how physical recovery needs were more readily expressed, whereas emotional and existential concerns were softened, held back, or communicated through silence, humor, or reliance on family members. The included cases illustrate three domains: unspoken suffering as a barrier to well-being, family members' work in making patients' needs visible, and becoming dependent on nursing care as a patient. The findings show that patients undergoing open repair struggle to voice vulnerability directly during hospitalization. The study highlights the importance of nursing care that attends not only to explicit requests for help, but also to subtle verbal, embodied, and relational expressions of vulnerability.

title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood.

METHODS: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis.

RESULTS: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI.

CONCLUSIONS: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis.

title: Comparison of Midterm Outcomes of Different Patch Types for Endarterectomy of the Common Femoral Artery. Secondary Analysis from the ARISTON Multicenter Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to analyze patients who underwent femoral endarterectomy (FEA) for common femoral artery disease (CFAD) within the multicenter AtheRectomy-assIsted endovaScular Therapy versus OpeN (ARISTON) registry aiming to compare the short-term and midterm outcomes based on the use of different patch materials.

METHODS: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicenter observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary end point of the study was clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

RESULTS: A total of 547 patients undergoing FEA with patch angioplasty were included in the analysis and stratified according to the patch material into 3 groups: (i) prosthetic patch (PP; group A, n = 249), (ii) bovine pericardium patch (BPP; group B, n = 262), and (iii) great saphenous vein patch (GSVP; group C, n = 36). Baseline characteristics differed significantly among groups. Technical success of the FEA procedure was achieved in all cases. Perioperative mortality was low and not significantly different between groups. Kaplan-Meier estimates of freedom from CD-TLR at 2 years were 86.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 80.8-90.2%) in the PP group, 88.9% (95% CI, 83.1-92.8%) in the BPP group, and 69.8% (95% CI, 49.3-83.3%) in the GSVP group, with no statistically significant difference between groups (log-rank P = 0.067). In multivariable analysis for freedom from CD-TLR, neither BPP (hazard ratio [HR] 0.78, 95% CI 0.47-1.29; P = 0.330) nor GSVP (HR 1.99, 95% CI 0.95-4.17; P = 0.069) was significantly associated with the outcome.

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary multicenter real-world experience, PP and BPP were the most used materials for patch reconstruction after FEA in patients with primary CFAD. Although the distribution of baseline risk factors was different between groups, midterm freedom from CD-TLR was not significantly different between groups. The findings describe contemporary surgeon-selected practice but do not determine the optimal allocation strategy, thereby reinforcing a clinically relevant message for contemporary vascular surgery: appropriate patient selection, meticulous technical execution, and comprehensive revascularization strategy are the key drivers of clinical outcomes, whereas patch material should likely be regarded as a complementary component within an individualized reconstructive framework.

METHODS: The study is a secondary analysis of patients from a retrospective multicenter observational registry of FEA with patch angioplasty, extracted the ARISTON collaborative. The primary end point of the study was clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

title: Early stroke after aortic arch repair: Comparative and proportional meta-analyses of open, hybrid, and total endovascular strategies.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early stroke remains one of the most devastating complications after aortic arch repair. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks.

METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026. Observational studies reporting neurological outcomes after adult open, hybrid, or total endovascular aortic arch repair were included. The primary comparative meta-analysis pooled propensity score-matched or weighted studies comparing hybrid with open repair using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Separate proportional random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled stroke incidences for each strategy. Risk of bias was assessed using Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions and the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The protocol was prospectively registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420261461659).

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included. Seven propensity score-matched or weighted cohorts comprising 948 patients (474 open and 474 hybrid repairs) contributed to the primary comparative meta-analysis. No significant difference in early stroke was identified between hybrid and open repair [odds ratio, 1.99; 95% confidence interval, 0.46-8.58; P = .292; I2 = 52.9%). Post hoc comparative analyses restricted to dissection cohorts (3 cohorts; 572 patients) and zone 0 hybrid repair (3 cohorts; 448 patients) were also inconclusive and highly imprecise. In descriptive proportional analyses, pooled early-stroke incidences were 5.3% after open, 7.5% after hybrid, and 6.4% after total endovascular repair. Technique-stratified incidences were 6.1% for conventional open repair, 4.4% for open repair with frozen elephant trunk, and 5.3% for branched total endovascular repair.

CONCLUSIONS: Adjusted comparative evidence showed no significant difference in early stroke between hybrid and open aortic arch repair. Evidence for total endovascular repair remains predominantly noncomparative. Treatment should be individualized according to aortic pathology, urgency, anatomy, operative risk, and institutional expertise.

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated early stroke after open, hybrid, and total endovascular aortic arch repair using separate comparative and proportional frameworks. METHODS: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception through July 27, 2026.

title: ArtAssist sequential compression biomechanical device as a cost-dominant limb salvage strategy for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia: A decade and half, single-center cohort study with health economic and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive a median €88,820/patient; the long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device (SCBD) is lacking.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

RESULTS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (hazard ratio: 1.70, 1.80, 1.71; all P ≤ .012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = .008). Ninety-day rental (€1373/patient) reduced total expenditure sixfold vs primary amputation (€5.3M vs €30.8M), saving €76,500/patient. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity yielded a gain of 3.37 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) per patient; incremental cost-effectiveness ratio €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a sixfold reduction in costs vs primary amputation, +3.37 QALYs/patient, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-center cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for nonreconstructible CLTI.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity.

title: Contemporary Analysis of the Volume-Outcome Relationship for Patients With Nontraumatic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale. We examined the association of volume metrics with outcomes in an SAH cohort.

METHODS: All adult (≥18 years) hospitalizations with a primary diagnosis of nontraumatic SAH were identified from the 2016 to 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database. Multivariable regression models were developed to evaluate the independent and joint associations of SAH admission and clipping and coiling procedural volume with in-hospital outcomes.

RESULTS: Of an estimated 142 271 hospitalizations, index mortality was 20.2%. Following risk adjustment, both increasing SAH admission volume and clipping and coiling procedural volume were independently associated with reduced mortality. When modeled jointly, however, clipping and coiling procedural volume remained an independent predictor of mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 0.981 per 10 procedures, P<0.001) whereas SAH admission volume was no longer significant (P=0.40).

CONCLUSIONS: Joint examination of SAH and clipping and coiling procedural volume revealed procedural caseload to be the dominant predictor of in-hospital mortality, suggesting that survival benefits historically attributed to admission volume may be more precisely explained by procedural expertise. These findings support reexamination of volume-based benchmarks in contemporary cerebrovascular care frameworks.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) carries a substantial mortality burden and risk of long-term morbidity. Although prior investigations have demonstrated an inverse association between SAH admission volume and in-hospital mortality, reported thresholds remain broad. Importantly, the relative importance of both admission and procedural volume has yet to be evaluated on a national scale.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain.

METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively; P=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]); P for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin.

CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial.

title: Exercise and Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms: A Paradigm Shift Toward Informed, Personalized Activity Guidelines.
abstract: Exercise is widely recognized for its cardiovascular benefits; however, its safety and role in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysms (TAAs) remains complex due to its distinctive biomechanical vulnerabilities. Fundamentally different from abdominal aortic aneurysms, TAAs develop from distinct pathophysiological processes that affect their hemodynamic responses to stressors and influence their risk of adverse aortic events. Exercise induces acute hemodynamic changes, including increased stroke volume, systolic and pulse pressures, and transient aortic stiffening. These changes impose mechanical stress on the aortic wall, potentially accelerating aneurysm progression or triggering adverse aortic events. Although moderate aerobic exercise generally appears safe with potential cardiovascular benefits, evidence supporting safe practices in TAAs is limited. Current guidelines frequently extrapolate from abdominal aortic aneurysm data, which overlook the specificities of the thoracic aorta. This review underscores the urgent need for comprehensive research, using advanced imaging, biomarker profiling, and real-time hemodynamic monitoring to understand how different exercise modalities and intensities affect TAAs. Well-designed prospective studies are crucial to improve risk stratification, optimize antihypertensive strategies, develop personalized exercise prescriptions, and provide evidence-informed guidance to patients. Perioperative strategies like prehabilitation and structured postoperative rehabilitation show promise but lack rigorous evaluation. Ultimately, this work advocates a paradigm shift from conservative inactivity toward informed, individualized physical activity regimens tailored to each patient's risk profile. This approach aims to maximize cardiovascular benefits while minimizing adverse aortic events, thereby improving overall health and quality of life in patients with TAAs.

title: Paradoxical Association of Body Mass Index With Occurrence and Mortality of Venous Thromboembolism in Hospitalized Patients: A National Hospital-Based Cohort Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty.

METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort. Participants were categorized as lean weight (BMI <18.5 kg/m2), normal weight (18.5 ≤BMI<24.0 kg/m2), overweight (24.0 ≤BMI <28.0 kg/m2), and obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2). Odds ratios (ORs) were calculated by logistic regression models.

RESULTS: In all participants, 59 002 (1.8%) developed VTE during hospitalization. After adjusting for the confounding factors, compared with normal weight, the risk of VTE occurrence reduced by 18% (odds ratio [OR], 0.82 [95% CI, 0.80-0.83]) in participants with overweight and 22% (OR, 0.78,[95% CI, 0.75-0.81]) in participants with obesity. The protective association of overweight/obesity was more pronounced in age ≥65 years, female patients, and surgery participants (Pfor interaction <0.05), whereas in internal medical participants, obesity was associated with a higher risk of VTE occurrence (OR, 1.11 [95% CI, 1.01-1.21]). A total of 636 (1.1%) patients with VTE died before discharge. No significant association was observed between overweight/obesity and post-VTE mortality. However, in the surgical subgroup, obesity was associated with a lower risk of post-VTE mortality (OR, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.17-0.80], Pfor interaction <0.05).

CONCLUSION: An inverse association between BMI and VTE occurrence was observed among at-risk inpatients, most pronounced in older, female, and surgical subgroups. Notably, obesity remained a risk factor in medical patients, whereas among surgical patients who developed VTE, it was paradoxically associated with lower mortality.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The association between body mass index (BMI) and venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurrence and mortality is controversial. This study aimed to investigate the association of BMI with VTE occurrence and mortality and explore the consistency across age, sex, and medical specialty. METHODS: This study included 3 199 526 inpatients at potential risk for VTE from a nationwide hospital-based cohort.

title: When History Returns: Hybrid Management of Syphilitic Aortitis Causing Severe Aortic Arch Branch Stenosis and Cerebral Hypoperfusion.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular manifestations of tertiary syphilis are rare in the antibiotic era, but important to consider in atypical vascular findings. These manifestations typically appear several years after the primary infection and may lead to structural damage in the cardiovascular system, requiring surgical intervention despite appropriate antibiotic therapy.

REPORT: This case describes a rare manifestation of cardiovascular syphilis in a 46 year old woman presenting with dizziness, pre-syncope, and syncope consistent with global cerebral ischaemia. Extensive evaluation revealed syphilitic aortitis with severe stenosis and or occlusion of all the major aortic arch branches. The patient was managed with antibiotic therapy in combination with surgical revascularisation. Both endovascular and open surgical approaches were used to restore blood flow to the left common carotid, left vertebral, and left subclavian arteries. This intervention improved cerebral perfusion and resolved the patient's symptoms. At two years, the carotid stent was patent, while the carotid subclavian bypass was occluded. The patient remained free from cerebral ischaemic symptoms but reported bilateral arm claudication.

CONCLUSION: Tertiary syphilis should be considered as a differential diagnosis when atypical arterial disease is encountered. Hybrid revascularisation may provide an effective, less invasive treatment strategy.

These manifestations typically appear several years after the primary infection and may lead to structural damage in the cardiovascular system, requiring surgical intervention despite appropriate antibiotic therapy. REPORT: This case describes a rare manifestation of cardiovascular syphilis in a 46 year old woman presenting with dizziness, pre-syncope, and syncope consistent with global cerebral ischaemia.

title: Functional outcome after recurrent laryngeal nerve injury following thoracic aortic surgery.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury is a recognized complication of aortic surgery, yet data on long-term functional outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of RLN injury and assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis included adult patients undergoing aortic arch or thoracoabdominal aortic surgery between 2001 and 2024. RLN injury was diagnosed by postoperative vocal cord paralysis. Aortic arch surgery included partial and total arch replacement, while thoracoabdominal surgery involved the proximal descending aorta. The primary end point was full voice recovery. Secondary end points included recovery of normal vocal cord mobility, residual dysphonia, the need for voice therapy, and vocal cord interventions.

RESULTS: Among 2983 patients undergoing aortic surgery, 70 (2.3%) were diagnosed with postoperative RLN injury. Median follow-up was 17 (interquartile range, 7-25) months. The incidence of RLN injury was 1.7% after arch surgery and 5.3% after thoracoabdominal procedures. At final follow-up, 34 patients (50%) achieved full voice recovery, while 20 (30%) had mild dysphonia, 9 (13%) moderate dysphonia, and 5 (7%) severe dysphonia. Voice therapy was performed in 49 (70%) patients, and 10 (14%) required additional vocal cord interventions.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large cohort, the incidence of RLN injury after aortic surgery was lower than previously reported. Functional outcomes were favorable, with most patients achieving full or near-complete voice recovery through conservative or interventional management. Structured follow-up and multidisciplinary care remain essential to optimize outcomes after RLN injury.

This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of RLN injury and assess voice recovery after thoracic aortic surgery. title: Acute management of pelvic ring injuries: identifying common treatment principles across institutional algorithms.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear.

METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus were searched on January 8, 2026, for peer-reviewed publications published from January 1, 2006, through December 31, 2025 that described algorithms, pathways, or protocols for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries. Two independent reviewers performed study selection and data extraction. Algorithm components related to mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, imaging, hemorrhage control, and damage control resuscitation were extracted and compared using descriptive quantitative and qualitative synthesis.

RESULTS: The search identified 328 records that underwent title and abstract screening, and 63 articles were assessed for full-text eligibility. Twenty-five studies were included in the final analysis. All included algorithms (25/25, 100%) used physiology-based decision-making. Early noninvasive mechanical stabilization was specified in 23/25 algorithms (92%); pelvic binders were specified in 17/25 (68%). Angiography with potential angioembolization was included in 19/25 algorithms (76%), exploratory laparotomy in 10/25 (40%), and resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) in 3/25 (12%). Computed tomography was incorporated into 20/25 algorithms (80%), whereas pelvic radiography was included in 18/25 (72%). Fracture morphology was used as a treatment decision point in 4/25 algorithms (16%), and pelvic packing was described in 20/25 publications (80%).

CONCLUSION: Published algorithms for the acute management of pelvic ring injuries demonstrate substantial consistency despite institutional variation. Early mechanical stabilization, physiologic assessment, damage control resuscitation, radiologic evaluation, and structured hemorrhage-control pathways were identified as the most common components of contemporary management algorithms.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Pelvic ring injuries are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, particularly in patients presenting with hemodynamic instability and major hemorrhage. Numerous institutions have developed management algorithms for the acute treatment of pelvic ring injuries; however, the common principles underlying these pathways remain unclear. METHODS: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected.

title: Venous Hypertension Associated with an Abnormal Configuration of a Protruding Cephalic Arch Stent in Arteriovenous Haemodialysis Access: A Case Report.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cephalic arch stenosis is a common cause of access dysfunction in brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistulae, and recurrent lesions are often treated with stent placement. Although stent protrusion into the axillary vein is frequently tolerated, an abnormal stent-vein configuration combined with in stent re-stenosis may impair physiological venous drainage. This case report presents severe venous hypertension resulting from in stent re-stenosis within the protruding segment impairing physiological axillary venous outflow and an abnormal stent-vein configuration caused by stent tip contact with the opposite axillary vein wall, redistributing access flow.

REPORT: A 75 year old man receiving long term haemodialysis developed upper extremity oedema and prolonged post-dialysis bleeding from his brachiocephalic arteriovenous fistula. Computed tomography showed a cephalic arch stent protruding across the cephalic axillary junction, its tip contacting the axillary vein wall opposite the junction. Access fistulography demonstrated severe in stent re-stenosis with neointimal hyperplasia reducing the available sidewall openings. Through the remaining patent openings, part of the access flow continued centrally and part was redirected into the axillary venous segment peripheral to the cephalic axillary junction, with retrograde opacification and subsequent collateral drainage. The protruding stent segment was excised, and the axillary vein reconstructed with a patch. After surgery, oedema improved, collateral venous flow decreased, and the access remained functional at one year despite residual re-stenosis.

DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that cephalic arch stent protrusion may become clinically significant when in stent re-stenosis within the protruding segment impairs axillary venous outflow and the stent-vein configuration causes access flow redistribution. In this patient, neointimal hyperplasia reduced the sidewall openings, impairing physiological axillary venous outflow, while residual openings allowed redistribution of access flow into the peripheral axillary venous segment. Recognition of this abnormal stent-vein configuration and flow pattern is important because open surgical reconstruction may be required to restore venous drainage while preserving haemodialysis access function.

Although stent protrusion into the axillary vein is frequently tolerated, an abnormal stent-vein configuration combined with in stent re-stenosis may impair physiological venous drainage. This case report presents severe venous hypertension resulting from in stent re-stenosis within the protruding segment impairing physiological axillary venous outflow and an abnormal stent-vein configuration caused by stent tip contact with the opposite axillary vein wall, redistributing access flow.

title: Contemporary Management of Subclavian and Axillary Artery Aneurysms in Connective Tissue Disease: Navigating Therapeutic Uncertainty in a Rare Vascular Disease without Dedicated Guidelines.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based. Explicit guidance from the Society for Vascular Surgery and the European Society for Vascular Surgery is lacking.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of the English-language literature to identify all reported cases of subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in patients with heritable connective-tissue disorders. Searches were conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from inception to June 30, 2025. Data were extracted on treatment modality (open surgical, endovascular, or hybrid) and clinical outcomes (limb loss, revascularization patency, complications, and need for reintervention). The review protocol was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261332695).

RESULTS: Of 142 records identified, 24 studies met the inclusion criteria after duplicate removal and screening. These studies described 43 subclavian and axillary artery aneurysms in 25 patients (15 men [60%] and 10 women [40%]; median age, 46 years; range, 11-68). Aneurysm diameter was reported for 36 of 43 aneurysms (84%; median, 40 mm; range, 22-100 mm) and was not reported for the remaining 7 (16%). Marfan syndrome was the most frequent underlying disorder (20/25, 80%), followed by vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome type IV (3/25, 12%) and Loeys-Dietz syndrome/TGFBR2-related arteriopathy (2/25, 8%). Eight aneurysms (8/43, 19%) required urgent or emergent treatment. Treatment modalities comprised open surgical repair in 22 of 43 aneurysms (51%) - including interposition grafting in 12/22 (55%), bypass in 5/22 (23%), arterial ligation in 3/22 (14%), and aneurysmectomy with end-to-end anastomosis in 2/22 (9%) - hybrid procedures in 15 (35%), and endovascular therapy in 6 (14%) - including covered stent-grafting in 5/6 (83%) and coil/liquid embolization in 1/6 (17%). Immediate technical success - complete aneurysm exclusion without endoleak at the index procedure- was 95% (41 of 43 aneurysms). Two aneurysms (4.7%), both in the hybrid group, represented an index-procedure failure due to endoleak (one type I, one type III); freedom from reintervention was therefore 95% (41/43). Both were subsequently excluded after a secondary reintervention, yielding a delayed technical success rate of 100% (43/43). No 30-day mortality or limb loss was reported. Primary patency of the treated segment was 100% (43/43), as no graft/segment thrombosis, occlusion, or flow-limiting stenosis occurred; secondary patency was 100% (43/43). Where a numeric follow-up duration could be extracted, mean follow-up was 8 months (range, 6-11 months) in the endovascular group (4/5 patients), 15 months (range, 2 weeks-4 years) in the open group (5/13 patients), and 15 months (range, 1-60 months) in the hybrid group (6/7 patients); a precise duration was not reported for the remaining patients.

CONCLUSION: The available evidence demonstrates that both open and endovascular repair can achieve satisfactory short- and mid-term outcomes. However, patient selection, procedural planning, and surveillance protocols remain poorly standardized. The observed recurrences and the limited duration of follow-up reported in the literature underscore the need for rigorous, lifelong surveillance. Prospective multicenter registries are warranted to refine best practice and to guide the development of devices and techniques tailored to fragile connective-tissue vessels.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Subclavian artery aneurysms represent one of the rarest forms of peripheral arterial aneurysmal disease. Despite their low incidence, management in patients with underlying connective tissue disorders poses specific challenges related to intrinsic vessel fragility. Because of their rarity, the available literature is largely confined to case reports and small, heterogeneous retrospective series, and management remains largely experience-based rather than evidence-based.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to zone 0 or 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, and none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost to follow-up (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (such as aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, and survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (zone 1-3; complete 56% vs incomplete/LTF 27%; P < .001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs incomplete/LTF 18%; P < .001), in-hospital thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension (7% vs 2%; P = .028), and thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs incomplete/LTF 5%; P = .002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete 12% vs incomplete 5%; P = .007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs 15%; P = .002) within 1-year of acute dissection. The long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete 97% vs incomplete 97% vs LTF 91%), 3-years (complete 92% vs incomplete 95% vs LTF 81%; P = .021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (P = .13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (hazard ratio, 2.87; 95% confidence interval, 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (hazard ratio, 2.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and midterm survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Reintervention burden and patency of hemodialysis vascular access in a 15-year single-center cohort.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Maintaining a hemodialysis access typically requires repeated intervention; yet, the cumulative reintervention burden-distinct from patency-is rarely quantified, and configuration-specific estimates from Asian centers are scarce. In this study, we evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous access cases over 15 years at a single center.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 871 consecutive cases of upper extremity arteriovenous access (648 fistulas; 223 grafts) created in 810 patients between 2009 and 2024. From operative records, every subsequent procedure was determined to be patency-maintaining or access-abandoning; operations unrelated to the access under study, including kidney transplantation, catheter procedures, and peripheral arterial interventions, were excluded. Patency was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method according to the accepted reporting standards and was compared across configurations-radiocephalic fistula, brachiocephalic fistula, basilic vein transposition, and graft. The reintervention burden is expressed as interventions per access-year. The predictors of the loss of primary patency were identified using multivariable Cox regression, and in a competing risk analysis, kidney transplantation was considered a competing event.

RESULTS: The median follow-up duration was 14.7 months. The overall primary, assisted primary, and secondary patency rates were 60.3%, 50.5%, and 44.6%; 87.1%, 81.5%, and 77.1%; and 96.8%, 95.7%, and 94.1% at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. The 1-year primary patency rates differed by the configuration: 70.1% for radiocephalic fistulas, 63.3% for brachiocephalic fistulas, 71.6% for basilic vein transpositions, and 36.2% for grafts (P < .001). Across 2211 access-years, 743 patency-maintaining interventions were performed (0.336 per access-year), and 37.2% of access cases required at least one reintervention. The intervention burden was concentrated in grafts: 1.09 intervention per access-year for grafts vs 0.25 intervention per access-year for autogenous fistulas, with a difference of approximately 4.4-fold. The graft configuration (hazard ratio, 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.86-3.06), female sex (1.37; 1.10-1.71), ischemic heart disease (1.42; 1.04-1.94), and diabetes (1.26; 1.00-1.57) independently predicted the loss of primary patency. These findings persisted after excluding maturation-assisting procedures and in the competing risk analysis (subdistribution hazard ratio for graft reintervention, 2.32).

CONCLUSIONS: High secondary patency was achieved at the cost of substantial reintervention concentrated in grafts, which required maintenance that was approximately 4.4 times that of autogenous fistulas. Reporting the explicit reintervention burden alongside patency supports autogenous-first, configuration-aware access planning and patient counseling.

In this study, we evaluated patency and quantified the configuration-specific reintervention burden of upper-extremity arteriovenous access cases over 15 years at a single center. title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD.

METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year.

RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year.

CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

title: Real-life venous thromboembolism risk scores in multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment with daratumumab and lenalidomide has improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), however the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is high. Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort study.

METHODS: All consecutive MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and concomitant LMWH-ASA thromboprophylaxis between July, 2018 and September, 2023 were evaluated through chart review. Kaplan-Meier method and Concordance-Index (C-index) were used to estimate risk scores' prognostic accuracy.

RESULTS: 95 patients (median age 74 years) were included (n= 47 NTE-MM, and n= 48 RRMM). At 12 months from Dara-Rd initiation, 10 (10.4%) patients developed VTE; 4 (4.2%) had bleeding complications, and 2 (2.1%) patients died. Six VTE events (6.2%) occurred within first 6 months from Dara-Rd initiation while on LMWH prophylaxis, whereas 2 VTE (2%) developed in two patients receiving aspirin. The accuracy of IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM and EHR-CAT scores was generally poor, with C-Index values ranging from 0.43 (95% confidence intervals [95%CI] 0.30 to 0.56) to 0.53 (95%CI: 0.38 to 0.68). LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was completed by 89.5% of the cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-life cohort of MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and guideline-recommended antithrombotic prophylaxis, currently available VTE risk scores demonstrated moderate to poor prognostic accuracy. LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was feasible but associated with residual VTE risk.

title: Direct oral anticoagulants versus vitamin K antagonists for the treatment of venous thromboembolism in adults with sickle cell disease: a Bayesian meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly used as alternatives to vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) for the treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) in patients with sickle cell disease (SCD). However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing DOACs with VKAs in patients with SCD and VTE. PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to March 2026. Primary outcomes were recurrent VTE and major bleeding (MB). Bayesian random-effects models with weakly informative priors were used to estimate pooled odds ratios (ORs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Posterior probabilities were derived using Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling.

RESULTS: Four retrospective studies including 271 patients (155 DOACs and 116 VKAs) were included. Recurrent VTE did not differ between groups (OR, 0.82; 95% CrI, 0.38-1.75), with a 67.1% posterior probability favoring DOACs, indicating equipoise. DOACs were associated with a significantly lower risk of MB (OR, 0.25; 95% CrI, 0.07-0.80), with a 99.2% probability of superiority. Between-study heterogeneity was low (τ = 0.15 for recurrent VTE; τ = 0.30 for MB).

CONCLUSION: DOACs demonstrate comparable efficacy to VKAs for preventing recurrent VTE in SCD, with a clinically meaningful reduction in MB. Given their safety profile and convenience, DOACs may be preferred; randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

However, comparative evidence is limited to small observational studies, and prior frequentist meta-analyses may be unreliable due to sparse data and zero-event outcomes. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare the efficacy and safety of DOACs versus VKAs for VTE treatment in adults with SCD.

title: Morganella morganii Detected During Transfemoral Amputation in a Diabetic Foot With Soft Tissue Necrosis.
abstract: This case report describes a 63-year-old man with diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease who was referred to our clinic with circulatory insufficiency and a foul-smelling necrotizing wound of the right lower extremity. The patient had previously undergone bilateral balloon angioplasty, which restored distal pulses; however, progressive soft tissue deterioration led to extensive purulent ulcers along the anteromedial and posterior aspects of the lower leg. Imaging demonstrated subcutaneous gas in the posterior soft tissues, and transfemoral amputation was performed. During surgical dissection, purulent discharge was observed along the anteromedial aspect of the femur, and intraoperative samples were obtained for microbiological analysis. Cultures yielded Enterobacter species and Morganella morganii, the latter being an opportunistic Gram-negative bacillus that is rarely implicated in musculoskeletal infections. This case is notable for the uncommon identification of Morganella morganii in a deep musculoskeletal infection and emphasizes the importance of broad microbiological consideration in necrotizing soft tissue infections, particularly in patients with diabetes or other predisposing conditions. Timely surgical intervention, adequate source control, and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy remain essential in such complex clinical scenarios.

title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×109/L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×109/L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

title: Clinical significance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in glycemic control and ischemic limb damage in type 2 diabetes with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical relevance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) complicated by chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) .

METHODS: A total of 520 patients with CLTI were collected and divided into two groups based on the history of T2DM: the combined T2DM group and the non-T2DM group. The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

RESULTS: The CTI in the combined T2DM group was significantly greater than that in the non-T2DM group (P < 0.001). The CTI in the poorly controlled blood glucose group was significantly greater than that in the well controlled blood glucose group (P < 0.001). Regardless of whether CLTI patients had T2DM, the CTI in the overweight group was greater than that in the non-overweight group (P < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the CTI discriminating the high wound, ischemia, and foot infection (WIfI) classification was 0.813 (P < 0.001). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that an increased CTI was an independently associated factor for the high WIfI classification in CLTI patients (OR = 6.409, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with CLTI and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

CONCLUSIONS: The CTI was closely related to the presence of T2DM, blood glucose control level, and overweight status in CLTI patients. The CTI has certain clinical value in discriminating the degree of ischemia in CLTI, and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed.

title: Nongeneral Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals (PIs), and prespecified influence diagnostics.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with GA (risk ratio [RR] 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-1.52; I2≈86%; wide PI). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I2≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in intensive care unit stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

CONCLUSION: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to GA. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.

While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus.

title: One-year outcomes of hepatic artery stenosis after pediatric liver transplantation: Results from the international, multicenter HEPATIC registry.
abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to describe one-year graft and patient survival after hepatic artery stenosis (HAS) following pediatric liver transplantation (pLT), and to explore outcomes by timing of HAS diagnosis and treatment strategy within the HAS cohort.

METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed. Donor-, recipient-, and transplant-related characteristics were analyzed. The primary outcome was one-year graft and patient survival.

RESULTS: HAS was diagnosed in 1.2% of patients (n = 130; 51% female; median age 4.4 years [IQR 1.4-11.6]), of whom 5% (n = 7) progressed to thrombosis (HAT). One-year graft and patient survival were 93% and 96%, respectively. Management consisted mainly of antithrombotic therapy alone (41.5%) or endovascular therapy (EVT; 41.5%), with no significant difference in one-year graft or patient survival between these approaches. Early HAS (≤21 days post-pLT) was associated with significantly higher one-year graft loss than late HAS (16%vs. 1%; p < 0.001). All deaths occurred in the early HAS group.

CONCLUSIONS: One-year graft and patient survival after HAS were high. Antithrombotic therapy alone and EVT were the most common management strategies. Early HAS was associated with lower one-year survival. Prospective studies with standardized diagnostic and treatment criteria are needed for validation.

METHODS: Patients who developed HAS after pLT were included as per definition from the HEPATIC registry. The registry contains data from 32 centers across 21 countries over a 20-year period, during which 10,564 primary pLTs were performed.

title: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion With Signs of Ocular Hypoperfusion After Parent Artery Occlusion for a Traumatic Carotid-Cavernous Fistula: A Case Report.
abstract: A carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) can cause a wide range of ocular complications, including venous stasis retinopathy, secondary glaucoma, and central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). Retinal complications have been reported after endovascular closure of the shunt, but there are few reports describing the ophthalmic course of an eye in which the shunt persisted and in which parent artery occlusion of the internal carotid artery was required. A 63-year-old man was diagnosed with a traumatic right internal carotid artery CCF after a road traffic injury and underwent endovascular treatment on the second and third days after the injury. Because both the transvenous and the transarterial approaches were unsuccessful, parent artery occlusion of the right internal carotid artery was performed. According to the report from the referring institution, occlusion of the shunt was incomplete, and shunt flow into the right superior ophthalmic vein persisted. Angiography approximately six months after the injury confirmed the residual shunt, and no further endovascular treatment was considered feasible. Two months later, the patient noticed decreased vision in the right eye, presented to a local ophthalmologist, and was referred to our department. At presentation, best-corrected visual acuity was 0.2 (logMAR 0.70) in the right eye, and the intraocular pressure (IOP) was 14 mmHg. The right eye showed dilated episcleral vessels, dilated retinal veins, attenuated retinal arteries, retinal hemorrhages extending from the posterior pole to the periphery, and marked macular edema, but venous tortuosity was not prominent. The pupillary light reflex was reduced, and pharmacologic mydriasis was poor, without posterior synechiae or iris atrophy. Spontaneous pulsation of the central retinal artery was present in the affected eye and was augmented by gentle digital pressure, whereas no pulsation was seen in the fellow eye. On widefield fluorescein angiography, dye first entered the central retinal artery 20.1 seconds after the start of injection and complete arterial filling was reached at 25 seconds; numerous microaneurysms were seen from the posterior pole to the mid-periphery, with widespread vascular leakage and reduced perfusion of the retinal capillary network. The fellow eye showed only a few microaneurysms and scattered hard exudates, consistent with mild nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy. The patient had type 2 diabetes mellitus, untreated for approximately 10 years and restarted after the current injury, and hypertension. An intravitreal injection of an aflibercept biosimilar 2 mg was given on the day of presentation, followed by panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) delivered in four sessions for a total of 1,580 burns. Twenty-five days after the injection, the macular edema had clearly decreased but had not completely resolved, and it had recurred by day 67. Throughout the course, the IOP remained consistently lower in the affected eye than in the fellow eye. No iris or angle neovascularization was observed. In this eye, findings of CRVO coexisted with findings suggesting reduced ocular perfusion pressure. Even in a patient with systemic risk factors, local factors should be considered when the findings are confined to, or markedly more severe in, one eye. When no further treatment of the causative lesion is possible, management of the ocular complications is limited to ophthalmic measures, and their effects and limitations must be evaluated separately.

Retinal complications have been reported after endovascular closure of the shunt, but there are few reports describing the ophthalmic course of an eye in which the shunt persisted and in which parent artery occlusion of the internal carotid artery was required. A 63-year-old man was diagnosed with a traumatic right internal carotid artery CCF after a road traffic injury and underwent endovascular treatment on the second and third days after the injury.

title: Clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism: secondary outcomes of the Hydra randomized clinical trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite its high prevalence, practice-based data on management and outcomes after cancer-associated pulmonary embolism (PE) are scarce, and no studies have investigated quality of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE.

METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer. Patients with PE at baseline or during 90-day follow-up were included in this study. Outcomes were recurrent venous thromboembolism, major bleeding, all-cause mortality, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life as assessed by the Pulmonary Embolism Quality of Life (PEmb-QoL) questionnaire. PEmb-QoL scores were compared with those for the general PE population reported in the FOCUS study. Lower scores indicate better QoL.

RESULTS: A total of 125 patients were included, of which 103 (82%) had PE at baseline, and 22 (18%) developed PE during follow-up. The 90-day cumulative incidence of recurrent venous thromboembolism and major bleeding was 2.5% (95% CI 0.67%-6.6%) and 2.5% (95% CI 0.68%-6.7%), respectively. All-cause mortality at 90 days was 32% (95% CI 23%-40%). Two-thirds of patients continued anticoagulation until less than 24 hours before death, and the median time between stopping anticoagulation and death was 10 days (IQR, 4-14). The median 90-day PEmb-QoL score was 33% (IQR, 13-51) versus 20% (IQR, 10-40) reported in the FOCUS study.

CONCLUSION: Patients with cancer-associated PE suffer from high mortality, high morbidity, and impaired quality of life. Anticoagulation therapy is frequently continued until the last days of life.

OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate clinical outcomes, anticoagulation practice patterns, and quality of life after cancer-associated PE. METHODS: The Hydra randomized clinical trial assessed the safety of the YEARS algorithm versus computed tomography pulmonary angiography only to exclude acute PE in patients with cancer.

title: Adherence to the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines for the Management of Neck of Femur Fractures.
abstract: Introduction Over 72,000 hip fractures occur annually in the United Kingdom, costing over £2 billion, with 10% mortality at 30 days and 30% annually. Therefore, the study aimed to compare hip fracture care at North Manchester General Hospital with the British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) guidelines. Methodology A retrospective review of electronic patient records at Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust was conducted from September to November 2025. Patients aged >60 years with native intracapsular or extracapsular femoral neck fractures, or those aged >60 years with pathological femoral neck fractures, were included. Descriptive analysis was performed to ascertain compliance with BOAST guidelines. Results The management of 51 patients was audited against 13 BOAST parameters. 100% compliance was achieved in seven parameters: certainty of diagnosis, a multidisciplinary team (MDT) approach to patient care, preoperative optimisation by an orthogeriatric team within 72 hours, documented weight-bearing status, falls risk assessment, bone health assessment, and data entry into the National Hip Fracture Database (NHFD). Parameters with less than 100% compliance were post-operative physiotherapy (50, 98%), venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis (50, 98%), analgesia (46, 91%), VTE assessment (45, 88%), post-operative delirium assessment (43, 84%), and surgery within 36 hours (32, 62.8%). Reasons for non-compliance included transfer to the intensive care unit (ICU) for post-operative physiotherapy; workload-related delays in VTE prophylaxis; unfamiliarity with local analgesia protocols among newly appointed National Health Service (NHS) doctors; inconsistent documentation of VTE assessment; and inconsistent completion of post-operative delirium assessments, with unclear responsibilities between doctors and coordinators. Limited theatre capacity and the need for medical optimisation accounted for non-compliance with the 36-hour surgery target. Conclusions BOAST compliance was good overall, but gaps in documentation, timing, and role clarity remain. Improvements include enforcing admission checklists, recording arousal, attention, and acute change using the abbreviated mental test-4 (4AT), pharmacist incident reporting, trauma coordinator oversight, and neck of femur training.
