title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making.

METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons.

RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss.

CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base.

HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients.

title: Longitudinal monitoring of adalimumab levels and anti-adalimumab antibodies in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis: a prospective cohort study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to clarify the association between longitudinal adalimumab concentrations, anti-adalimumab antibodies (AAA) levels, and clinical response in Chinese patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS).

METHODS: A prospective multi-center, observational cohort study of AS patients receiving adalimumab therapy was conducted. Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization. Adalimumab concentrations were measured using a validated sandwich immunoassay. Measurement of AAA levels was performed with a laboratory-developed immunoassay system integrating electrochemiluminescence technology with specific immunomagnetic separation, with result reported as signal-to-noise ratio (S/N).

RESULTS: A total of 140 patients receiving adalimumab monotherapy were included. The median follow-up period was 169 days, and 711 plasma samples were available for adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels measurements. Seven patients had pre-existing AAA, and 120 (90.2%) of the remaining 133 patients tested positive for AAA during follow-up. A total of 48 patients were excluded from the exposure-response relationship dataset owing to pre-existing AAA (n=7), lack of active disease (n=26), incomplete follow-up (n=8), and prolonged dosing intervals (n=7). Among the remaining 92 patients, a total of 58 (63%) achieved clinical response. Adalimumab concentrations were higher, and AAA levels were significantly lower, in responders compared with non-responders at multiple time points. Exposure-response relationship models also revealed a steady-state adalimumab concentration target of 5.1 μg/mL and a week-4 concentration target of 3.3 μg/mL, corresponding to an 80% probability of clinical response. Thirty-six of 92 patients (39.1%) exhibited AAA-S/N values exceeding the putative clinically meaningful threshold (AAA-S/N=10). Patients in the high-AAA group (AAA-S/N≥10) had lower drug levels (median: 1.5 μg/mL vs. 6.9 μg/mL, P<0.0001) and poorer response rates (38.8% vs. 78.6%, P = 0.0002), relative to those in the low-AAA group (AAA-S/N<10). Furthermore, patients who were week-4 AAA-positive exhibited a 1.8-fold increased risk of non-response (relative risk, 95% confidence interval, 1.1-2.8).

CONCLUSIONS: Our results demonstrate that longitudinal profiles of adalimumab concentrations and AAA levels show a strong association with clinical responses in this Chinese AS cohort, which may inform therapeutic drug monitoring-guided adalimumab treatment strategies that remain to be further validated.

Disease activity was assessed with the AS Disease Activity Score (ASDAS), and clinical responders were defined based on ASDAS improvement together with C-reactive protein normalization.

title: Temporal Net Water Uptake Evolution and Its Association with Functional Outcome in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Subacute lesion growth after acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is associated with worse functional outcomes. The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes. In this study, we aimed to determine how associations between NWU and functional outcome vary across imaging times up to 1 week after stroke.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We included patients from the Multicenter Randomized Clinical Trial of Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke in the Netherlands (MRCLEAN-NO IV) trial with anterior circulation large vessel occlusion who were treated with endovascular treatment and had baseline, 24-hour, and 1-week follow-up noncontrast CT scans. Functional outcome at 90 days was evaluated using the mRS, analyzed both as functional independence (mRS 0-2) and across the full ordinal distribution (mRS 0-6). In the primary analysis, associations between NWU measured at different imaging time points and functional independence were examined using univariable and multivariable logistic regression models. To evaluate temporal changes in NWU, ΔNWU was calculated at different time intervals (baseline to 24 hours, 24 hours to 1 week, and baseline to 1 week), and its association with outcomes was analyzed using analogous regression models.

RESULTS: Of 539 MRCLEAN-NO IV patients, 115 were included in this study. The median time from stroke onset to randomization was 92 (IQR, 70-140) minutes. The median NWU evolved from 4.3% (interquartile range [IQR], 2.1%-6.8%) at baseline to 9.0% (IQR, 3.0%-13%) at 24 hours and 15% (IQR, 11%-19%) at 1 week. The median patient-level change (ΔNWU) from baseline to 1 week was 10% (IQR, 5.3%-16%). NWU measured at 1 week, but not at baseline or 24 hours, was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an adjusted OR (aOR) of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.90) per 5-percentage-point increase in NWU. Furthermore, a higher increase in NWU from baseline to 1-week imaging was significantly associated with functional dependence, with an aOR of 0.66 (95% CI, 0.47-0.86) per 5-percentage-point increase in ΔNWU1wk-BL.

CONCLUSIONS: In our population, NWU measured at 1 week is associated with 90-day clinical outcomes, suggesting that lesion evolution continues in the first week after stroke onset and may therefore represent a target for secondary treatments to improve clinical outcomes.

The ischemic lesion severity can be assessed with net water uptake (NWU), a CT-based marker of edema. Pretreatment NWU has been associated with worse functional outcomes; however, it remains unclear how the temporal changes in NWU influence functional outcomes.

title: Impact of direct-to-operating room transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of a direct-to-operating room (DOR) transfer protocol for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) on surgical volume, interhospital transfer patterns, and surgical outcomes at a tertiary referral center.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. In January 2020, a multidisciplinary rapid-response transfer protocol was implemented to facilitate DOR transfers. Patients were stratified into pre- and postimplementation cohorts. Differences in case volume, transfer patterns, transfer distance, time to treatment, and surgical outcomes between groups were assessed using univariable analysis, with statistical significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: A total of 96 patients underwent rAAA repair during the study period, with 28.1% treated before and 71.9% treated after implementation of the transfer protocol. Baseline characteristics were similar between cohorts, except for a higher prevalence of diabetes (40.7% vs 14.5%; P = .005) and former smokers (59.3% vs 34.8%; P = .029) in the preimplementation group. The annual rAAA repair volume increased threefold after implementation, from a mean of 4.5 to 13.8 cases/year. Overall, 86.5% of patients were transferred from outside hospitals, with a significant increase in the proportion of external transfers after implementation (70.4% vs 92.8%; P = .007). Median transfer distance increased from 23.7 to 49.1 miles (P = .017) and time from transfer acceptance to operating room arrival decreased from 173 to 124 minutes (P = .145). Distance-adjusted transfer time decreased significantly from 9.5 to 4.1 min/mile (P = .017). Endovascular repair was performed in 68.8% of patients, with no difference between cohorts. In-hospital stroke (6.2%), myocardial infarction (7.3%), and mortality (22.9%) rates were similar between groups. Median length of stay was 6.6 days. Thirty-day outcomes did not differ between cohorts, with readmission in 13.5%, reintervention in 36.5%, and mortality in 25.0% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of a multidisciplinary DOR protocol for rAAA was associated with a sustained increase in surgical volume, higher rates of interhospital transfer, expansion of the regional referral network, and lower distance-adjusted transfer times, with perioperative outcomes remaining within contemporary benchmarks.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-institution cohort study used institutional databases and the Vascular Quality Initiative registry to identify all patients undergoing rAAA repair between 2014 and 2024. title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) in Medicare Advantage and Medicare Fee-for-Service: Differences in Patient Characteristics, Utilization, and Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over half of Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in privately administered Medicare Advantage (MA) plans, and aortic stenosis predominantly affects older patients. In this study, we evaluated whether differences in care delivery between MA and fee-for-service (FFS) Medicare contribute to cardiovascular outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR).

METHODS: Medicare patients who underwent TAVR from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were eligible for cohort inclusion. TAVR utilization rates in MA and FFS were calculated as the age- and sex-standardized number of procedures per 10 000 person-years. Patient characteristics were compared between MA and FFS using standardized mean differences (SMDs), with an SMD ≥10% considered meaningful. The association of MA versus FFS enrollment with 30-day and 1-year outcomes was assessed using logistic and Cox regression models, respectively.

RESULTS: Among the 317 630 patients (64.4% FFS, 35.6% MA) undergoing TAVR, the mean age was 80.6±7.0 years, and 55.1% were men. TAVR utilization rates were similar between MA and FFS, with 11.2 TAVRs/10 000 person-years in FFS compared with 11.7 TAVRs/10 000 person-years in MA by the end of the study. Compared with FFS patients, MA patients were more likely to be Black (5.4% versus 3.0%; SMD, -11.9) and dual-enrolled in Medicaid (13.7% versus 8.6%; SMD, -16.3). Comorbidity profiles were similar (SMD, <10%). In the comorbidity-adjusted model, MA patients had lower odds of 30-day death (adjusted odds ratio, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.86-0.95]). At 1 year, MA patients had a lower adjusted risk of death (hazard ratio, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.92-0.96]), all-cause readmission (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.85-0.88]), stroke (hazard ratio, 0.90 [95% CI, 0.87-0.94]), and aortic valve reintervention (hazard ratio, 0.86 [95% CI, 0.76-0.96]).

CONCLUSIONS: Despite similar clinical profiles and TAVR utilization, MA patients appeared to experience better 30-day and 1-year outcomes than FFS patients. Differences in care delivery may contribute, but future studies are needed to understand differences in outcomes.

METHODS: Medicare patients who underwent TAVR from January 1, 2018, to December 31, 2022, were eligible for cohort inclusion.

title: Changes in Stroke Care Regionalization in California Associated With Evolving Evidence of Benefit for Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Network Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2015 demonstration of the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) led to increases in interhospital transfer of patients with large vessel occlusion stroke. We sought to characterize the associated evolution in stroke care regionalization.

METHODS: We used comprehensive California statewide all-payer administrative data from 2010 to 2021 to identify ischemic stroke encounters and transfers (using recorded disposition and adjacent claims). We applied network analysis methods to create the interhospital transfer network, examine access to EVT-capable hospitals (time-varying, based on performance of ≥2 EVT cases that year), and used block models to identify clusters of hospitals closely connected through transfer by year and pre- versus post-2015. We used regression modeling with a linear spline and knot at 2015 to examine changes in network characteristics over time.

RESULTS: We identified 19 244 transfers between 338 hospitals. Pre-2015, 7 of 11 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. Post-2015, 24 of 26 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. More hospitals had EVT capability over time (21.6% [70/324] to 33.7% [106/315]). EVT-capable hospitals consistently received more transferred patients relative to noncapable hospitals (mean number of received transfers/y pre-2015: 55.2 versus 15.6; post-2015: 97.3 versus 13.8). Initially, transfers for EVT increased from 10.7% of EVT cases having an interhospital transfer in 2010 to 36.0% by 2016. After 2016, the trend reversed, decreasing to 21.7% by 2021.

CONCLUSIONS: The California stroke system of care became less regionalized for EVT access from 2010 to 2021. Although we expected increased consolidation with fewer clusters centered around EVT-capable hospitals, we instead observed an increased number of EVT-capable hospitals with more clusters around them and less need for transfer to access EVT. More work is needed to examine the relative trade-offs of regionalization patterns in stroke systems of care, given recognized benefits of more regionalized care around higher-volume centers in other conditions.

title: Early endovascular salvage of acute inferior vena cava obstruction after liver transplantation.
abstract: Inferior vena cava obstruction following liver transplantation is rare but life-threatening. Although endovascular management has been described in delayed presentations, evidence supporting intervention in the immediate postoperative period remains limited. We report the case of a 43-year-old man with acute caval thrombosis and venous outflow obstruction following bicaval liver transplantation. Impending graft failure and hemodynamic instability prompted urgent endovascular intervention. Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy was performed. Two torsion-related stenotic segments persisted, and a self-expanding bare-metal venous stent was deployed, restoring caval flow. Early thrombectomy and stenting may offer effective salvage in select high-risk patients with acute caval obstruction.

Although endovascular management has been described in delayed presentations, evidence supporting intervention in the immediate postoperative period remains limited. title: Dichloroacetate mitigates experimental abdominal aortic aneurysm via suppression of CXCL5-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a life-threatening vascular disease with high rupture-associated mortality. Current management relies on surgical or endovascular repair, with no effective pharmacological therapy. Inflammation and immune cell infiltration are central to AAA pathogenesis, but the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined.

METHODS: Human AAA tissues and murine AAA models (CaCl2 and porcine pancreatic elastase) were analyzed for chemokine expression and immune cell infiltration. The role of CXCL5 was investigated using immunohistochemistry, RNA-seq, and flow cytometry. The pharmacological effects of dichloroacetate (DCA), a pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase inhibitor, were assessed in vitro in smooth muscle cells and in vivo in AAA models.

RESULTS: CXCL5 was markedly enriched in human AAA lesions and associated with neutrophil infiltration. In murine AAA, neutrophil accumulation was evident and correlated with CXCL5 expression. DCA treatment suppressed ROS generation and NF-κB activation in smooth muscle cells, thereby reducing CXCL5 expression. Functionally, DCA significantly attenuated AAA formation in both CaCl2- and elastase-induced models. Mechanistically, DCA mitigated AAA progression by inhibiting CXCL5-mediated neutrophil chemotaxis.

CONCLUSION: CXCL5-driven neutrophil recruitment is a key mechanism in AAA pathogenesis. DCA suppresses CXCL5 expression through inhibition of oxidative stress and NF-κB signaling, conferring protection against experimental AAA. These findings highlight CXCL5 as a potential therapeutic target and establish DCA as a promising candidate drug for AAA treatment.

Current management relies on surgical or endovascular repair, with no effective pharmacological therapy. Inflammation and immune cell infiltration are central to AAA pathogenesis, but the molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined.

title: Long-Term Azole Therapy After Subtotal Graft Removal for Trichosporon asahii Aortic Graft Infection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Trichosporonosis is a fatal opportunistic infection (mortality 30%-90%). Trichosporon aortic prosthetic graft infection has not been reported.

CASE SUMMARY: A 55-year-old immunocompetent man developed Trichosporon asahii aortic graft infection 3 months after type A dissection repair, presenting with fever and peripheral emboli. At redo total arch replacement, the infected woven polyester graft was excised, but the expanded polytetrafluoroethylene stent graft was too deep in the descending aorta to remove and was retained after debridement. Long-term azole therapy achieved control without recurrence over 2 years.

DISCUSSION: Diagnosis is difficult because culture-negative cases are not uncommon in prosthetic cardiovascular infection, and optimal management is undefined. The favorable outcome despite a retained expanded polytetrafluoroethylene segment may reflect its lower biofilm formation than woven polyester, though this remains speculative.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Consider T asahii in culture-negative graft infection. When explantation is unsafe, subtotal removal plus long-term azole therapy can be effective.

title: Endovascular Iliac Vein Revascularization Versus Conservative Management for Chronic, Symptomatic Iliac Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To synthesize the existing evidence comparing endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management for chronic, symptomatic venous obstruction.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparator-controlled studies of endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management. The primary outcome was the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS); secondary outcomes were the Villalta score, Venous Insufficiency Epidemiological and Economic Study Quality of Life (VEINES-QOL), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain. Continuous outcomes were pooled as mean differences (MD) using random-effects models with the Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman adjustment. Certainty was assessed with GRADE (PROSPERO CRD420261446246).

RESULTS: Four studies (three randomized trials, one cohort; 554 patients; n per outcome: VCSS 317, Villalta 479, VAS 267, VEINES-QOL 274) met eligibility. Revascularization reduced VCSS (MD - 2.24, 95% confidence interval [CI] - 3.86 to -0.63) and the Villalta score (MD - 3.48, 95% CI - 4.75 to - 2.21; both I2 = 0%). VAS pain and VEINES-QOL were inconclusive under the primary model. Technical success was 96.6%, stent thrombosis 1.9%. The largest trial showed threefold more bleeding (major and non-major, 11.6% vs. 3.6%), mainly non-major. Certainty was low for VCSS and Villalta and very low for VEINES-QOL and VAS pain.

CONCLUSION: Revascularization reduced venous symptom severity under the primary model, though neither estimate was robust to omitting individual studies, and the VCSS prediction interval crossed the null. Bleeding risk was increased in the largest trial; quality-of-life and pain effects were inconclusive. The evidence offers modest support for revascularization in patients failing conservative therapy, with short follow-up.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Cochrane CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov for comparator-controlled studies of endovascular iliac vein revascularization versus conservative management. The primary outcome was the Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS); secondary outcomes were the Villalta score, Venous Insufficiency Epidemiological and Economic Study Quality of Life (VEINES-QOL), and Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) pain.

title: Ascites and Hyponatremia.
abstract: Ascites and hyponatremia in cirrhosis both arise from portal hypertension-induced splanchnic vasodilation, leading to reduced effective arterial blood volume and neurohormonal activation. Ascites represents the most common decompensating event in cirrhosis and is associated with significant morbidity and mortality, while hyponatremia independently predicts poor prognosis and transplant outcomes. This article outlines evidence-based diagnostic strategies and stepwise management, including dietary modification, diuretics, paracentesis, transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt and transplant referral, as well as emerging therapies. These two conditions are interrelated, and multidisciplinary care is needed.

title: Aortoesophageal fistula resulting from the treatment of the "Corkscrew esophagus" by serial endoscopic botulinum toxin injections.
abstract: An aortoesophageal fistula (AEF) is a rare condition and invariably lethal if not diagnosed and treated promptly. These fistulae usually occur from erosion of unsuspected thoracic aortic aneurysms into the adjacent esophagus, ingestion of foreign bodies, or after aortic surgery but can also develop after aggressive treatment of esophageal motility disorders. We report the case of a 69-year-old woman who developed an AEF after serial endoscopic injections of botulinum toxin into the esophagus for treatment of distal esophageal spasm or the "Corkscrew esophagus." Guidelines for treatment of this rare, previously undescribed presentation of a secondary AEF are currently ill-defined.

title: The first decade of data from the Irish National Orthopaedic Register: trends in hip and knee arthroplasty, implant utilisation and patient outcomes.
abstract:
AIMS: The Irish National Orthopaedic Register (INOR) was established to monitor total hip (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) practice, implant utilisation and patient outcomes in Ireland following the recall of the Articular Surface Replacement (ASR) metal-on-metal implant. This study presents the first decade of INOR data (2015-2024) from participating hospitals, evaluating patterns in arthroplasty activity, implant fixation, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) and clinical outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective descriptive analysis of aggregated data from the INOR National Report (2015-2024) and accompanying appendices was performed, including demographics, procedural activity, implant utilisation, fixation strategies, PROMs (Oxford Hip Score [OHS], Oxford Knee Score [OKS], EQ-5D-5L) and clinical outcomes (30-day surgical site infection, dislocation, periprosthetic fracture, venous thromboembolism, mortality, and one-year revision).

RESULTS: A total of 43,291 arthroplasty procedures were recorded across 17 participating hospitals, including 22,249 primary THAs (51%), 18,102 primary TKAs (42%), 1,864 revision THAs (4%) and 1,076 revision TKAs (3%). Annual volume increased from 841 cases in 2015 to 10,266 in 2024. Cementless fixation in primary THA increased from 43% in 2015 to 71% in 2024. Mean OHS improved from 17.9 preoperatively to 44.0, and mean OKS from 19.5 to 40.5, at five years. Mean EQ-5D-5L improved from 0.265 to 0.818 following THA and from 0.364 to 0.793 following TKA at five years. The 30-day SSI rate was 0.5% for both THA and TKA; one-year revision occurred in 1.0% of THAs and 0.8% of TKAs, and 30-day mortality was 0.1% overall.

CONCLUSION: During its first decade, INOR expanded its capture of arthroplasty procedures and generated data on implant utilisation, PROMs and clinical outcomes among participating hospitals. Because of phased onboarding and incomplete national coverage, these findings reflect practice at participating institutions rather than a complete national picture, and revision rate estimates should be interpreted cautiously given incomplete denominator capture. As participation grows, INOR is positioned to support implant surveillance, quality improvement and evidence-based arthroplasty practice in Ireland.

title: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty for occlusive lesions of pulmonary artery in Takayasu arteritis: A cohort study.
abstract: BackgroundOcclusive pulmonary arterial lesions represent a major technical challenge for balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in patients with Takayasu arteritis-associated pulmonary artery involvement. However, evidence and procedural guidance regarding BPA for occlusive lesions in this population remain limited.ObjectivesThis study aimed to summarize our center experience with BPA for occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions in patients with Takayasu arteritis and to identify potential risk factors associated with restenosis after BPA.DesignRetrospective cohort.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled patients with Takayasu arteritis who had occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions. Lesions were morphologically categorized as subtotal or total occlusions. Total occlusions were further subclassified as cone-shaped, pouch-like, or ostial occlusions.ResultsWe included 66 patients with Takayasu arteritis, in whom 182 occlusive lesions were identified. In terms of locations, most ostial occlusions (56.52%) located lobar, while other kinds of lesions more common located segmentally. Total occlusions more frequently required guide-extension catheter support than subtotal occlusions (70.21% vs. 40.63%, P<0.001). Hard-tip guidewires were required for revascularization in 53.85% of ostial occlusions, compared with only 3.13% of subtotal occlusions. Lesion-level technical success rates among attempted lesions decreased with increasing lesion complexity: 100% for subtotal occlusions, 96.0% for cone-shaped occlusions, 68.4% for pouch-like occlusions, and 43.8% for ostial occlusions. The corresponding recanalization rates among all identified lesions were 78.69%, 88.9%, 52.04%, and 10.14%, respectively. In exploratory univariable Firth penalized logistic regression, irregular anticoagulation was associated with a higher likelihood of restenosis (OR 8.51, 95% CI 1.39-60.91; P=0.021), whereas baseline hemodynamics were not associated with restenosis.ConclusionThe techniques and devices illustrated in this study might guide the BPA performance in addressing occlusive lesions.

title: Antithrombotic use patterns for secondary stroke prevention in ischemic stroke patients with active malignancy: The STOP-SPAM study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cancer-associated stroke is increasingly recognized as a distinct ischemic stroke subtype linked to malignancy-related hypercoagulability. Optimal secondary prevention is uncertain, and antithrombotic practice varies. We examined treatment patterns and compared outcomes of anticoagulation versus antiplatelet therapy in patients with active cancer and ischemic stroke.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied adults with active malignancy and ischemic stroke at a single academic center (2015-2021). Patients were grouped by physician-selected antithrombotic regimen. Univariable logistic regression identified factors associated with anticoagulant use. Comparative effectiveness and safety were assessed with competing-risk survival analysis using inverse probability of treatment weighting. The primary outcome was recurrent ischemic stroke within 180 days.

RESULTS: Among 311 patients, 237 (76.2%) received antiplatelets and 69 (22.2%) anticoagulation. Anticoagulated patients more often had metastatic cancer, multi-territory infarction, and higher NIHSS. Metastatic disease (OR 8.39, 95% CI 3.86-18.25) and combined anterior/posterior circulation infarction (OR 5.77, 95% CI 3.23-10.31) were strongly associated with anticoagulant selection. After weighting, anticoagulation was associated with lower recurrent stroke risk at 180 days versus antiplatelets (sHR 0.31, 95% CI 0.19-0.52). Major bleeding (13.0% vs 5.1%), venous thromboembolism (23.2% vs 5.5%), and mortality (55.1% vs 25.7%) were higher with anticoagulation, likely reflecting greater disease burden.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinicians preferentially used anticoagulation in patients with features suggesting hypercoagulability. Anticoagulation was associated with lower recurrent stroke risk but higher bleeding rates. Prospective studies are needed to define optimal secondary prevention.

Optimal secondary prevention is uncertain, and antithrombotic practice varies. We examined treatment patterns and compared outcomes of anticoagulation versus antiplatelet therapy in patients with active cancer and ischemic stroke.

title: Clinical outcomes associated with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist therapy in patients with peripheral artery disease and diabetes.
abstract:
AIM: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) and diabetes are associated with high risks of limb complications and mortality. Although glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP1-RAs) improve cardiovascular outcomes, their effect on limb outcomes in PAD remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the Clalit Health Services database. Adults with PAD and diabetes were classified according to GLP1-RA dispensing exposure, and inverse probability of treatment weighting was used to balance measured baseline characteristics in the primary analysis. The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-limb revascularization or amputation. To address potential immortal time bias, all-cause mortality was additionally evaluated using an incident-treatment risk-set approach aligned to the qualifying GLP1-RA exposure date, while sustained GLP1-RA exposure was evaluated for MALE using a time-varying persistent-use model.

RESULTS: Among 20,031 patients, 5960 met the original GLP1-RA exposure definition and 14,071 were classified as non-users. In the original IPTW-weighted analysis, GLP1-RA exposure was associated with lower risks of MALE, revascularization, major amputation, and all-cause mortality. In the time-aligned risk-set analysis, GLP1-RA exposure remained associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.73-0.88; P < 0.001). In a time-varying analysis of sustained exposure, persistent GLP1-RA use was associated with a lower hazard of MALE (adjusted HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.44-0.94; P = 0.022).

CONCLUSION: In patients with PAD and diabetes, GLP1-RA exposure was associated with favorable clinical outcomes. Time-aligned analyses demonstrated a lower risk of all-cause mortality, while sustained GLP1-RA exposure was associated with lower MALE risk. Given the observational design, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal treatment effects.

title: Janus kinase inhibitor use in adults aged 65 years and older: A clinical review across atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata, and psoriasis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors are increasingly used as systemic therapies for inflammatory dermatoses, but adults aged 65 and older are underrepresented in their clinical trials.

OBJECTIVE: To synthesize the efficacy, safety, and regulatory evidence on JAK inhibitors in adults aged 65 and older with atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata, and psoriasis.

METHODS: Clinical review synthesizing phase 3 trials, integrated safety analyses, real-world cohorts, and Food and Drug Administration/European Medicines Agency labeling with age-stratified outcomes into practice recommendations (Supplementary Appendix 1B).

RESULTS: In atopic dermatitis, upadacitinib 15 mg and abrocitinib 100 mg are effective in older adults, with higher doses generally avoided. In alopecia areata, baricitinib shows efficacy in small older-adult cohorts, while ritlecitinib data in this age group remain too limited for age-specific conclusions. In psoriasis, deucravacitinib provides durable responses and avoids boxed warnings for major adverse cardiovascular events or venous thromboembolism, while catalytic JAK inhibitors for psoriatic arthritis need label-directed dosing and close monitoring.

CONCLUSION: JAK inhibitors may be a reasonable option for carefully selected older adults, but the decision should be a deliberate one. It rests on disease-specific efficacy, baseline cardiovascular and oncologic risk, modifiable comorbidities, label-directed dosing, and close monitoring. Age-stratified data remain sparse, and each decision should be individualized.

METHODS: Clinical review synthesizing phase 3 trials, integrated safety analyses, real-world cohorts, and Food and Drug Administration/European Medicines Agency labeling with age-stratified outcomes into practice recommendations (Supplementary Appendix 1B).

title: Prognostic Value of the Pan-Immune Inflammatory Value and Fibrinogen-To-Albumin Ratio for Amputation in Patients With Lower Extremity Arterial Disease.
abstract: BackgroundLower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) remains a major cause of amputation, even after successful endovascular revascularization therapy (EVT). The prognostic associations of the pan-immune inflammatory value (PIV) and fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) in LEAD remain unclear. This study investigated the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk and evaluated their incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical variables.MethodsIn this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 1,082 patients with LEAD who underwent EVT at four tertiary hospitals in Southwest China between January 2018 and July 2023 were analyzed. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk. Exploratory cut-off values were derived using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The incremental prognostic value of adding PIV and FAR to clinical variables was assessed using time-dependent ROC analysis.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 31 months, 198 (18.3%) patients experienced amputation. RCS revealed significant nonlinear associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk (p for nonlinearity < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, higher levels of both biomarkers remained independently associated with increased amputation risk (Z-PIV: HR = 1.379; Z-FAR: HR = 1.176; both p < 0.001). The addition of PIV and FAR to the clinical model enhanced time-dependent discrimination; the AUC(t) increased from 0.771 to 0.819 at 1 year, 0.766 to 0.806 at 2 years, and 0.762 to 0.807 at 3 years (all adjusted p < 0.001). Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses yielded consistent results after accounting for death as a competing event.ConclusionPIV and FAR were independently associated with amputation risk in patients with LEAD who underwent EVT. The addition of these biomarkers to established clinical variables provided incremental prognostic value and may offer additional prognostic information for risk stratification.

title: Uterine Artery Embolization Combined with Hysteroscopic Surgery for the Treatment of Complex Submucosal Leiomyomas with Refractory Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Submucosal uterine fibroids are a common structural cause of abnormal uterine bleeding in women of reproductive age. Transcervical resection of myoma (TCRM), as the standard procedure, still faces many challenges in the management of cases with rich blood supply or rapid growth.

CASE DATA: We report a case of a young nulliparous patient who developed recurrent acute massive haemorrhage one month after the initial TCRM due to complex submucosal fibroids, which failed to respond to medication. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated that branches of the left uterine artery directly supplied the lesion. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) was then performed, and a second TCRM was performed after embolization to achieve complete resection of the lesion. Review of the initial postoperative pathology revealed increased tumor cellularity with focal proliferative activity. The Ki-67 index in hot-spot areas was about 10%, indicating active cell proliferation. The final diagnosis was cellular leiomyoma. After nearly 6 months of follow-up, the patient's menstruation returned to normal, but long-term outcomes such as reproductive function still require longer-term follow-up.

CONCLUSION: This case indicates that the combination of UAE and TCRM achieves a favorable short‑term outcome in the treatment of hypervascular submucosal fibroids complicated with intractable acute hemorrhage. Given the limitations of the single‑case study and the relatively short follow‑up duration, the long‑term efficacy and fertility preservation outcomes remain to be further verified. Individualized clinical decision‑making and prolonged follow‑up are therefore recommended.

Transcervical resection of myoma (TCRM), as the standard procedure, still faces many challenges in the management of cases with rich blood supply or rapid growth. CASE DATA: We report a case of a young nulliparous patient who developed recurrent acute massive haemorrhage one month after the initial TCRM due to complex submucosal fibroids, which failed to respond to medication.

title: Age-dependent associations of peripheral immune-inflammatory indices with cerebrovascular remodeling after revascularization in ischemic moyamoya disease.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Peripheral immune-inflammatory activity may influence postoperative vascular remodeling in Moyamoya disease (MMD), but the relevant pathways may differ by developmental stage. We investigated age-dependent associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory indices with two complementary imaging outcomes: collateralization angiogenesis ratio (CAR) and arterial residual volume (ARV).

METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 108 patients with ischemic MMD who underwent revascularization (76 adults and 32 pediatric patients). Associations of neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), neutrophil-to-platelet ratio (NPR), and platelet-to-albumin ratio (PAR) with CAR and ARV were screened using Spearman correlations with Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Standardized multivariable linear models used HC3 robust standard errors and adjusted for age, sex, Suzuki stage, and follow-up. Effect modification was evaluated using cohort-by-marker and continuous age-by-marker interactions.

RESULTS: CAR and ARV did not differ between adults and pediatric patients (P = 0.583 and P = 0.853, respectively) and were uncorrelated within either cohort, supporting their interpretation as distinct remodeling dimensions. In unadjusted analyses, pediatric NPR correlated inversely with CAR (ρ=-0.431, P = 0.014), whereas adult PLR correlated inversely with ARV (ρ=-0.242, P = 0.035); neither association survived false-discovery-rate correction. After adjustment, pediatric NPR remained inversely associated with CAR (standardized β=-0.380, 95% CI -0.652 to -0.108; P = 0.006). The adult PLR-ARV association was borderline (β=-0.255, 95% CI -0.512 to 0.002; P = 0.052). PLR showed significant age-dependent effect modification: the PLR pediatric-cohort interaction was positive (β=0.547, 95% CI 0.112 to 0.981; P = 0.014), and the PLR continuous-age interaction was negative (β=-0.264, 95% CI -0.485 to -0.043; P = 0.019), indicating that the PLR-ARV relationship became more negative with increasing age.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory analysis, peripheral inflammatory indices were associated with different postoperative remodeling pathways according to developmental stage. The age-dependent PLR-ARV relationship was the most consistent interaction signal, whereas the adjusted pediatric NPR-CAR association suggests a potentially localized collateralization mechanism. However, these exploratory findings require validation in larger, prospectively characterized cohorts.

We investigated age-dependent associations of blood cell-derived inflammatory indices with two complementary imaging outcomes: collateralization angiogenesis ratio (CAR) and arterial residual volume (ARV). METHODS: This retrospective observational study included 108 patients with ischemic MMD who underwent revascularization (76 adults and 32 pediatric patients).

title: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta versus resuscitative thoracotomy in traumatic non-compressible torso hemorrhage: A structured narrative systematic review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-compressible torso hemorrhage (NCTH) is a leading cause of preventable trauma death. Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) has served as salvage intervention, while resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) has emerged as a less invasive alternative, though evidence remains discordant.

METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL through March 2026 for comparative studies of REBOA versus RT in adult NCTH patients. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I and RoB 2. A structured narrative synthesis was performed.

RESULTS: Thirteen studies were included (1 RCT, 12 observational; n ≈ 7942). Observational studies consistently associated REBOA with lower in-hospital mortality, though all were at serious or critical risk of bias from confounding (GRADE: very low). The UK-REBOA trial was stopped early for potential harm (posterior OR 1.58, 95% CrI 0.72-3.52).

CONCLUSION: Observational evidence associates REBOA with lower mortality, but this reflects confounding rather than causal benefit. Equipoise remains for randomized trials in patients with isolated infradiaphragmatic hemorrhage and preserved cardiac activity.

Resuscitative thoracotomy (RT) has served as salvage intervention, while resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) has emerged as a less invasive alternative, though evidence remains discordant. METHODS: Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane CENTRAL through March 2026 for comparative studies of REBOA versus RT in adult NCTH patients.

title: Effect of Surgical Subspecialty on Time to Development of Postoperative Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a major cause of surgical morbidity despite guideline-based prophylaxis. Whether VTE timing and thromboprophylaxis patterns differ across surgical subspecialties is incompletely characterized.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study of adults with imaging-confirmed postoperative VTE during the index admission within a multihospital healthcare system (2013 to 2019). VTE events were identified using natural language processing and confirmed by chart review. The primary outcome was time to postoperative VTE; the secondary outcome was time to thromboprophylaxis. Kaplan-Meier analyses and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models evaluated associations across surgical specialties.

RESULTS: Among 1,520 patients with postoperative VTE, 24.9% had deep vein thrombosis only, 67.2% pulmonary embolism only, and 7.9% both. Median time to VTE was 4 days (interquartile range 2.0 to 8.0); pulmonary embolism occurred earlier than deep vein thrombosis (3 vs 6 days; p < 0.001). Neurosurgery had the highest VTE incidence (0.23% of neurosurgical cases), whereas orthopaedic surgery demonstrated the highest adjusted hazard for postoperative VTE. Overall, 76% received postoperative thromboprophylaxis beginning a median of 1.3 days after surgery (interquartile range 0.8 to 1.7). Patients without thromboprophylaxis developed VTE earlier than those receiving prophylaxis (2.0 vs 4.0 days; p < 0.001). Cardiac surgery demonstrated the lowest adjusted likelihood of thromboprophylaxis, whereas thoracic surgery had the highest (hazard ratio 5.8, 95% CI 2.8 to 12.1; reference cardiac), and trauma patients were less likely to receive prophylaxis (hazard ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.34 to 0.57).

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative VTE risk, timing, and thromboprophylaxis practices vary substantially across surgical subspecialties. These findings support specialty-specific VTE risk assessment, prophylaxis strategies, and postoperative surveillance.

Whether VTE timing and thromboprophylaxis patterns differ across surgical subspecialties is incompletely characterized. title: Mechanisms and Management of Acquired Aseptic Intracardiac Communications After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation: Single-Center Case Series Insights.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acquired aseptic intracardiac communications (AICCs) are rare but clinically relevant structural complications following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), typically resulting from mechanical injury to the aortic annulus, interventricular septum, or adjacent structures. Evidence regarding their incidence, mechanisms, and optimal management remains limited.

AIM: To review the mechanisms and management of post-TAVI AICCs and to present a single-center experience focusing on multimodality imaging, procedural characteristics, and outcomes of transcatheter closure.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients diagnosed with AICCs after TAVI at our institution. Clinical characteristics, anatomical mechanisms, imaging findings, procedural details, and follow-up outcomes were evaluated. A complementary literature review was performed.

RESULTS: Four patients (mean age 74 years) developed iatrogenic intracardiac communications, including ventricular septal defects, aorto-right ventricular fistulas, and complex root injuries. Mechanisms included severe annular or subannular calcification, aggressive balloon dilation, and valve-in-valve procedures with frame fracture. Multimodality imaging using transthoracic and transesophageal echocardiography combined with cardiac computed tomography enabled precise anatomical characterization and procedural planning in all cases. Following Heart Team discussion, transcatheter closure achieved procedural success in all patients, with complete or functionally complete elimination of shunt flow and no major device-related complications. During follow-up ranging from 8 months to 2.5 years, all patients remained clinically stable without recurrence.

CONCLUSIONS: AICCs after TAVI are mechanism-driven complications requiring early recognition and individualized management. Multimodality imaging is central to diagnosis and procedural planning, and transcatheter closure represents a safe and effective first-line treatment in appropriately selected patients.

AIM: To review the mechanisms and management of post-TAVI AICCs and to present a single-center experience focusing on multimodality imaging, procedural characteristics, and outcomes of transcatheter closure.

title: Pulmonary embolism as the initial manifestation of steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome in an adolescent: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is uncommon in adolescents and often presents with non-specific symptoms, which may delay diagnosis. Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a recognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism; however, thromboembolic events may occasionally precede overt renal manifestations, creating additional diagnostic challenges.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 17-year-old male adolescent with steroid-responsive NS initially presenting with PE. The patient initially developed fever, cough, and abdominal pain, leading to a preliminary diagnosis of pneumonia and cholecystitis before PE was identified. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography revealed bilateral multiple pulmonary emboli. Laboratory evaluation showed hypoalbuminemia, but initial repeated urinalyses were negative for proteinuria and renal function was preserved. During hospitalization, the patient developed edema, acute kidney injury, and nephrotic-range proteinuria. No definite evidence of secondary NS was identified. Renal biopsy was not performed due to concurrent anticoagulation therapy and refusal from the patient's family. His symptoms improved after anticoagulation and glucocorticoid therapy, and there was no recurrence during a two-year follow-up.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights two important diagnostic challenges: PE should be considered even in adolescents with non-specific symptoms, and NS may remain clinically silent when thromboembolic events occur, particularly in patients with unexplained PE accompanied by hypoalbuminemia.

Nephrotic syndrome (NS) is a recognized risk factor for venous thromboembolism; however, thromboembolic events may occasionally precede overt renal manifestations, creating additional diagnostic challenges. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a case of a 17-year-old male adolescent with steroid-responsive NS initially presenting with PE.

title: Treatment and Prevention of Variceal Bleeding.
abstract: Variceal bleeding is a life-threatening complication of portal hypertension, though mortality has been dramatically reduced by advances in acute management and prophylaxis. Management of acute variceal bleeding includes vasoactive drugs, antibiotics, restrictive transfusion, and endoscopic therapy within 12 hours. Endovascular techniques such as transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt and retrograde transvenous obliteration may be required in select or refractory cases. Prevention of variceal bleeding entails identifying at-risk patients with clinically significant portal hypertension and decreasing portal pressure with nonselective beta blockers (preferably carvedilol). Less severe forms of portal hypertensive gastrointestinal bleeding include portal hypertensive gastropathy, enteropathy, and colopathy.

title: Paravertebral percutaneous embolization of isolated zone 3 endoleak after branched endovascular aortic arch repair.
abstract: A 78-year-old man with a zone 3 aortic aneurysm was treated with a thoracic branch endoprosthesis. Surveillance imaging showed an arterial-phase endoleak; despite sac stability, concern for a type I/III etiology prompted intervention. Under fusion guidance, the sac was accessed percutaneously with a needle inserted via a left T2 paravertebral trajectory. Intrasac angiography excluded aortic or subclavian communication and showed type II endoleak from a single collateral artery without spinal or cerebral perfusion. The cavity, collateral, and tract were embolized with n-butyl cyanoacrylate. One-month imaging showed endoleak resolution-an early technical success, though durability remains unestablished.

title: Mediation of the sex disparity in COVID-19 mortality by arterial and venous thromboembolism: a multicenter cohort study. The Dutch COVID & Thrombosis Coalition.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Previous studies have demonstrated a notable sex difference in COVID-19 mortality without a clear explanation. Concurrent thrombosis could underlie this sex disparity.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether differentially occurring venous and arterial thromboembolic events (VTEs and ATEs, respectively) explain the association between sex and mortality in patients with COVID-19.

METHODS: A multicenter cohort study in the Netherlands was conducted between February 2020 and May 2022. Suspected or confirmed patients with COVID-19 admitted to the ward or Intensive Care Unit (ICU) were included. All-cause mortality, VTE, and ATE were the primary outcomes. Counterfactual mediation analyses with a random intercept for center were performed to decompose the total effect of sex on mortality into the natural direct effect (ie, the effect of sex on mortality not operating through VTE/ATE) and the natural indirect effect (ie, the effect of sex on mortality mediated by VTE/ATE), and to estimate the proportion mediated (ie, the fraction of the total effect explained by VTE/ATE) through VTE and ATE.

RESULTS: In total, 3255 patients with COVID-19 were included. Females showed lower cumulative incidences of mortality (15% vs 22%), VTE (10 vs 16%), and ATE (1.4 vs 3%) than males. Females demonstrated lower odds ratios (ORs) for mortality (OR 0.59; 95% CI 0.49-0.72), VTE (OR 0.57; 95% CI 0.46-0.72), and ATE (OR 0.64; 95% CI 0.39-1.03) than males. Counterfactual mediation analyses showed that the proportions mediated were 7.95% (95% CI 3.01%-17.63%) for VTE and 3.28% (95% CI 0.42%-8.68%) for ATE, respectively.

CONCLUSIONS: The lower incidence of VTE and ATE in females explains the sex difference in mortality in hospitalized patients with COVID-19 only to a minor extent. Further investigation is warranted to unravel sex-related factors in COVID-19.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate whether differentially occurring venous and arterial thromboembolic events (VTEs and ATEs, respectively) explain the association between sex and mortality in patients with COVID-19.

title: [Imaging-Guided Percutaneous Superior Vena Cava Catheterization for Hemodialysis Access in Patients With Thoracic Central Vein Obstruction].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the safety and feasibility of percutaneous superior vena cava (SVC) catheterization in patients with thoracic central vein obstruction (TCVO) and to assess the accuracy of preprocedural multi-detector computed tomography venography (MDCTV) in predicting SVC puncture angles.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 106 patients who underwent percutaneous SVC catheterization for TCVO between January 2020 and December 2023. Patient baseline characteristics, surgical data, and follow-up information were collected. Preprocedural MDCTV images were analyzed using OsiriX, a medical imaging interpretation and processing software, to determine predicted puncture angles. A paired-sample t-test was used to examine the agreement between MDCTV-predicted puncture angle and the actual puncture angle measured by intraoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Technical success rates and perioperative complication rates were recorded, and catheter patency rates were assessed using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis.

RESULTS: Among the 106 patients, 78.3% (83/106) had type 2B TCVO and 19.8% (21/106) had type 3 TCVO. The technical success rate of the procedure was 100% (106/106), and the incidence of severe complications was 1.9% (2/106). There were no statistically significant differences between the preprocedural MDCTV-predicted and intraoperative DSA-measured puncture angles in the coronal plane (11.46° vs 11.37°, P = 0.977) or the sagittal plane (18.62° vs 17.12°, P = 0.848). Catheter patency rates were 98.1% at 14 days and 80% at 24 months.

CONCLUSION: Percutaneous SVC catheterization is a safe and effective vascular access salvage option for patients with TCVO when conventional vascular access options have been exhausted. Preprocedural MDCTV can effectively predict SVC puncture angles, providing an objective basis for preprocedural route planning, thereby reducing operative risks and improving technical success rates.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 106 patients who underwent percutaneous SVC catheterization for TCVO between January 2020 and December 2023. Patient baseline characteristics, surgical data, and follow-up information were collected.

title: Retropancreatic tunneling of femoral vein for supraceliac aorta to superior mesenteric artery bypass.
abstract: Durability of superior mesenteric artery bypass depends on inflow and conduit. The supraceliac aorta is typically unaffected by atherosclerosis, and when used for mesenteric bypass inflow, yields an antegrade, kink-resistant graft configuration. Femoral vein as conduit is infection-resistant and excellent in caliber. This report describes two men who underwent supraceliac aorta-to-superior mesenteric artery bypass with femoral vein routed through a retropancreatic tunnel-one with chronic mesenteric ischemia after failed revascularizations and one with visceral stenoses from aortitis. The grafts remained widely patent at 24 and 7 months. Supraceliac inflow with retropancreatic femoral vein is a feasible and possibly preferable method of mesenteric revascularization.

title: Prior-driven multimodal contrastive learning with Fourier cross-attention to detect aortic dissection in 3D non-contrast CT.
abstract: Accurate identification of aortic dissection (AD) in emergencies is clinically critical. Non-contrast CT (NC-CT), the standard emergency imaging for chest pain, has limited AD diagnostic sensitivity. We developed an anatomy prior-driven multimodal contrastive learning framework, extracting discriminative features from contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) and radiological reports to enhance NC-CT-based AD detection. Aortic segmentation and straightening focus analysis on relevant anatomy, while our tri-encoder architecture leverages Fourier cross-attention (core innovation) to co-extract spatial and frequency-domain features with hybrid contrastive-focal frequency loss. After pre-training, only NC-CT is needed for inference. Evaluated on 134 subjects (70 AD, 64 non-AD), our method achieved 0.955 accuracy and 0.983 AUC, outperforming 9 SOTA models. External validation showed 0.933 accuracy, with lumen segmentation reaching an average Dice score of 0.773. These results demonstrate that our method can advance AD detection and enable accurate true/false lumen localization using NC-CT alone.

Non-contrast CT (NC-CT), the standard emergency imaging for chest pain, has limited AD diagnostic sensitivity. We developed an anatomy prior-driven multimodal contrastive learning framework, extracting discriminative features from contrast-enhanced CT (CE-CT) and radiological reports to enhance NC-CT-based AD detection.

title: Covered stent placement in the management of superior vena cava lesions in hemodialysis patients: A retrospective study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Superior vena cava lesions represent a challenging complication of central venous catheter use in maintenance hemodialysis patients. While endovascular intervention is the first-line treatment, restenosis rates remain high with plain balloon angioplasty and bare-metal stents. Covered stents have emerged as a potential alternative, yet data on their long-term efficacy in this specific population are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To analyze the clinical characteristics of hemodialysis patients with SVC lesions and evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of covered stent placement in treating these lesions.

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: The chi-squared or Fisher's exact test was used for categorical variables. For continuous variables, normality was assessed by the Shapiro-Wilk test; normally distributed data were compared using Welch's t-test with Hedges' g and 95% CI, and non-normally distributed data using the Mann-Whitney U test with r values and 95% CI.

RESULTS: A total of 24 patients were included. The main clinical symptoms were facial edema, limb edema, catheter dysfunction, and AVF dysfunction. The lesions were characterized as stenosis in 16 patients (67%) and occlusion in eight patients (33%). Subgroup analysis revealed no significant difference in the number of catheterizations or in total catheter indwelling time between the stenosis and occlusion groups (P > 0.05). However, the occlusion group required more balloons during the intervention (P = 0.016). Complications included intraoperative vascular rupture and arrhythmia. The median follow-up time was 27 months (21, 41), an the primary patency rate of the target lesions was 100%.

CONCLUSION: The use of Viabahn covered stents for treating SVC lesions in hemodialysis patients significantly improved the primary patency rate of target lesions, enhances clinical outcomes, and prolonged patency duration.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Superior vena cava lesions represent a challenging complication of central venous catheter use in maintenance hemodialysis patients. While endovascular intervention is the first-line treatment, restenosis rates remain high with plain balloon angioplasty and bare-metal stents. Covered stents have emerged as a potential alternative, yet data on their long-term efficacy in this specific population are limited.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy With Cerebral Protection Device for Persistent Left Atrial Appendage Thrombus: A Case Report With Literature Review.
abstract: Left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombi may not resolve following anticoagulant therapy. Persistent LAA thrombi despite being on therapeutic anticoagulation is not uncommon, and management of such thrombus is challenging. A novel strategy for such patients is mechanical thrombectomy and LAA occlusion device placement along with cerebral protection device deployment. Nevertheless, further investigation is needed to validate this emerging strategy.

title: Engineering Human Blood Vessel Organoids for Failed Ischemic Repair in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) remains a major cause of nonhealing wounds, tissue loss, amputation, and death despite advances in revascularization. This Review reframes CLTI as failed ischemic vascularized-tissue repair and evaluates how human vascular models can reproduce disease-specific repair failure and test regenerative interventions.

METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human CLTI with experimental studies of human blood vessel organoids (BVOs), engineered perfusable microvessels, vascular-on-chip systems, and vascularized tissue models. Direct CLTI observations are distinguished from mechanisms inferred from related ischemic, metabolic, and inflammatory systems. Model requirements and readouts are organized around disease-specific pathological benchmarks.

RESULTS: The synthesis indicates that restoration of macroscopic blood flow may be insufficient when microvascular maturation, tissue perfusion, and reparative remodeling remain defective. CLTI-oriented platforms should therefore reproduce sustained hypoperfusion, heterogeneous hypoxia, metabolic dysfunction, persistent inflammation, diabetes-associated microvascular injury, extracellular-matrix remodeling, and failed vascular maturation. BVOs are best positioned as the vascular core of modular ischemic-limb systems integrated, when required, with skeletal-muscle, wound, stromal, immune, matrix, and neural compartments. The hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF)-lactate-lactylation relationship is presented as a proposed, testable framework connecting oxygen sensing, glycolytic remodeling, lactate accumulation, endothelial and immune plasticity, and unstable vascular repair. A platform-specific roadmap combines patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells, microfluidic perfusion, multicellular coculture, multi-omic profiling, and structural, maturation, functional, durability, and tissue-repair endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: BVO-based and perfusion-enabled vascular platforms can support mechanistic validation, therapeutic and toxicity screening, patient-specific modeling, and vascularized construct design, provided that structural angiogenesis is distinguished from functional and durable tissue rescue.

This Review reframes CLTI as failed ischemic vascularized-tissue repair and evaluates how human vascular models can reproduce disease-specific repair failure and test regenerative interventions. METHODS: This narrative review synthesizes evidence from human CLTI with experimental studies of human blood vessel organoids (BVOs), engineered perfusable microvessels, vascular-on-chip systems, and vascularized tissue models.

title: From backbone to bedside: Nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury care.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) represents one of the most severe forms of central nervous system damage and has profound effects on the physical, psychological and social wellbeing of affected individuals. Patients with SCI are particularly vulnerable to secondary complications such as pressure ulcers, deep vein thrombosis and urinary tract infections. Nurses play a pivotal role in the prevention and management of these complications.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate nurses' knowledge and attitudes before and after implementation of a digital educational application focused on the care of patients with SCI.

METHODS: This prospective, two-phase study was conducted between January 2023 and July 2024. During the first phase (January - May 2023), 86 nurses employed in the intensive care unit (ICU), emergency department and rehabilitation centre completed a structured 21-item questionnaire assessing baseline knowledge and attitudes. During the second phase (May - July 2024), the same nurses were reassessed using the same questionnaire following a digital educational intervention. Statistical significance was set at p<0.05.

RESULTS: The findings demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in nurses' knowledge and attitudes following the intervention. Notable improvements were observed in areas related to complication prevention, the use of assistive devices, caregiver education, nutrition, bowel management and remaining informed about updates in patient care. Statistically significant correlations were identified between improvement and both department of employment and level of education. Nurses working in the ICU showed the greatest improvement (phase 1 v. phase 2: 3.1 v. 4.1), while nurses with postgraduate education also demonstrated statistically significant improvement (p=0.007).

CONCLUSION: The digital educational application was effective in enhancing nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding the care of patients with SCI. Continuous education, particularly within specialised clinical settings, is essential for optimising patient outcomes and maintaining high standards of care.

CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated nurses' knowledge and attitudes regarding spinal cord injury (SCI) care across intensive care, emergency and rehabilitation settings, and tested whether a low-cost, custom-built digital educational application could improve these outcomes. The intervention was associated with significant improvements in knowledge and attitudes, particularly around complication prevention, caregiver education and psychosocial support, with the largest gains seen among ICU nurses and those with postgraduate qualifications. These findings support digital training tools as an accessible way to strengthen nursing capacity for SCI care, especially where structured in-person continuing education is difficult to sustain.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Spinal cord injury (SCI) represents one of the most severe forms of central nervous system damage and has profound effects on the physical, psychological and social wellbeing of affected individuals. Patients with SCI are particularly vulnerable to secondary complications such as pressure ulcers, deep vein thrombosis and urinary tract infections. Nurses play a pivotal role in the prevention and management of these complications.

title: Bleeding complications in critically ill COVID‑19 patients receiving anticoagulation in a tertiary hospital intensive care unit.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease‑2019 (COVID‑19) is associated with a heightened inflammatory response, leading to thromboembolic events that influence patient outcomes. Complex anticoagulation strategies are often required to mitigate these complications. However, severe illness combined with such strategies may be associated with bleeding at multiple sites.

OBJECTIVES: To describe the incidence of bleeding and venous thromboembolism (VTE) in critically ill COVID‑19 patients receiving anticoagulation. Secondary objectives were to determine the incidence of transfusion in bleeding patients, and the association between inflammatory markers, coagulation parameters, and bleeding and/or VTE. Length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay and patient outcomes in the same cohort were also investigated.

METHODS: Participants included adult patients with confirmed COVID‑19 by positive polymerase chain reaction (PCR), admitted to the ICU from 1 April 2020 to 30 April 2021. A p‑value of <0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS: The study population comprised 103 patients. The anticoagulant of choice was low‑molecular‑weight heparin at therapeutic doses (median 80 mg/day). Bleeding occurred in 39.8% (n=41) of patients, predominantly from the oral mucosa (20.4%; n=21) and the gastrointestinal tract (13.6%; n=14). Of the patients who bled, 46.3% (n=19) received blood transfusions. Two patients (1.9%) developed grade 1 deep vein thrombosis. The median length of ICU stay was 7 days. Survival dropped below 50% (n=51) after 10 days of admission, and 25% (n=25) of patients survived beyond 28 days. Overall mortality was high at 65.0% (n=67).

CONCLUSION: COVID‑19‑positive critically ill patients receiving therapeutic anticoagulation exhibited an increased incidence of bleeding, accompanied by a high mortality rate.

CONTRIBUTION OF THE STUDY: This study provides South African data demonstrating a high burden of bleeding among critically ill patients with COVID‑19 receiving therapeutic anticoagulation. Bleeding risk was not explained by anticoagulation intensity alone but was associated with markers of thrombo‑inflammatory disease severity. These findings highlight the complex coexistence of thrombotic and haemorrhagic risks in severe COVID‑19 and challenge a simplistic approach to anticoagulation based solely on anticoagulant exposure. The study supports the need for individualised, dynamic, risk stratified anticoagulation strategies that incorporate clinical status, inflammatory markers and platelet trends.

Complex anticoagulation strategies are often required to mitigate these complications. However, severe illness combined with such strategies may be associated with bleeding at multiple sites.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative contemporary benchmarks: Varicose vein treatments.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous ablation is the main procedural treatment of patients with varicose veins. This study provides benchmark outcomes and utilization trends for thermal and nonthermal ablations for patients with varicose veins undergoing initial treatment in the Vascular Quality Initiative registry.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative Varicose Veins Registry was queried for patients treated between 2014 and 2025 at a truncal vein with no previous varicose venous treatment. Patients were stratified by index intervention into thermal or nonthermal ablation groups. Primary outcomes included improvement in Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS) and patient-reported outcomes assessed by Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI).

RESULTS: Among 44,883 patients undergoing 71,889 procedures, 38,978 (86.8%) were treated with ablation as the primary procedure. Thermal ablation declined from 91.5% to 53.0% of procedures (P < .001), whereas nonthermal ablation increased from 0% to 30.9% (P < .001) over the duration of the study. Ligation and stripping increased in the registry but remained low (0%-2.3%; P < .001). After exclusions, 23,598 patients undergoing initial truncal vein ablation were analyzed, including 21,920 (92.9%) thermal and 1678 (7.1%) nonthermal ablation. Patients undergoing thermal ablation were younger, had lower body mass index, had fewer previous deep vein thromboses, were less likely to receive pre-/perioperative anticoagulation, and more often had deep venous reflux. Patients treated with nonthermal ablations were more likely to be male and had more baseline ulceration but lower baseline HASTI scores, underwent fewer concomitant procedures, and more frequently underwent treatment of truncal veins other than the great saphenous vein. Thermal ablation had fewer systemic complications (0.3% vs 0.7%; P = .007), whereas local complication rates were similar between groups. Thermal ablation produced greater mean improvements in VCSS (-4.3 vs -3.2; P < .001) and HASTI (-6.9 vs -3.8; P < .001) post-treatment. In addition, a higher proportion of patients treated with thermal ablation reported improvement in VCSS (83.9% vs 74.6%; P < .001) and HASTI (86.3% vs 71.3%; P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Venous ablations improve symptoms of venous insufficiency in the majority of patients treated as measured by clinical severity scores and patient-reported outcomes. Complications are minor and infrequent regardless of the ablation modality.

This study provides benchmark outcomes and utilization trends for thermal and nonthermal ablations for patients with varicose veins undergoing initial treatment in the Vascular Quality Initiative registry. METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative Varicose Veins Registry was queried for patients treated between 2014 and 2025 at a truncal vein with no previous varicose venous treatment.
