title: Management of portomesenteric vein thrombosis following bariatric surgery.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) is a rare complication of bariatric surgery that can lead to cavernous transformation of the portal vein. There are no established treatment algorithms regarding anticoagulation (AC) only vs. catheter-directed thrombolysis in this population.

METHODS: Medical records at 4 urban bariatric surgery centers were queried for patients diagnosed with PMVT between 2012 and 2025. Patient characteristics, perioperative details, imaging at PMVT diagnosis, treatment course, and follow-up imaging were reviewed. Fisher's exact testing was conducted to identify correlations between extent of thrombosis, treatment course (anticoagulation vs. interventional radiology [IR] thrombolysis), and the outcome of cavernous transformation.

RESULTS: 71 patients were diagnosed with PMVT following bariatric surgery (68 LSG, 3 RYGB) at 4 centers between 2012 and 2025. Median time from surgery to PMVT diagnosis was 13 days. Three patients (4%) required reoperation for small bowel resection, of whom 2 underwent open thrombectomy and 1 underwent subsequent IR thrombolysis. Of the remaining patients, 6/68 (9%) underwent IR catheter-directed thrombolysis, and 62/68 (91%) received AC only. Of 53 patients with long-term data, 18 (34%) developed cavernous transformation. Among patients who had a main portal vein + intrahepatic portal vein + inflow (superior mesenteric vein or splenic vein) thrombosis, treatment with AC only was strongly associated with cavernous transformation (13/17, 76%) vs IR (1/5, 20%, p < 0.05). There were no deaths related to PMVT.

CONCLUSIONS: In this largest known case series of postbariatric surgery PMVT treated with anticoagulation vs. IR, we found that the PMVT clot pattern with the highest risk of developing cavernous transformation was the extensive type involving the main portal vein, an intrahepatic portal vein, and an inflow vein, whether the main portal vein clot was occlusive or nonocclusive. Early IR intervention was associated with decreased cavernous transformation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) is a rare complication of bariatric surgery that can lead to cavernous transformation of the portal vein. There are no established treatment algorithms regarding anticoagulation (AC) only vs. catheter-directed thrombolysis in this population.

title: Advancing practical skills and improving confidence in high-acuity, low-occurrence operative trauma using high-fidelity operative simulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Advancing endovascular approaches and subspecialty vascular care have significantly diminished general surgery residents' exposure to essential trauma techniques, creating a preparedness gap among graduates managing basic trauma emergencies. The Open Surgical Simulation System is a high-fidelity trauma surgery model enabling skill acquisition through hands-on practice. This study evaluates the outcomes of our curriculum development process and its impact on training outcomes.

METHODS: A longitudinal analysis of Open Surgical Simulation System simulation training was conducted from 2020 to 2026, encompassing multiple iterations of curriculum refinement based on continuous evaluation and feedback. The curriculum incorporated Kern-guided improvements in instructional design, implementation, and evaluation throughout the study period. Training outcomes were assessed using presimulation and postsimulation surveys with 5-point Likert scales measuring self-assessed knowledge, technical skills, and confidence across 6 procedures: resuscitative thoracotomy, exploratory laparotomy, splenectomy, hepatorrhaphy, small bowel resection, and retroperitoneal exploration. Paired t tests evaluated presimulation to postsimulation improvements across the full development period.

RESULTS: A total of 456 training events were conducted during the curriculum development period, of which 364 included complete paired pretraining and post-training assessments for analysis. The Open Surgical Simulation System curriculum consistently demonstrated significant improvements in confidence scores across all evaluated procedures (P < .001). Prior completion of Advanced Trauma Operative Management or Advanced Surgical Skills for Exposure in Trauma courses did not affect baseline confidence levels, and meaningful gains were observed across all trauma procedures.

CONCLUSION: Systematic development of the Open Surgical Simulation System curriculum using Kern's model enabled iterative curriculum refinement and successful geographic expansion while maintaining positive training outcomes. This simulation-based approach improved resident self-reported confidence across trauma procedures and supports the value of iterative curriculum development in addressing documented gaps in trauma surgery training.

The Open Surgical Simulation System is a high-fidelity trauma surgery model enabling skill acquisition through hands-on practice. This study evaluates the outcomes of our curriculum development process and its impact on training outcomes.

title: Patient and Clinician Perspectives on Postpartum Thromboembolism Risk and Pharmacologic Thromboprophylaxis Use: A Qualitative Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk is highest after delivery, and many hospitals recommend pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis during this period. There is a paucity of data on patient counselling received and clinician counselling provided on VTE risk and thromboprophylaxis. We aimed to determine information needs, perspectives and priorities regarding postpartum VTE risk communication and thromboprophylaxis education among people undergoing caesarean delivery and their obstetric clinicians.

DESIGN: Qualitative study.

SETTING: Single academic medical centre.

POPULATION: Postpartum individuals after caesarean delivery and obstetric clinicians.

METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were completed virtually by trained personnel with individuals within 12 weeks postpartum and obstetric clinicians to explore: (1) patient information needs on VTE risk communication; (2) perspectives on pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis; and (3) outcome priorities for decision-making around VTE and future research. Transcribed interviews were imported into a qualitative analytics software program. A standardized inductive coding framework was used in duplicate to identify themes.

MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: Qualitative data.

RESULTS: Fifteen patients and 10 obstetric clinicians were interviewed. Patients were educated on the risk for VTE after caesarean delivery and rationale for thromboprophylaxis. Although patients reported discomfort (e.g., bruising, injection site pain) from prophylaxis administration, they reflected a willingness to use this therapy to reduce their risk of VTE and protect themselves. Patients identified some gaps in knowledge, opportunities for enhanced materials for education and willingness to participate in research. Clinicians endorsed providing counselling on VTE risk and thromboprophylaxis but identified barriers and recognized uncertainties on optimal management. Clinicians valued research that will improve evidence-based guidelines.

CONCLUSIONS: While routine education on VTE risk and thromboprophylaxis is being provided, there are opportunities to improve communication. Patients and clinicians alike identified the necessity of research to inform precise individualized VTE risk estimates and the efficacy and risks of thromboprophylaxis.

There is a paucity of data on patient counselling received and clinician counselling provided on VTE risk and thromboprophylaxis. We aimed to determine information needs, perspectives and priorities regarding postpartum VTE risk communication and thromboprophylaxis education among people undergoing caesarean delivery and their obstetric clinicians.

title: Endoscopic ultrasound vascular parameter-based stratification for precise treatment of esophagogastric varices: a study on endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue glue obliteration.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To establish a hierarchical model based on endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) vascular parameters for predicting outcomes following EUS‑guided tissue glue obliteration in patients with esophagogastric varices (EGV), and to develop a precise treatment strategy.

METHODS: Clinical and EUS data from 56 patients with F2-F3 EGV were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified into mild, moderate, and severe abnormality groups according to EUS‑derived vascular parameters. The primary outcome was rebleeding within 12 months. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent risk factors. Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling and cross‑validation. The incremental predictive value of the stratification system was assessed using net reclassification improvement (NRI).

RESULTS: The overall rebleeding rate at 12 months was 25.00%, with a stepwise increase across the mild (5.56%), moderate (28.00%), and severe (46.15%) groups (P = 0.033). The variceal remission rate at 6 months showed a corresponding inverse gradient (83.33%, 64.00%, and 38.46%, respectively; P = 0.036). Portal vein flow velocity was identified as an independent protective factor against rebleeding (OR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.84, P = 0.009). The stratification system demonstrated incremental predictive value beyond Child-Pugh, MELD, and Baveno criteria (NRI = 0.243, P < 0.001). Internal validation confirmed model stability without overfitting (optimism‑corrected AUC = 0.88).

CONCLUSIONS: The EUS‑based vascular parameter stratification system effectively predicts rebleeding risk and treatment outcomes in patients with EGV undergoing endoscopic therapy. Portal vein flow velocity is a key independent predictor. This stratification approach may serve as a practical tool to guide individualized treatment decisions, though external validation in larger cohorts is warranted.

METHODS: Clinical and EUS data from 56 patients with F2-F3 EGV were retrospectively analyzed. Patients were classified into mild, moderate, and severe abnormality groups according to EUS‑derived vascular parameters.

title: Interpretable machine learning analysis for predicting the instability of the distal false lumen after thoracic endovascular aortic repair in type B aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The instability of the distal false lumen (FL) is a serious complication after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD). This study aimed to construct a prediction model to predict the risk of instability of the distal FL after TEVAR for TBAD at an early stage.

METHODS: We retrospectively collected the demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristic information of patients with TBAD who received TEVAR between July 2014 and August 2023. The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) and multiple logistic regression were used to screen predictive variables. Then, four machine learning models were constructed using the screened features, and these models were validated using bootstrap re-samples. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), decision curve analysis (DCA), calibration curve analysis, and the area under the Precision-Recall (PR) curve (PRAUC) were used to compare the performance of the models. SHapley Additive ex Planations (SHAP) was used to explain the best model.

RESULTS: The analysis ultimately included 202 TBAD patients who received TEVAR, among whom 34 (16.83%) patients experienced instability of the distal FL. The predictors in the final model included age, the length of residual FL (LRFL), and preoperative lymphocyte percentage. The Random Forest (RF) model demonstrated the best predictive performance, with AUC and PRAUC of 0.923 (95% CI: 0.861-0.974) and 0.801 (95% CI: 0.655-0.914) respectively. SHAP analysis indicated that the anatomical index of LRFL was the most crucial feature in the prediction model.

CONCLUSION: The RF model constructed in this study can effectively predict the instability of the distal FL after TEVAR in patients with TBAD, which may help clinicians develop personalized treatment and postoperative monitoring plans based on the characteristics of patients to improve the prognosis of TBAD.

CLINICAL IMPACT: The unstable expansion of the distal false lumen is an important cause of poor prognosis after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) in patients with Stanford type B aortic dissection (TBAD). Early identification of high-risk patients is crucial for optimizing treatment and follow-up strategies. The prediction model constructed in this study can help clinicians evaluate the risk of instability of distal false lumen in patients in the early stage after TEVAR, and it has a certain degree of interpretability.

This study aimed to construct a prediction model to predict the risk of instability of the distal FL after TEVAR for TBAD at an early stage. METHODS: We retrospectively collected the demographic, clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristic information of patients with TBAD who received TEVAR between July 2014 and August 2023.

title: Risk prediction model for lower extremity artery bailout stenting based on machine learning and CT radiomics.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To explore radiomics features derived from preoperative lower extremity arterial CT angiography (CTA) images and develop a machine learning model to predict the risk of bailout stenting in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) undergoing endovascular treatment. Furthermore, to enhance the model's interpretability using the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method.

METHODS: We retrospectively collected clinical and imaging data from 118 lower extremity patients who underwent femoropopliteal arterial intervention at our hospital from January 2020 to December 2025. Patients were divided into a balloon-only group and a stent group based on whether a stent was implanted. We used the LASSO regression algorithm to screen for key radiomics features, and systematically compared the predictive performance of eight mainstream machine learning algorithms, including Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and XGBoost. Model performance was evaluated using 5-fold nested cross-validation, and the SMOTE oversampling technique was introduced to address the issue of class imbalance. Based on the optimal model, we constructed a fusion model incorporating both clinical features, and employed the SHAP method to interpret the model's decision-making mechanism.

RESULTS: The Random Forest model demonstrated the best overall performance among all algorithms, achieving an AUC of 0.894 (95% CI 0.841-0.939) for predicting bailout stenting. It also yielded the lowest Brier score (0.12) and exhibited the optimal calibration curve. Furthermore, both the SVM (AUC = 0.886) and XGBoost (AUC = 0.882) models showed favorable generalization capabilities. Notably, the combined model incorporating clinical features (lesion type and TASC classification) maintained highly robust predictive performance (AUC = 0.893), confirming the independent value of radiomics features in capturing the micro-heterogeneity of plaques. SHAP analysis further revealed that high-order texture features were the most critical biomarkers driving the model's predictions.

CONCLUSION: The Random Forest model based on CT imaging radiomics can non-invasively and accurately predict the risk of bailout stenting in lower extremity arterial intervention. However, given the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size, these findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating. The model requires external validation before it can be considered for real-world decision support.

Furthermore, to enhance the model's interpretability using the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method. METHODS: We retrospectively collected clinical and imaging data from 118 lower extremity patients who underwent femoropopliteal arterial intervention at our hospital from January 2020 to December 2025.

title: Early cardiopulmonary adaptation following arteriovenous fistula creation in pre-dialysis chronic kidney disease patients: a prospective echocardiographic study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation induces substantial haemodynamic alterations through increased venous return and reduced systemic vascular resistance. Although cardiovascular remodelling after AVF creation has been described in haemodialysis populations, prospective echocardiographic data in pre-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients remain limited.

METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled adult pre-dialysis CKD patients undergoing elective AVF creation at the University of Malaya Medical Centre between March 2021 and December 2022. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed before AVF creation, at early follow-up (4-12 weeks), and at late follow-up ( ≥ ≥ 6 months). Parameters assessed included left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), left ventricular end-systolic volume (LVESV), left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), stroke volume (SV), left ventricular mass index (LVMI), cardiac index (CI), pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), and right ventricular functional indices. Paired analyses were performed using paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests according to normality of paired differences.

RESULTS: Thirty-four patients underwent baseline echocardiography, with 27 completing early follow-up and 14 completing late follow-up. Mean age was 65.2 ± 8.9 years, and 52.9% were male. At early follow-up, LVEDV increased from 79.8 ± 21.8 mL to 104.8 ± 32.0 mL (mean difference + 25.0 mL, 95% confidence interval 11.1-39.0; p = 0.001), and LVESV increased from 29.4 ± 10.5 mL to 37.5 ± 15.5 mL (mean difference + 8.1 mL, 95% confidence interval 2.1-14.1; p = 0.012). SV increased from 50.5 ± 13.5 mL to 66.2 ± 21.0 mL (mean difference + 15.8 mL, 95% confidence interval 6.5-24.9; p = 0.002), accompanied by an increase in cardiac index (CI) from 2.18 ± 0.65 to 3.05 ± 1.15 L/min/m² (mean difference + 0.87 L/min/m², 95% confidence interval 0.28-1.46; p = 0.007). LVEF remained preserved throughout follow-up. PASP increased from 28.0 ± 8.6 mmHg to 34.2 ± 9.9 mmHg (mean difference + 6.2 mmHg, 95% confidence interval 0.7-11.7; p = 0.032), while TAPSE also increased. Patients with proximal AVFs demonstrated greater PASP increases than those with distal AVFs.

CONCLUSIONS: AVF creation induces early cardiopulmonary adaptation in pre-dialysis CKD patients, characterised by increased LV volume loading, augmented cardiac output, and increased pulmonary haemodynamic burden while preserving systolic function. Proximal AVFs may confer greater pulmonary circulatory burden, supporting selective cardiovascular surveillance in higher-risk patients, although larger studies are needed to confirm these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation induces substantial haemodynamic alterations through increased venous return and reduced systemic vascular resistance. Although cardiovascular remodelling after AVF creation has been described in haemodialysis populations, prospective echocardiographic data in pre-dialysis chronic kidney disease (CKD) patients remain limited. METHODS: This prospective observational study enrolled adult pre-dialysis CKD patients undergoing elective AVF creation at the University of Malaya Medical Centre between March 2021 and December 2022.

title: The crab technique for complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal external carotid artery: a case report.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is an established treatment for carotid artery stenosis. However, complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal external carotid artery (ECA) may increase the technical difficulty of conventional CEA. We describe the Crab technique, a modified CEA approach combining proximal ECA exposure, concomitant endarterectomy, and Y-shaped patch reconstruction.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 68-year-old man with severe right carotid bifurcation stenosis underwent the Crab technique. Preoperative computed tomography angiography showed severe stenosis at the origin of the right internal carotid artery with concomitant proximal ECA involvement. The procedure included extended arteriotomy onto the proximal ECA, direct common, internal, and external carotid endarterectomy, and reconstruction with a surgeon-modified Y-shaped patch. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged without neurologic or wound-related complications.

CONCLUSIONS: The Crab technique may represent a technically feasible modification of conventional CEA in selected patients with complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal ECA. It allows direct plaque removal and bifurcation-oriented reconstruction while preserving the native anatomy. However, its safety, durability, and appropriate indications require further evaluation in larger case series with longer imaging follow-up.

However, complex carotid bifurcation disease involving the proximal external carotid artery (ECA) may increase the technical difficulty of conventional CEA. We describe the Crab technique, a modified CEA approach combining proximal ECA exposure, concomitant endarterectomy, and Y-shaped patch reconstruction.

title: Aorto-Uni-Iliac Versus Bifurcated Endograft Configuration for Endovascular Repair of Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To compare perioperative outcomes between aorto-uni-iliac (AUI) and bifurcated (BIF) endograft configurations in patients undergoing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) for ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA).

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for studies comparing AUI and BIF endografts in the treatment of rAAA. A total of 373 studies were screened in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Pooled analyses were performed using random-effects meta-analysis, and effect sizes were reported as risk ratios (RRs) or mean differences with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Statistical significance was defined as P < 0.05. Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Six cohort studies comprising 799 patients (23.5% female) were included, of whom 243 (30.4%) underwent EVAR with an AUI configuration. There was no statistically significant difference between AUI and BIF groups in 30-day mortality (RR, 1.62; 95% CI, 0.89-2.97), postoperative myocardial infarction, abdominal compartment syndrome, dialysis requirement, conversion to open repair, or operative time. Sensitivity analyses demonstrated that exclusion of individual studies altered the pooled effect estimate for 30-day mortality, favoring BIF configuration.

CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing EVAR for rAAA, perioperative outcomes did not differ significantly between AUI and BIF endograft configurations. Although sensitivity analyses favored BIF, the overall findings suggest that graft configuration alone may play a limited role in determining rAAA surgical outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for studies comparing AUI and BIF endografts in the treatment of rAAA. A total of 373 studies were screened in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines.

title: Robot‑assisted versus open radical nephrectomy and venous tumor thrombectomy: perioperative and oncologic outcomes-an inverse probability of treatment weighting analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Open radical nephrectomy and venous thrombectomy (ORN‑VT) is standard for renal cell carcinoma with tumor thrombus (RCC-TT), but robot‑assisted radical nephrectomy and venous thrombectomy (RARN‑VT) may improve outcomes. We used inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) to compare perioperative and oncologic results.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 418 patients (239 RARN‑VT, 179 ORN‑VT) treated at a high‑volume center between 2014 and 2025. IPTW balanced 19 baseline covariates using the covariate balancing propensity score method. Weighted regression was used for perioperative outcomes, and weighted Cox regression for progression‑free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). Propensity score matching (PSM) and an overlapping time‑period analysis (2020-2025) were performed as sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: After IPTW, all covariates were well balanced. RARN‑VT was associated with significantly shorter operation time (β = - 91.63), less estimated blood loss (β = - 885.05), lower transfusion volume (β = - 561.32), shorter length of stay (β = - 2.79), and reduced odds of blood transfusion (OR = 0.26) and any postoperative complication (OR = 0.44) (all P < 0.001). PFS showed no significant difference between approaches (log‑rank P > 0.05). Both sensitivity analyses confirmed the association between RARN‑VT and better perioperative outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: For RCC and TT patients, RARN‑VT was associated with improved perioperative outcomes. Prospective or randomized studies are warranted to further explore the oncological equivalence or superiority of the robotic approach.

title: Subscapular hepatic hematoma and extensive venous thrombosis associated with suspected fascioliasis: a case report from Ethiopia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fascioliasis, a zoonotic infection caused by Fasciola hepatica, is endemic in parts of Ethiopia. While hepatobiliary symptoms are common, vascular complications such as portal vein thrombosis (PVT) and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are rarely reported. We describe a case of suspected fascioliasis presenting with a large hepatic subcapsular hematoma, PVT, and extensive DVT in a patient from a rural endemic area with a history of sheep farming.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 58-year-old woman from a rural highland area of Ethiopia, with a history of sheep farming and frequent consumption of inadequately cleaned raw vegetables, initially presented with progressive right lower limb swelling due to proximal deep vein thrombosis (DVT). One month later, despite therapeutic anticoagulation, she developed severe right upper quadrant abdominal pain and symptoms of anemia. Triphasic abdominal computed tomography (CT) revealed a large right hepatic subcapsular hematoma (approximately 732 mL), multifocal intraparenchymal lesions, portal vein thrombosis, and extension of thrombosis to the right external and common iliac veins. No serological testing for Fasciola hepatica was performed, and repeated stool examinations for eggs were negative. Persistent eosinophilia (peaking at 32.7%), combined with her occupational exposure to sheep and dietary history, raised strong clinical suspicion for fascioliasis despite repeatedly negative stool examinations. She was managed with blood transfusion, careful anticoagulation, and empiric triclabendazole therapy (400 mg daily for two days). Her symptoms, eosinophilia, hematoma, and thrombi showed gradual resolution on follow-up imaging at six months.

CONCLUSION: Fascioliasis should be considered in patients from endemic areas who present with unexplained eosinophilia, hepatic abnormalities, and thrombotic events, even when parasitological tests are negative and serological confirmation is unavailable. A history of sheep farming or raw vegetable consumption provides important diagnostic clues. Prompt recognition and empiric antiparasitic treatment, along with supportive care, can lead to favorable outcomes.

While hepatobiliary symptoms are common, vascular complications such as portal vein thrombosis (PVT) and deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are rarely reported. We describe a case of suspected fascioliasis presenting with a large hepatic subcapsular hematoma, PVT, and extensive DVT in a patient from a rural endemic area with a history of sheep farming.

title: Cross-database thromboembolic reporting signals for ovarian cancer therapies: a focus on bevacizumab.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thromboembolic events (TEs) can disrupt ovarian cancer treatment and adversely affect outcomes. Post-marketing reporting patterns across systemic therapies and regulatory databases remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We analyzed the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS; 2004Q1-2025Q1), Canada Vigilance (2002-2025), and Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database (JADER; 2004-2025). Reports involved ovarian, fallopian tube, or primary peritoneal cancer and prespecified systemic therapies. MedDRA preferred term-validated definitions identified venous thromboembolism (VTE), arterial thromboembolism (ATE), and their union (any_TE). We assessed ROR, PRR, chi-square, information component, and IC025 within each database; cross-database replication was the primary criterion. Pooled and covariate-adjusted analyses were supportive. Bevacizumab subgroup, co-medication, time-to-onset (TTO), fatal-outcome, network, and drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses provided descriptive or exploratory context.

RESULTS: After excluding male-coded records, 55,271 reports met inclusion, including 1,296 TE cases. Seven of 39 drug-event combinations replicated in at least two databases. Bevacizumab alone replicated for any_TE, VTE, and ATE in all three systems. In FAERS, RORs were 2.28 (95% CI 1.96-2.65; IC025 0.81) for any_TE and 2.38 (1.94-2.93; IC025 0.81) for VTE. The ATE ROR was 2.34 (1.91-2.87; IC025 0.79). Paclitaxel replicated for any_TE and ATE, whereas doxorubicin replicated for any_TE and VTE. Rucaparib appeared in one database and was not assessable for replication. Only 1,757/45,025 (3.9%) FAERS reports had usable dates. Median recorded TTO was 90 days for bevacizumab and 13 days for carboplatin and paclitaxel; these selected intervals were interpreted descriptively. Genetically proxied VEGFA inhibition was associated with stroke (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.09-1.26; P = 1.33e-05), but not with VTE or pulmonary embolism.

CONCLUSIONS: Bevacizumab showed the most reproducible reporting signals across all three databases for composite, venous, and arterial thromboembolism. Together with greater MR concordance for arterial outcomes, this phenotype-resolved pattern motivates separate biological hypotheses for VTE and ATE. Clinically, it reinforces vigilance for both phenotypes during bevacizumab-containing ovarian cancer treatment and supports phenotype-specific prospective validation.

Post-marketing reporting patterns across systemic therapies and regulatory databases remain poorly characterized. title: Factors associated with patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The factors influencing patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting remain incompletely understood. We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025. Studies reporting associations between potential risk factors and stent outcomes were included. Data were synthesized narratively, and random-effects meta-analyses with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed when comparable multivariable-adjusted estimates were available.

RESULTS: A total of 49 studies were included, predominantly involving retrospective cohorts. The meta-analysis suggested that post-thrombotic disease, stent extension across or below the inguinal ligament, and hyperlipidemia were associated with an increased risk of patency loss, whereas increasing age showed a modest inverse association with patency loss. The narrative evidence suggested that greater anatomical disease extent was associated with poorer stent patency, whereas the evidence regarding impaired venous inflow was heterogeneous and varied according to the disease phenotype, anatomical segment, and inflow definition. Pooled analyses did not identify statistically significant associations of sex, stent length, or number of stents with patency loss. Evidence regarding anticoagulation discontinuation and adjunctive antiplatelet therapy was insufficient and inconsistent.

CONCLUSIONS: Patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting appears to be associated with the disease phenotype, higher anatomical disease burden, and stent landing strategy. Venous inflow impairment may also be associated with poorer stent patency, although the evidence was heterogeneous. The predominantly retrospective evidence precludes causal inference. Prospective studies with standardized definitions and robust adjustment are needed to improve risk stratification and optimize post-stenting management.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: The factors influencing patency loss after iliocaval and iliofemoral venous stenting remain incompletely understood. We therefore conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesize the available evidence. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Library were searched to December 2025.

title: Early acute kidney injury after pulmonary endarterectomy: incidence, associated perioperative factors, and early outcome in a single-centre retrospective cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) is the standard treatment for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, but factors associated with acute kidney injury (AKI) remain uncertain. We examined perioperative factors associated with AKI within 48 h and evaluated an exploratory early postoperative risk-identification model.

METHODS: We screened 126 consecutive adults with operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension who underwent PEA at a tertiary referral centre between January 2018 and December 2020. Eight met predefined exclusion criteria and one of 118 eligible patients had no assessable renal criterion. AKI was defined by the 2012 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine and urine-output criteria. Eleven patients whose status could not be determined, because one criterion was negative and the other unavailable, were excluded, leaving 106 for analysis. Multiple imputation assessed missing-covariate sensitivity, and the combined model underwent bootstrap validation, calibration and decision-curve analysis.

RESULTS: AKI occurred in 42 of 106 adults (39.6%): 35 stage 1, four stage 2 and three stage 3; alternative handling of the indeterminate cases gave incidences between 35.9% and 45.3%. When extracorporeal circulation (ECC), deep hypothermic circulatory arrest and aortic cross-clamp durations were analysed together, only ECC duration remained independently associated with AKI (adjusted odds ratio 1.032 per minute, 95% confidence interval 1.012-1.052; p = 0.001). Age was the only independently associated preoperative variable (1.034 per year, 1.004-1.065; p = 0.027). An integrated model combining age (1.035 per year, 1.007-1.063; p = 0.014) and ECC duration (1.025 per minute, 1.009-1.041; p = 0.003) gave apparent and optimism-corrected areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.718 and 0.706, with a calibration slope of 0.97. Albumin at intensive care unit admission was inversely associated with AKI in univariable analysis but was not independently associated in the integrated model (p = 0.129) and improved neither fit nor discrimination. Haemodynamic improvement was similar in both groups, but 30-day mortality was higher among patients with AKI (14.3% vs. 0%; p = 0.003).

CONCLUSIONS: Among adults undergoing PEA for operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, longer ECC duration and older age were associated with AKI within 48 h. Similar haemodynamic recovery did not exclude renal injury. The model is exploratory and requires external validation.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT07132619. Retrospectively registered 13 August 2025.

We examined perioperative factors associated with AKI within 48 h and evaluated an exploratory early postoperative risk-identification model. METHODS: We screened 126 consecutive adults with operable chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension who underwent PEA at a tertiary referral centre between January 2018 and December 2020.

title: Incidence of peripheral intravenous catheter: related phlebitis among hospitalized adults in Southwest Ethiopia-a prospective observational study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVCs) are among the most commonly used invasive devices in hospitalized patients. However, their use is frequently complicated by phlebitis, which contributes to patient discomfort, interruption of therapy, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to determine the incidence of PIVC-related phlebitis and identify associated factors among adult hospitalized patients at Jimma University Medical Center (JUMC), Southwest Ethiopia.

METHODS: A hospital-based prospective observational study was conducted among adult patients admitted to the emergency and medical wards of JUMC from 01 December 2025 to 07 March 2026. A total of 384 patients requiring PIVC were enrolled using a consecutive sampling technique, of which 372 completed inpatient follow-up. Data were collected through patient interviews, direct observation, and medical record review using a structured questionnaire. Phlebitis was assessed using Jackson's Visual Infusion Phlebitis (VIP) scoring system. Data were entered into EpiData version 4.6 and analyzed using SPSS version 25. Bivariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with phlebitis. Statistical significance was declared at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: The overall incidence of PIVC-related phlebitis was 55.9% (95% CI 50.8-60.9). Most cases were mild, with grade 1 and grade 2 phlebitis accounting for 47.2% and 36.2% of cases, respectively. Female sex (AOR = 4.6, 95% CI 2.68-8.06), longer catheter dwell time (per additional day) (AOR = 1.38, 95% CI 1.18-1.61, P = 0.01), administration of intravenous medications (AOR = 2.3, 95% CI 1.15-4.62), and catheter insertion in the emergency unit (AOR = 2.6, 95% CI 1.52-4.58) were independently associated with phlebitis.

CONCLUSIONS: The incidence of PIVC-related phlebitis at JUMC was markedly higher than internationally recommended threshold. Increasing catheter dwell time, intravenous medication administration, emergency unit catheter insertion, and female sex were independently associated with phlebitis. Strengthening infection prevention practices, routine catheter site monitoring, timely catheter replacement, and adherence to evidence-based catheter management protocols are essential to reduce the burden of phlebitis and improve patient safety.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable.

However, their use is frequently complicated by phlebitis, which contributes to patient discomfort, interruption of therapy, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs. This study aimed to determine the incidence of PIVC-related phlebitis and identify associated factors among adult hospitalized patients at Jimma University Medical Center (JUMC), Southwest Ethiopia.

title: Risk factors of amputation in patients undergoing angioplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Critical limb ischemia (CLI) represents the severe stage of peripheral arterial disease. Angioplasty can restore blood flow to failing limbs, yet some patients still face amputation. Limited researches have explored how risk factors predict post-procedure outcomes.

METHODS: A thorough search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, and the Cochrane Library for pertinent articles released by April 21 2025. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to calculate pooled odds ratios (ORs) along with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Key risk factors for amputation post-angioplasty comprise end-stage renal disease, diabetes mellitus, and hemodialysis. Subgroup analyses and leave-one-out sensitivity analyses were performed to investigate sources of heterogeneity and result reliability.

RESULTS: A total of 55 cohort studies involving 477,880 participants met the inclusion criteria. Meta-analysis showed that amputation was significantly associated with diabetes mellitus (OR 2.76, 95% CI 2.09-3.65, p < 0.001). Moreover, Findings revealed a significant association between amputation and end-stage renal disease (OR 1.76, 95% CI 1.39-2.23, p<0.001) as well as hemodialysis (OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.52-2.73, p<0.001). Conversely, amputation did not show a correlation with dyslipidemia (OR 0.74, 95% CI 0.52-1.07, p=0.105) or smoking (OR 1.90, 95% CI 0.99-3.65, p=0.053) in patients post-angioplasty. These findings were corroborated by trim and fill analysis and leave-one-out sensitivity tests.

CONCLUSIONS: The major risk factors for amputation were patient- and surgery-related. This information helps clinicians identify high-risk patients who need amputation following an angioplasty and early intervention.

title: Dynamic cerebral autoregulation and exercise-induced neurovascular coupling as potential markers of cerebral hyperperfusion after carotid stenting.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to prospectively evaluate whether impaired dynamic cerebral autoregulation (dCA) and exercise-induced neurovascular coupling (NVC) parameters in carotid stenosis predict cerebral hyperperfusion (CH) after carotid artery stenting (CAS).

METHODS: This study was conducted based on prospectively collected data from a single-center observational registry. Between October 2023 and September 2024, the registry enrolled 237 patients scheduled to undergo CAS, all with carotid artery stenosis (≥ 70% for asymptomatic or ≥ 50% for symptomatic stenosis). To assess NVC, transcranial Doppler (TCD) was performed within 24 h prior to CAS. NVC was evaluated by measuring the increase in cerebral blood velocity (CBv) in the middle cerebral artery (MCA) during stimulation. Ultimately, 93 patients proceeded to stenting and were included in the present analysis.

RESULTS: Among 93 patients undergoing CAS, 16.1% (n = 15) developed CH. These patients exhibited significantly lower phase values in very low frequency (VLF) compared to non-CH patients during exercise (23.12° vs. 41.82°, p < 0.05). NVC was compromised in CH patients, demonstrated by reduced exercise-induced flow response (EIFR) (5.6% vs. 8.6%, p = 0.041) and Δcerebrovascular conductance index (ΔCVCi) (p = 0.015). The hemodynamic and regulatory model integrating phase at VLF, ΔCVCi, and EIFR showed a higher AUC compared with the clinical model, though the difference did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.20).

CONCLUSION: This study suggests that dCA and NVC parameters during exercise stimulation may serve as potential predictors of CH after CAS, supporting further investigation of cerebrovascular autoregulation assessment in preoperative evaluation for carotid revascularization.

title: Is the effect of sex on post-thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke age-dependent? Results from an international prospective registry (EVA-TRISP).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate the effect of sex on clinical outcomes after endovascular treatment (EVT) in ischemic stroke patients and whether this effect is age dependent.

METHODS: We used data from EVA-TRISP, a multicentre registry of consecutive EVT patients. Primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, analysed with unadjusted and adjusted mixed model ordinal regression. We compared women with men and assessed the interaction between age and sex. We assessed age both as a continuous variable and dichotomized at the population median.

RESULTS: In total, 12,915 EVT patients were included for the current study (median age 74 [IQR 64-82] years, 6,251 [48.4%] women). Female patients were older (77 [IQR 67-84] vs 72 [IQR: 62-80], p < 0.001) and had a higher median baseline NIHSS (15 [IQR 9-19] vs 14 [IQR 8-19], p < 0.001). Female sex was associated with worse functional outcome in the unadjusted analysis (cOR 1.22, 95%CI:1.14-1.29) but not in the adjusted analysis (acOR 1.02, 95%CI:0.95-1.09). We found no significant interaction between age and sex when assessing age as a continuous variable (p = 0.08), but observed a significant interaction when dichotomizing age (p = 0.01). In patients aged 74 or younger, women had worse outcomes than men (acOR 1.10, 95%CI:1.003-1.20) while sex was not associated with functional outcome in older patients (acOR 0.93, 95%CI:0.85-1.02).

CONCLUSION: We did not find clear evidence that the effect of sex on post-EVT outcomes is modified by age when using age as continuous variable, but observed a worse outcome in women in patients aged 74 or younger.

METHODS: We used data from EVA-TRISP, a multicentre registry of consecutive EVT patients. Primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score, analysed with unadjusted and adjusted mixed model ordinal regression.

title: The Great Divergence: Quantifying Hospital-Physician Payment Inequity in Medicare 2019 to 2023.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medicare reimburses hospitals through diagnosis-related groups (DRGs) and physicians through Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes, systems that have diverged significantly over time. We quantified hospital-to-physician payment divergence across matched general surgery procedures from 2019 to 2023.

METHODS: DRG and CPT payment data were obtained from the Medicare Inpatient Prospective Payment System and Physician Fee Schedule 2019 to 2023. 16 CPT codes were matched to corresponding MS-DRGs at maximum and minimum complexity. This yielded 31 DRG/CPT ratio time series for 489,111 discharges. Trend analysis employed ordinary least squares regression, Mann-Kendall tests, and Sen slope with Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) false discovery rate correction.

RESULTS: 24/31 DRG/CPT ratio series (77.4%) demonstrated statistically significant increasing trends after BH-correction, with no series showing a significant decline. Mean DRG-Max to CPT ratios increased 23.1% while mean CPT payments declined 3.5% in real terms. The largest increases were observed for EVAR (+4.7 points/y, P=0.021), heart transplantation (+4.0 points/y, P=0.031), and liver transplantation (+1.8 points/y, P=0.006). Divergence was also significant for high-volume procedures, including cholecystectomy and small bowel resection.

CONCLUSIONS: Significant payment divergence exists between hospitals and physicians across general surgery. DRG weights recalibrate annually using hospital cost data, while physician conversion factors consistently lag inflation. This divergence may be further amplified in all patient refined-DRGs used by state Medicaid programs and commercial insurers, where severity adjustments generate higher hospital payments while physician CPT payments remain unchanged. Future policy alignment of DRG and CPT methodologies is critical to preserving equity and sustaining surgical care delivery.

We quantified hospital-to-physician payment divergence across matched general surgery procedures from 2019 to 2023. METHODS: DRG and CPT payment data were obtained from the Medicare Inpatient Prospective Payment System and Physician Fee Schedule 2019 to 2023.

title: Identification of thrombotic complications of the arm in blood donors: Evidence from literature and national data.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Research on donor complications has focused mainly on vasovagal reactions, with less attention to local complications. Early detection of upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis (UDVT) is essential to prevent serious outcomes such as pulmonary embolism. This study assesses the association between UDVT and blood donation to facilitate identification and improve donor care.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: A literature search was conducted using PubMed and Notify Library. Reports on therapeutic apheresis and clinical studies were excluded. Articles reporting aggregated data or individual cases of venous thrombosis, thrombophlebitis or phlebitis after donation of blood or components of blood were selected. Furthermore, donor records suggestive of arm thrombosis from December 2022 to January 2025 were extracted from our blood bank database. Donors were interviewed by telephone with a standardized questionnaire.

RESULTS: A literature search yielded 7 reports presenting 9 cases of UDVT, as well as a conference summary describing 20 cases. Arm pain and swelling were common symptoms, typically occurring within hours to days after donation. Risk factors for thrombosis were repeated sport-related arm movements, complicated phlebotomy, smoking, oral contraceptive use and genetic mutations. In our blood bank, 12 donors reported symptoms suggestive of venous thrombosis. Based on information collected in the interviews, there were three cases of UDVT, four cases of thrombophlebitis, two cases of phlebitis, one finger infection, one leg deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and one haematoma.

CONCLUSION: UDVT is a rare complication that can occur days after donation. Prompt evaluation and referral to a general practitioner will contribute to preventing harmful consequences.

Early detection of upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis (UDVT) is essential to prevent serious outcomes such as pulmonary embolism. This study assesses the association between UDVT and blood donation to facilitate identification and improve donor care.

title: Association between prior peritoneal dialysis and arteriovenous fistula maturation and patency in patients with end-stage renal disease: a comparative study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) undergoing peritoneal dialysis (PD) often require transition to hemodialysis (HD), yet the association between prior PD and arteriovenous fistula (AVF) outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare AVF maturation and patency between patients with and without prior PD.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, comparative study included patients with ESRD who underwent their first AVF creation between January 2018 and December 2022. AVF maturation, patency, and related parameters were compared between patients with and without prior PD.

RESULTS: A total of 571 patients were included for analysis and 82 patients (14.4%) had a history of PD. Patients who had PD had significantly lower rates of overall successful (87.8% vs. 94.1%, p = 0.037) and unassisted AVF maturation (65.9% vs. 82.4%, p = 0.001) compared with non-PD patients, as well as lower one-year primary (60.2% vs. 70.7%, p = 0.046) and cumulative patency rates (86.5% vs. 93.4%, p = 0.027). In multivariable analyses, prior PD was independently associated with a lower likelihood of unassisted AVF maturation (odds ratio [OR] = 0.442, 95% CI = 0.219-0.891, p = 0.022) and a higher risk of one-year cumulative patency failure (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.759, 95% CI 1.343-5.667, p = 0.006).

CONCLUSIONS: Prior PD may be associated with lower AVF maturation and patency rates. Early vascular access planning might be recommended for PD patients approaching technique failure. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.

This study aimed to compare AVF maturation and patency between patients with and without prior PD. METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, comparative study included patients with ESRD who underwent their first AVF creation between January 2018 and December 2022.

title: Risk factors, evaluation, and treatment advances for adverse distal aortic remodeling after type A aortic dissection repair: a systematic review.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adverse distal aortic remodeling after type A aortic dissection (TAAD) repair is the principal cause of late aneurysm formation, rupture, and reintervention, significantly compromising long-term survival in patients with TAAD.

METHODS: This study is a systematic review. A comprehensive search of Chinese and English databases up to December 10, 2025 was performed to systematically identify imaging-based risk factors for adverse distal aortic remodeling after TAAD repair and to summarize the efficacy and limitations of current endovascular intervention strategies.

RESULTS: After systematically searching CNKI, Wanfang Data, VIP, PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science, a total of 31 studies involving 5330 patients were included.

CONCLUSION: Imaging-based risk factors for adverse distal aortic remodeling include early postoperative descending aortic diameter ≥ 40 mm, a patent or partially thrombosed false lumen, and distal anastomotic new entry (DANE). Endovascular techniques, including false lumen occlusion, aortic true lumen stenting, and adjunctive intimal fenestration, can effectively improve patient outcomes. Early identification of high-risk patients and individualized intervention are key to enhancing the long-term prognosis of individuals with TAAD.

METHODS: This study is a systematic review. A comprehensive search of Chinese and English databases up to December 10, 2025 was performed to systematically identify imaging-based risk factors for adverse distal aortic remodeling after TAAD repair and to summarize the efficacy and limitations of current endovascular intervention strategies.

title: Chronic traumatic popliteal arteriovenous fistula presenting twenty years after shotgun injury: a case report and critical literature review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) account for only 2.5-4% of penetrating vascular injuries, yet their natural history is insidious: most remain hemodynamically compensated for years before clinical decompensation. Delayed popliteal AVF poses unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because of the anatomically confined surgical field, proximity of neurovascular structures, and historical amputation rates of 10-20%. This report is prepared in accordance with the CARE criteria for case reports.

CASE PRESENTATION: A 64-year-old male smoker presented with a 10-day history of progressive left popliteal pain and a pulsatile mass, precisely 20 years after conservative management of a shotgun injury to the same limb. Physical examination revealed a continuous machinery-type bruit and thrill. CT angiography confirmed a direct popliteal arteriovenous communication, a 25 mm secondary venous aneurysm, proximal arterial dilation to 16 mm, and-critically-incidental cardiomegaly with ascending aortic dilation (44 mm), may reflect chronic systemic high-output circulatory adaptation secondary to AV shunting. Open surgical repair with fistula ligation and aneurysmorrhaphy was performed.

DISCUSSION: This case exemplifies the full natural history of a chronic traumatic AVF: prolonged asymptomatic compensation, progressive vascular remodeling, venous aneurysm formation, and systemic cardiac adaptation. We present an analysis of pathophysiology, diagnostic modalities, and evidence-based treatment selection alongside a proposed five-step management algorithm.

CONCLUSION: Traumatic popliteal AVF can remain silent for decades. The coexistence of venous aneurysm, chronic cardiac remodeling, and 20-year-old scar tissue argues for individualized management guided by echocardiographic hemodynamics and anatomic complexity.

Delayed popliteal AVF poses unique diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because of the anatomically confined surgical field, proximity of neurovascular structures, and historical amputation rates of 10-20%. This report is prepared in accordance with the CARE criteria for case reports.

title: Spleen stiffness measured by sound touch elastography predicts survival after TIPS in patients with cirrhosis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) is an effective procedure for managing portal hypertension-related complications. Liver and spleen stiffness may noninvasively predict post-TIPS survival. The aim of this study was to establish a predictive model that integrates elastography parameters and other noninvasive markers to predict survival in patients after TIPS.

METHODS: This was a single-center prospective study. A total of 89 patients who underwent the TIPS procedure in our department between July 2021 and December 2023 were enrolled. Liver and spleen stiffness were assessed using sound touch elastography before the TIPS procedure. The primary outcome of the present study was patient mortality, and the secondary outcome was further decompensation after the TIPS procedure. Kaplan-Meier curves were used to analyze mortality risk across groups.

RESULTS: A total of 39 patients (43.8%) developed further decompensation. Spleen stiffness and liver stiffness, were significantly higher in the further decompensation group than in the non-decompensation group (34.16 vs. 26.12 kPa and 16.59 vs. 14.7 kPa, respectively). However, there was no statistically significant difference in liver stiffness. The cutoff value of S-STE for predicting further decompensation was 35.27 Kpa. The cutoff value for S-STE for predicting mortality was 36.435 kPa. Using a Child-Pugh score threshold of 9.5 and an S-STE value of 36.435 kPa, patients were classified into good, moderate, and poor prognosis groups. The mortality rates were 2.0%, 77.8%, and 29.0%, respectively. Kaplan-Meier curves revealed a significant difference in mortality among the three groups (log-rank: p < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: S-STE is a noninvasive imaging modality. An S-STE value of 36.435 kPa combined with a Child-Pugh score of 9.5 provides a risk-stratification predictive model for patients after TIPS. This approach may assist in the clinical management of these patients.

title: Global burden and trends of lower extremity peripheral arterial disease, 1990-2021: findings from GBD 2021.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lower extremity peripheral arterial disease (LEPAD) is a major atherosclerotic condition in ageing populations, contributing to mobility loss, disability, and excess cardiovascular risk. Using modelled estimates from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, we assessed global, regional, and national LEPAD burden from 1990 to 2021 and projected age-standardised trends to 2040.

METHODS: Modelled estimates of LEPAD prevalence, incidence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were extracted from the GBD 2021 study for 204 countries and territories and stratified by age, sex, and socio-demographic index (SDI). Unless otherwise stated, all rates are age-standardised using the GBD world standard population and are reported per 100,000 population with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). Temporal trends were summarised using estimated annual percentage change (EAPC), risk-attributable burdens were assessed using GBD comparative risk assessment outputs, and autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models were used for trend-based projections.

RESULTS: In 2021, 113.7 million (95% UI 98.5-131.2) people were living with LEPAD worldwide, with 10.0 million (8.7-11.6) incident cases, 67,700 (59,900-74,300) deaths, and 1.56 million (1.27-2.05) DALYs. The ASPR, ASIR, ASDR, and age-standardised DALY rate were 1,326.5 (1,153.8-1,526.5), 115.4 (100.0-132.7), 0.8 (0.7-0.9), and 18.6 (15.2-24.2) per 100,000 population, respectively. From 1990 to 2021, age-standardised death and DALY rates declined overall, whereas absolute case numbers increased. High-SDI regions had the highest age-standardised prevalence and incidence rates, while low- and low-middle-SDI regions showed less favourable temporal trends. High fasting plasma glucose and kidney dysfunction were the largest modelled contributors to LEPAD-related deaths and DALYs. ARIMA projections suggested a possible increase in ASPR through 2040, although these forecasts should be interpreted as descriptive trend extrapolations.

CONCLUSIONS: LEPAD remains a substantial and unevenly distributed global health burden. In the context of population ageing and multimorbidity, prevention strategies should prioritise early detection among older adults and integrated control of cardiometabolic and renal risk factors, particularly in lower-resource settings.

Using modelled estimates from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study, we assessed global, regional, and national LEPAD burden from 1990 to 2021 and projected age-standardised trends to 2040. METHODS: Modelled estimates of LEPAD prevalence, incidence, deaths, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) were extracted from the GBD 2021 study for 204 countries and territories and stratified by age, sex, and socio-demographic index (SDI).

title: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and its impact on inpatient outcomes in inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospitalizations with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), and current guidelines recommend routine pharmacological thromboprophylaxis during admission. However, there is limited evidence regarding the occurrence of Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) in this population. We examined the incidence and risk of HIT among hospitalizations with IBD.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study using the National Inpatient Sample dataset spanning ten years. We identified the predictive factors of HIT and assessed its impact on inpatient outcomes of IBD hospitalizations. We included hospitalizations aged ≥18 years with any discharge diagnosis (primary or secondary) of IBD, identified using ICD-CM codes.

RESULTS: Among 3,093,632 hospitalizations with IBD, 2,218 (0.07%) were diagnosed with HIT. IBD hospitalizations had 40% higher odds of developing HIT (AOR: 1.42; 95% CI: 1.28-1.56). Compared with those without HIT, IBD hospitalizations with HIT had higher odds of mortality (AOR: 3.23; 95% CI: 2.21-4.74), longer mean length of stay (β: 7.3, 95% CI: 6.07-8.49), and higher mean total hospital charges (β: $97,211, 95% CI: $83,540-$129,417). Additionally, they had increased odds of both venous and arterial thromboembolic events, as well as significant bleeding events.

CONCLUSIONS: Hospitalizations with IBD had increased risk of HIT, which is subsequently associated with worse in-hospital outcomes. While recognizing the benefits of VTE prophylaxis in this population, further investigation is necessary to better understand the observed risk of HIT. Utilizing innovative methods, such as clinical decision support tools combined with established HIT prevention and management practices, may help improve patient outcomes.

However, there is limited evidence regarding the occurrence of Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) in this population. We examined the incidence and risk of HIT among hospitalizations with IBD.

title: Association between high triglyceride-glucose index status and one-year all-cause mortality in patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm: a MIMIC-IV cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is widely used as a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been associated with a range of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, its role in the longer-term prognosis of patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), particularly one-year mortality, remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TyG index and one-year mortality in patients with TAA and to assess its potential prognostic value.

METHODS: This study used data from the MIMIC-IV database and included 554 patients with TAA. Patients were classified into low- and high-TyG groups according to the median TyG index. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess the association between the TyG index and one-year mortality, and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to examine potential nonlinear relationships. Kaplan-Meier survival curves and Cox proportional hazards models were used for time-to-event analyses. The predictive performance, clinical net benefit, and calibration of models incorporating the TyG index were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, decision curve analysis, and calibration curves. In addition, sensitivity and subgroup analyses were conducted to examine the robustness of the findings.

RESULTS: In the overall TAA cohort, after full adjustment, the high-TyG group was significantly associated with an increased risk of one-year mortality (OR = 1.829, 95% CI: 1.083-3.091, P = 0.024). Similar findings were observed among ICU patients (OR = 3.273, 95% CI: 1.128-9.498, P = 0.029). RCS analysis suggested a potential nonlinear relationship between the TyG index and one-year mortality. Kaplan-Meier curves showed a lower one-year survival rate in the high-TyG group than in the low-TyG group, although the log-rank test did not reach statistical significance. In Cox proportional hazards models, high TyG status was associated with an increased risk of one-year mortality in both the overall cohort (HR = 1.651, 95% CI: 1.041-2.618, P = 0.033) and ICU patients (HR = 2.922, 95% CI: 1.154-7.397, P = 0.024). ROC analysis showed that adding high TyG status increased the model AUC from 0.686 to 0.702 in the overall cohort and from 0.809 to 0.844 in ICU patients; however, these incremental improvements were not statistically significant. Decision curve analysis and calibration curves indicated that the model incorporating high TyG status provided a slightly greater net benefit and a marginally lower Brier score. Sensitivity analyses showed that the association between high TyG status and increased one-year mortality remained directionally consistent when the TyG index was categorized into tertiles, after excluding patients with ruptured TAA, and after excluding patients who died during hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: In patients with TAA, high TyG status was independently associated with an increased risk of one-year all-cause mortality. This association was consistent across sensitivity analyses and time-to-event analyses. Incorporating high TyG status into clinical models provided modest incremental prognostic information, but the improvement in predictive performance was limited, suggesting that it should not be used as a standalone clinical prediction tool. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings and clarify its clinical utility.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is widely used as a surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been associated with a range of adverse cardiovascular outcomes. However, its role in the longer-term prognosis of patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), particularly one-year mortality, remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between the TyG index and one-year mortality in patients with TAA and to assess its potential prognostic value.

title: Patient-specific 3D-printed porous titanium implants for complex foot and ankle reconstruction: Clinical and radiographic outcomes - A current concepts review of the literature.
abstract: Critical-sized bone defects of the foot and ankle have traditionally been managed with bulk structural allograft or major amputation, both carrying substantial limitations, prompting exploration of patient-specific 3D-printed porous titanium implants as a structural alternative, though supporting evidence remains fragmented. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement and a pre-registered PROSPERO protocol, this current concepts review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, identifying 22 clinical studies (4 Level III, 17 Level IV, 1 Level V; published 2015-2026) comprising 289 adult patients undergoing complex foot and ankle reconstruction with these implants; two independent reviewers performed screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment, with primary outcomes-osseous union, limb salvage, and major amputation-synthesized descriptively as pooled proportions, counting overlapping cohorts once. The pooled limb-salvage rate was 92% (196/214 limbs) and major amputation rate 8% (21/276 patients); among 13 studies reporting a patient-level union endpoint, pooled union was 89% (64/72 patients), with consistent functional improvement and a weighted mean follow-up of 25 months. However, the pooled reoperation rate reached 26% (74/289 patients), driven predominantly by deep infection, with prior ipsilateral infection (odds ratio 14.9) and neuropathy (odds ratio 5.76) as independent predictors; the single comparative study found significantly higher articular fusion and no implant subsidence versus femoral head allograft (p = 0.018 and p = 0.016, respectively). These implants achieve high limb-salvage and union rates with a low major amputation rate, offset by a substantial reoperation burden. Prospective comparative studies with standardized union definitions and longer follow-up are needed.
englishSummary: Critical-sized bone defects of the foot and ankle have traditionally been managed with bulk structural allograft or major amputation, both carrying substantial limitations, prompting exploration of patient-specific 3D-printed porous titanium implants as a structural alternative, though supporting evidence remains fragmented. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement and a pre-registered PROSPERO protocol, this current concepts review searched PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library, identifying 22 clinical studies (4 Level III, 17 Level IV, 1 Level V; published 2015-2026) comprising 289 adult patients undergoing complex foot and ankle reconstruction with these implants; two independent reviewers performed screening, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment, with primary outcomes-osseous union, limb salvage, and major amputation-synthesized descriptively as pooled proportions, counting overlapping cohorts once. The pooled limb-salvage rate was 92% (196/214 limbs) and major amputation rate 8% (21/276 patients); among 13 studies reporting a patient-level union endpoint, pooled union was 89% (64/72 patients), with consistent functional improvement and a weighted mean follow-up of 25 months.

title: Sex- and Age-specific Outcomes After Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (RAAA) remains a medical catastrophe. Although early outcomes improved, contemporary data integrating early and long-term survival, and postdischarge care needs across sex- and age groups is limited.

METHODS: This nationwide cohort included Dutch RAAA repairs between 2014 and 2023. Dutch Surgical Aneurysm Audit data were linked to Statistics Netherlands registries. Outcomes included 90-day mortality, long-term survival, and postdischarge care.

RESULTS: Of the 3642 patients, 15.2% were women, who were older (76.3 vs. 74.0 y) and more often required open repair (61.4% vs. 54.0%). Ninety-day mortality increased with age and was higher in women (39.1% vs. 29.1%), but female sex was not independently associated with early mortality after adjustment.Among 90-day survivors, absolute long-term survival was similar, but relative survival was lower in women (5-year relative survival 68.0% vs. 78.3%). Women were less often discharged home (42.4% vs. 56.7%) and more frequently required early homecare (47.7% vs. 34.7%). Reinterventions were more common after EVAR than open repair and occurred less frequently in women.

CONCLUSION: In this nationwide linked audit-registry analysis, outcomes after RAAA repair improved substantially, despite lower estimated in-hospital turndown rates than in earlier eras. The higher early mortality in women WAS reflected by differences in age, presentation severity, and repair type - possibly reflecting less favorable aneurysm anatomy. Female sex also associated with an increased long-term excess mortality and greater postdischarge dependency. These findings indicate that optimization of care for women with a RAAA is not confined to perioperative mortality, but extends across the entire care pathway.

Although early outcomes improved, contemporary data integrating early and long-term survival, and postdischarge care needs across sex- and age groups is limited. title: PRe-emptive abdominal aortic aneurysm sac Embolization during endoVascular Aortic Repair (PREVAR) for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm-study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a potentially lethal condition if left untreated. AAA growth is a predictor of rupture as well as decreased survival. Minimally invasive infrarenal endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is the primary option for AAA treatment. One of the most common complications after EVAR is the presence of type 2 endoleaks (T2ELs), i.e., continued retrograde perfusion of the aneurysm sac by aortic side branches, typically the lumbar arteries. In many cases, a T2EL prevents optimal aneurysm exclusion and is associated with continued aneurysm growth. Thus, a low but persistent risk of rupture and a high rate of reinterventions remain an issue/concern in the presence of T2ELs. In addition, failure of aneurysm sac shrinkage even without concomitant endoleak is associated with decreased long-term survival. Pre-emptive as well as postoperative selective side branch occlusion to prevent or treat T2ELs is time-consuming and technically demanding with a low technical and clinical success rate. Therefore, perioperative, nonselective embolization of the aneurysm sac during EVAR has been proposed to prevent T2EL and promote sac shrinkage (PREVAR-Clinical Trial NCT05575570).

METHODS: Patients scheduled for EVAR at the Department of Vascular Surgery, Rigshospitalet Copenhagen University Hospital, The Heart Center, Denmark, are offered inclusion in this study. Patients are randomized to infrarenal EVAR (control) or infrarenal EVAR plus sac embolization with Shape Memory plugs (SMP) (intervention). The plugs are based on a resorbable scaffolding and a small radiopaque marker causing minimal imaging artifacts on computed tomography angiography (CTA). The number of plugs is individually calculated based on aneurysm sac flow volume. Postoperative follow-up (FU) is performed after 3 months, 1 year, and 5 years with both contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) and 3-phase CTA (without contrast, arterial phase, and venous phase). AAA sac volume change is the primary endpoint. Incidence of T2EL, reintervention rate, and long-term survival are the secondary endpoints. The study is terminated after the final patient has completed the 5-year FU.

DISCUSSION: EVAR has revolutionized AAA treatment since its introduction. In the short term, outcomes are superior to open aortic repair in anatomically suitable candidates. However, the high incidence of T2ELs and failure of AAA sac shrinkages associated with reinterventions and decreased survival in many patients. Preliminary data on intraoperative AAA sac embolization during EVAR seems to promote sac shrinkage. SMP plugs are tested and CE marked (Conformité Européenne) for embolization treatment but the effect of aneurysm sac embolization during EVAR is poorly known. This randomized study investigates the effect of aneurysm sac embolization with SMP plug material in a single-center setting.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Clinical Trial, PREVAR-Clinical Trial NCT05575570, registered October 12, 2022, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05575570 .

title: Fibrinogen Early In Severe Trauma studY II (FEISTY II): study protocol for a randomised clinical trial of fibrinogen concentrate vs cryoprecipitate in traumatic haemorrhage in Australia and New Zealand.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Haemorrhage is a leading cause of preventable death amongst severe trauma patients and is often complicated by hypofibrinogenaemia. Fibrinogen replacement can be achieved using fibrinogen concentrate (FC) or Cryoprecipitate (Cryo), but comparative evidence in traumatic haemorrhage is limited.

PRIMARY OBJECTIVE: To determine, in trauma patients with major haemorrhage and hypofibrinogenaemia, whether fibrinogen replacement using FC compared to Cryo increases the number of days alive and out of hospital (at home) within the first 90 days after randomisation (DAOH90).

METHODS: The Fibrinogen Early In Severe Trauma studY II (FEISTY II) is a phase III, multi-centre, randomised, two-arm parallel, open-label, superiority trial comparing FC and Cryo for fibrinogen replacement in severely injured trauma patients with major haemorrhage and hypofibrinogenaemia. Inclusion criteria are adults (≥ 18 years) affected by trauma and judged to have significant active haemorrhage with FIBTEM A5 ≤ 10 mm, TEG FF A10 ≤ 15 mm or FibC ≤ 2 g/L, for whom the local Major Haemorrhage Protocol (MHP) has been activated and/or emergency blood products have been transfused. Exclusion criteria are injuries judged incompatible with survival, inability to randomise within 6 h of trauma centre admission, pregnancy, objection to blood products, genetic or acquired coagulation disorder, dedicated fibrinogen replacement prior to randomisation, participation in competing study, and pre-existing co-morbidity that may interfere with the assessment of outcome. Patients will be block randomised 1:1 and stratified by site and clinical suspicion of Traumatic Brain Injury. The primary outcome is DAOH90. Secondary outcomes include all-cause mortality, transfusion requirements and measures of functional recovery and quality of life. Safety data will include symptomatic deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), myocardial infarction (MI), ischaemic stroke and transfusion reactions. A total of 900 patients will be recruited by trauma centre clinical staff across 23 trauma centres in Australia and New Zealand.

DISCUSSION: The optimal approach to fibrinogen replacement in traumatic haemorrhage remains uncertain. FEISTY II is a multi-centre randomised clinical trial in severely injured bleeding trauma patients, comparing FC to Cryo in terms of efficacy, safety, and cost-effectiveness.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov. NCT05449834 . Registered on 08 July 2022. 1st Participant enrolled 21 November 2022.
